Deadly Sentencing — Innate Technique (6th level)

Starting at 6th level, your mastery over Judge’s Gavel has improved. You can now re-summon your gavel as a free action. You can also spend 2 CE to increase the size of the gavel for 1 minute. The damage dice increase by one tier (d8<d10<d12<2d8). As an action, you can swing the enlarged gavel down on a 10 feet diameter square within 5 feet of you, forcing creatures within range to make a Dexterity saving throw or take twice your gavel’s damage.

Deadly Sentencing — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, when rolling for evidence you can roll two dice and pick the one you find more beneficial. This becomes 3 at 18th level.

Deadly Sentencing — Innate Technique (18th level)

Finally, at 18th level, you have reached the peak of your technique, showing off to others that only with skill you can truly win. You can now use Deadly Sentencing a number of times equal to your CE modifier without spending Cursed Energy each long rest.

Disaster Flames — Innate Technique (1st level)

You are born with a great power, with nigh-endless possibilities, fire manipulation, allowing you to burn down everything in your way.

Starting at 1st level, you have learned the basics of fire manipulation, being able to launch a wave of flames from your hands as well as the ability to cast Control Flames. As a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy, you unleash a 15 ft cone which forces people to make a Dexterity save. On a failure, they take 2d8 fire damage or half as much damage on a success. The fire ignites any flammable objects in the area that aren’t being worn or carried. Your damage dice increases to 3d8 at 5th level, 4d8 at 11th level, and 5d8 at 17th level.

Disaster Flames — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Beginning 3rd level, with a better understanding of the flames you possess, you can now create volcanoes. As an action for 2 Cursed Energy per volcano, you can create a number of volcanoes up to your Cursed Energy modifier within 60 ft of you, with each volcano occupying a 5 ft circle. As a bonus action, you can force every creature in a 30 ft long and 5 ft wide line originating from each volcano to make a Dexterity saving throw as the volcanoes erupt and disappear. On a failure, they take Xd10 fire damage equal to proficiency and become restrained by the magma for 1 minute. On success, they take half as much damage and are not restrained. The creature can make a Strength saving throw at the beginning of their turns, ending the condition early on success. Any area targeted by this feature becomes difficult terrain.

Disaster Flames — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned how to create small insect shikigami from your body. As an action for 4 Cursed Energy, you can create a swarm of Ember Insects Swarm within 5 ft. These shikigami act immediately after your turn.

Disaster Flames — Innate Technique (11th level)

When you reach 11th level, you have learned to extract the maximum from Disaster Flames, creating your Maximum. As an action for 10 Cursed Energy, you can fly up 120 ft in the air until the end of your next turn and create a single gigantic meteor. In the following turn you float down 120 ft harmlessly. Every other creature in a 120 ft radius centered on you must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 10d4 bludgeoning damage + 10d6 fire damage and are knocked prone. On a success, they take half as much damage.

Disaster Storms — Innate Technique (1st level)

You are born with an amazing power, with many possibilities, storm creation to ride the breeze.

Starting at 1st level, you have learned the basics of storm generation and can launch a wave of cutting winds from your hands as well as the ability to cast Gust. As a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy, you unleash a 15-foot cone which forces targets in range to make a Dexterity save. On a failure, they take 2d8 slashing or thunder (your choice) damage or half as much damage on a success. Your damage dice increases to 3d8 at 5th level, 4d8 at 11th level, and 5d8 at 17th level.

Disaster Storms — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, as an action for 2 cursed energy you can make a ranged cursed energy attack roll against a creature you can see within 60 ft. On a hit, you deal 3d6 lightning damage.

If another creature is within 10 ft of the target, you can make another attack against them, dealing half as much damage on a hit. This damage increases to 4d6 at 6th level, 6d6 at 11th level, and 8d6 at 18th level.

Disaster Storms — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you can spend 3 cursed energy as an action to create a localized storm centered on you in a 10 ft radius for 1 minute. You can spend additional cursed energy up to your proficiency bonus to increase the radius by 5 ft per cursed energy.
This area is difficult terrain and creatures that start their turn within range must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, they are knocked prone. Ranged attacks targeting a creature within this storm are made at disadvantage. When you deal lightning or thunder damage to a creature within this storm, you add your Cursed Energy modifier to the damage roll.

Disaster Storms — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to greatly amplify your storms. As an action for 10 cursed energy, you fill a 100 ft diameter sphere within 300 ft that you can see with a thick storm for 1 minute. The sphere is considered difficult terrain and heavily obscured to all creatures other than you. In addition to the effects of Storm Creation, all creatures other than you that start their turn within range take 3d10 lightning damage. When you take the Attack action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to replace one of your attacks with a use of Lightning, targeting a creature within the storm sphere with a ranged cursed energy attack even if you can’t see them.

Starting at 11th level, with your studies you have learned how to condense the water that you create and use it as a ball of mass destruction. As an action for 6 Cursed Energy, you can choose one target within 30 feet of you. Make a cursed energy attack roll against it. On a hit, it will take 10d8 cold damage and be pushed 80 feet away from you.
You can instead as an action for 8 Cursed Energy choose a point within 30 feet of you. All creatures within a 10-foot radius circle of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure they take 8d12 cold damage or half as much damage on a success. If the area is enclosed it is filled with 10 feet of water.

Disaster Tides — Innate Technique (18th level)

At 18th level, you have reached the pinnacle of manipulating your tides, creating a massive wave that destroys everything in its path. As an action for 8 Cursed Energy, you can cast the Tsunami spell as an 8th-level spell.

Disaster Verdure — Innate Technique (1st level)

You are born with an amazing power, with many possibilities, plant manipulation, allowing you to protect those you care about.

Beginning at 1st level, Starting at 1st level, you have begun to understand the power of nature. You gain the ability to manipulate nature at will. You can cast Druidcraft at will and gain the following cursed techniques:

  • Binding Plants. As an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can choose one target within 30 feet of you trapped by plants. The target must make a Strength saving throw, on a failure it will be restrained. It can make a Strength check to break free from the plants, on a success they are free from the binds, on a failure they remain stuck.

  • Piercing Roots. As an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can raise a bunch of roots from the ground to strike a target. You force all creatures in a 50ft line to make a Dexterity saving throw, on a failure they take 1d12 piercing damage, on a success they take half as much damage. This damage increases to 2d12 at 5th level, 3d12 at 11th level, and to 4d12 at 18th level.

  • Wall of Roots. As a reaction for 1 Cursed Energy, you rise deep roots from the ground to defend yourself or allies from attacks. As a reaction to you or an ally being targeted by an attack, you spring forth a wall of roots 10 ft tall and 5ft wide. The wall has an amount of hit points equal to your Cursed Energy modifier times your proficiency bonus.

Disaster Verdure — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have learned how to create small wooden balls to launch and pierce your opponents. As an action, you can create a number of two wooden balls, at the price of two cursed energy. The wooden balls will have a number of hit points equal to your Cursed Energy modifier, an AC of 10 + your CE modifier, and will keep floating around you. As a bonus action, you can send one or more of your balls towards a target within 30 feet of you. Make a cursed energy attack roll, on a hit the balls create large branches that pierce through its target, dealing 2d10 piercing damage. Right after they hit or miss the balls will disappear. You can also spend your bonus action to stand on one of the balls, gaining flying speed equal to half your walking speed while standing on them.

Disaster Verdure — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you can create a circle of flower petals that surrounds your opponents and removes their will to fight. As an action for 5 Cursed Energy, you create a 30 ft diameter circle in a point within 100 feet of yourself, all creatures within that circle must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure they are charmed for 1 minute as their will to fight is completely drained and their mind enters a state of tranquility and happiness. While charmed in this way, they are unable to take any kind of actions that would help in the battle. A creature can repeat the save at the beginning of its turn or when they take damage. Any attacks against a charmed creature is made at advantage, and any saving throws other than saves against this feature the creature makes are at disadvantage.

Disaster Verdure — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have studied the true nature of your innate technique, creating a new type of plant that feeds on cursed energy. As an action for 6 Cursed Energy, you can create and launch a number of cursed buds equal to your CE modifier toward one or more targets within 30 feet. Make a cursed energy attack roll for each, on a hit they will attach to the creature. At the beginning of the creature's turns it loses an amount of Hit Points equal to your CE modifier and you steal 1 CE from the target. If an affected creature uses cursed energy while infected with a cursed bud, they lose hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. An affected creature can attempt a Strength check as an action against your CE save DC to remove the curse bud.
You can instead spend 10 Cursed Energy to create a Large tree within 10 feet that will launch one cursed bud at every hostile creature within 30 feet. The tree has an AC equal to your Cursed Energy save DC, hit points equal to your proficiency bonus times your level and lasts for 1 minute, launching one cursed bud at creatures within range at the beginning of your turn.

Disaster Vermin — Innate Technique (1st level)

You are born with a disgusting power, with many disgusting possibilities.

Beginning at 1st level, as an action for 2 cursed energy you create an Insect Swarm in a space you can see within 5 ft of you. You can command the swarm as a bonus action, otherwise it takes the dodge action. Your Insect Swarm is made up of actual insects created from your cursed energy, not shikigami and you can only have one Insect Swarm summoned at a time.

Disaster Vermin — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your mastery over insects has grown. You can have a number of Insect Swarms summoned equal to your proficiency bonus and can command any number of them as a bonus action.

Additionally, you gain access to an insect shikigami with a large pouch. As an action, you can summon up to 2 shikigami, spending 2 cursed energy per shikigami to summon them in an unoccupied space within 10 ft of you. You can command the Shikigami and Insect Swarm as part of the same bonus action.

Disaster Vermin — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned the power of the almighty swarm. As part of the bonus action to command your Insect Swarms, you can order different swarms to move closer and combine into one Vermin Swarm if within 5 ft of each other, becoming 1 size larger for every additional swarm. The Vermin Swarm gains the combined hit points and damage dice of all the swarms together. The individual Insect Swarms that make up the Vermin Swarms still count against your maximum number of controlled swarms.

Disaster Vermin — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned that your instinctual hunger is not without reason, but exists to stimulate the desire to multiply. As an action for 8 cursed energy, you create an insect egg affixed to a wall/ceiling. The cost to create the egg decreases by 1 CE per creature devoured by you or a swarm in the last 8 hours (min cost 1).

The egg has an AC equal to your Cursed Energy save DC and hit points equal to twice your level. If you die within an hour of creating the egg, it births an identical copy of you from it with current hit points equal to half your hit point maximum. Your cursed energy is passed on after your death, giving your new body your remaining cursed energy from when you died. You do not regain any gear you had beforehand.

Finally at 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, up to 3 creatures of your choice within your domain take 6d10 necrotic damage as eggs fester and burst from their skin.
A creature that dies within your domain is devoured and becomes an Insect Swarm. This Insect Swarm does not count against your maximum number of controlled swarms until the domain ends.

Dragon Vein — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique forms an unbreakable connection between you and the earth while your feet touch the ground.

At 1st level you have formed a powerful connection between you and the earth that keeps you grounded. While your feet are touching the ground, you add your proficiency bonus to melee damage rolls and have advantage on ability checks and saving throws against being forcefully moved.

Dragon Vein — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, as a bonus action for 3 CE while your feet are touching the ground, you form a Ley Line connection for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits:

  • You are immune to magical effects that would forcefully move or teleport you.

  • You reduce all damage taken by your proficiency bonus.

  • As a reaction to taking damage, you can spend 1 CE reinforce your body with cursed energy and gain resistance to the triggering damage type until the beginning of your next turn.

You lose these benefits while your feet are not touching the ground. At 11th level, you are immune to being grappled, restrained, or knocked prone while your Ley Line is active.

Dragon Vein — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to greater siphon the earth’s might. Once per turn when you hit with a melee attack while your Ley Line is active, you deal an additional 1d8 damage. This increases to 2d8 at 11th level and 3d8 at 18th level. If you have not moved since the start of your last turn, you can do this extra damage twice per turn and your speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn. Additionally, when you gain resistance to a damage type with your Ley Line as a reaction, you can instead spend 3 CE to make the resistance last until the Ley Line ends.

Dragon Vein — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus + your Cursed Energy modifier at the beginning of your turn while your feet are touching the ground. When you start your turn at half your hit point maximum or less while your Ley Line is active, you can spend 3 CE to gain resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn.

Dragon Vein — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. Creatures within your domain cannot teleport or fly more than 10 ft off the ground, otherwise they find themselves getting crushed into the ground and take 5d10 force damage. A creature can take this damage once per turn. Additionally, you are always considered under Ley Line.

Divergent Fist — Innate Technique (1st level)

A learnt technique using cursed energy manipulation created accidentally due to slow cursed energy, turns out to be effective.

At 1st level, once per turn, you can choose the damage of one of your unarmed strikes or weapon attacks. For 1 cursed energy, you cause the creature to take the attack’s damage in necrotic damage at the beginning of their turn. These strikes can’t be black flashes. If used with Cursed Strike, the additional necrotic damage doesn’t happen until the start of the creature’s turn.

Divergent Fist — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your lack of an innate technique has caused you to make up for it with pure martial prowess. Once per round, you can use one of the following abilities:

  • Manji Kick: As part of an unarmed strike, drop your knees and rotate your body down to give a massive kick in your opponent's face. On a hit, the opponent must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failure, the creature will be stunned until the beginning of their next turn and take twice as much bludgeoning damage from the attack.

  • One-Two: As a bonus action, you land a One-Two combo. Make two unarmed attacks. The first damage roll doesn’t add your ability modifier, but on a hit the second gains advantage. The second attack adds three times your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll if both attacks hit.

  • Weave: You enter a defensive stance. You take the dodge action as a reaction instead.

activation.condition: As part of a successful unarmed strike; on failed CON save stun until start of target's next turn. Double strike damage is manual.

effects.name: Stunned (Manji Kick)
effects.description: Stunned until the beginning of the target's next turn; double unarmed-strike damage must be applied manually.

description.value:
Divergent Fist — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, you have gained better manipulation over your divergent fist attack. You can now use Divergent Flow on two separate attacks on your turn. When a creature is damaged by your Divergent Flow, they must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure they become disoriented. Their next attack is made at disadvantage or creatures have advantage on the next saving throw forced by that creature.

Divergent Fist — Innate Technique (11th level)

Starting at 11th level, as an action, crouch, placing your fist over your palm. While in this stance, your movement is 0 and you can only make one attack on your following turn. This attack allows you to roll for a black flash, even if the attack is not a critical hit. You make all rolls for a black flash at advantage.

Divergent Fist — Innate Technique (18th level)

Finally, at 18th level, you no longer need to roll for a black flash after a critical hit or using Stance of Sparks, you always hit a black flash.

Earth Manipulation — Innate Technique (1st level)

A simple yet powerful technique to mold rock as you please.

Starting at 1st level, your technique allows you to mold stone using your cursed energy. As an action for 1 cursed energy, you can shape the stone around yourself to make a 5-foot cubes of stone within 30 feet. You can choose to create multiple stone cubes up to your CE modifier (the cubes must be connected) as part of the same action, spending 1 CE for each cube. Each cube has an AC equal to your cursed energy DC and hit points equal to 5 times your CE modifier.

You can move a creature using these cubes. When creating the cubes in a creature’s area, you can attempt to move the target to a space within 5 feet. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw, being pushed on a failure. If you create multiple stone cubes as part of the same action, a creature that fails the save is pushed to the end of the connected cubes.

Earth Manipulation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you gain access to new ways to manipulate the earth around yourself.
Rock Blast. As an action, you can spend 1 CE to imbue your cursed energy into a rock and launch it at a target within 30 feet. You can use your CE modifier or Strength modifier for the attack and damage roll. On a hit, you deal 1d12 bludgeoning damage (you can spend 1 additional CE to instead deal necrotic damage). If you have the extra attack feature, you can replace one of your attacks this way.
Earthen Armor. As a bonus action, you can spend CE up to your proficiency bonus to protect yourself with earth. For 1 minute, you gain a bonus to your AC equal to the cursed energy spent.
Tremor. As an action, you can spend 3 cursed energy to strike the ground. Creatures in a 20-foot radius around yourself must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 3d10 bludgeoning damage and are knocked prone. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not prone. Structures automatically fail and take maximum damage. This increases to 4d10 at 6th level, 5d10 at 11th level, and 6d10 at 18th level.

Earth Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to create large scale constructs. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you make a wall of stone. This wall is made of ten 10 foot by 10 foot panels that are 1 inch thick. Each panel must be touching at least one other panel. The wall has an AC equal to your cursed energy DC and a number of hit points equal to 10 times your CE modifier.

You can spend 1 CE as a bonus action to move connected panels within 60 feet of you up to 30 feet in a direction of your choice that is in contact with the ground. If this movement would move a creature, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or be pushed by the wall.

Earth Manipulation — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned a new way to use the stone you manipulate. You are now able to create two big arms that can catch a target. As an action for 5 cursed energy, you can force a target within 60 ft to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they are wedged between the arms taking 6d12 bludgeoning damage, and are restrained, becoming stuck between the hands until the start of your next turn. On a success, they are not restrained and take half damage.

You can also choose to keep the hands active by spending 1 CE at the start of your turns. Every turn you have it active you can use an action to crush a creature restrained by your hands, forcing them to make a Strength saving throw. If they fail they take another 4d12 bludgeoning damage or half as much on a success. A creature can use their action to make an Athletics or Acrobatics check against your Cursed Energy DC, escaping on a success. While maintaining your stone arms, they have AC 18 and HP equal to your maximum hit points and you must maintain concentration.

Earth Manipulation — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain take 6d12 bludgeoning damage and are restrained by shifting stone until the start of their next turn.
You can spend an action to change the environment of your domain.

  • You can create a large 20 ft radius, 1d10 x 10 feet deep chasm causing creatures to fall and take falling damage.

  • You can create a 100 ft tall tower of stone (as if casting Galdur’s Tower with 10 stories).

  • You can create 100 ft of difficult terrain in an area you can see. A creature that moves through this area takes 2d4 piercing damage for every 5 feet moved.

Eight Heads — Innate Technique (1st level)

One of your ancestors devoured Yamata no Orochi, the Eight Headed Serpent, creating a hereditary technique with its power.

Starting at 1st level, you have the ability to come back to life after you die, up to 8 times. When you are reduced to 0 hit points or die outright, you can spend 1 CE to come back to life at half your hitpoint maximum and harmful conditions other than exhaustion are removed. You have 8 lives and can use a life this way three times per long rest. This increases to four at 3rd level and eight at 6th level. You regain one expended life after eight days.

Eight Heads — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, when you make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability check or saving throw, you can spend 1 cursed energy to reroll and must use the new roll. You can use this feature up to 8 times per long rest.

activation.condition: Immediately after an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma ability check or saving throw

description.value:
Eight Heads — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, as an action you can spend up to 8 cursed energy to summon an equal number of fangs from the jaws of Yamata no Orochi as shikigami. They appear in unoccupied spaces of your choice within 10 ft. You can have up to 8 summoned at a time.
You can command any Fangs you have summoned as a bonus action. These Fangs disappear if you become unconscious and if destroyed cannot be resummoned for 1 minute. The Fangs hit points increase to 20 at 11th level.

Eight Heads — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, when you have at least 3 Fangs of Orochi summoned, you can command them as an action for 6 cursed energy to move up to 40 ft, encircle a creature, and embed themselves into the ground in an unoccupied area. A barrier forms, connecting the Fangs like a cylinder resembling a trigram and trapping any within.

The barrier has a height of 20 ft and can have a maximum diameter of 15 ft. It has 20 AC and hit points equal to the hit points of the Fangs of Orochi used to create it. A trapped creature makes a cursed energy save at the start of their turns, taking 10d4 necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful save.

If this damage reduces a humanoid to 0 hit points, the creature dies and you regain one life. Once you regain a life in this way, you cannot for 1 week.

Eight Heads — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have constructed a domain filled with your technique. The domain takes the form of grassy wetlands. At initiative 20, Yamata no Orochi forms from the earth. The shikigami does not take actions and does not have a turn in initiative. This is a false incarnation that only exists within your domain, containing the shackled mind of the original Yamata no Orochi.
On initiative 20 after Yamata no Orochi has formed, roll a 1d8. That number of creatures of your choice within the domain each suffer its bite. The shikigami disappears when your domain ends.

description.value:
Esoteric Art — Innate Technique (1st level)

You were born with the ability to create cursed paintings leading to unique subspaces.

Starting at 1st level, you can spend 1 cursed energy to create a painting of cursed ink under a Medium or smaller creature within 30 ft, forcing them to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are sucked into the painting. The painting takes the form of an empty 30 ft radius cube subspace of greyscale. You can change the color or create simple illustrations within the subspace as an action. You can enter, exit, place, or remove an item from the subspace of your paintings as a free action once per turn without spending cursed energy. Your subspace becomes 120 ft at 3rd level, 600 ft at 6th, and 1200 ft at 11th level.

At the beginning of your turn, you must spend 1 CE to keep any creatures (including yourself) within a painting. Otherwise, they reappear at the point they disappeared.

You can use a binding vow to remove the cost at the beginning of your turn by placing a method of escape. This creates an Exit Painting in a random, but accessible area within the subspace that allows a creature to exit the painting, reappearing in the space they disappeared.

You can have a number of subspaces equal to your CE modifier, but if you have creatures in different paintings, you must spend 1 cursed energy for each subspace at the start of your turn. This increases to twice your CE modifier of paintings at 11th level.

Alternatively, you can paint a physical painting and imbue it with up to 3 cursed energy during its creation, spending 1 hour painting per cursed energy. A creature that gets within 5 ft and can see the painting must make a Dexterity saving throw, getting sucked into the painting on a failed save. A painting imbued this way keeps a creature trapped for 3 rounds. The painting’s subspace can only be accessed through the physical painting.

At 3rd level, you can spend additional cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to imbue the painting with more power and increase the painting time. This increases to twice your CE modifier at 11th level. This allows the painting to keep an unwilling creature trapped for an additional round for every cursed energy spent. You can also use this painting to store items, but it also counts against the number of paintings you can have at once.

At 6th level, you can instead cause the painting to spend the imbued cursed energy to use Ink Wave against a creature that moves within 5 ft of it.

Esoteric Art — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you gain the ability to change the content of one of your paintings in one the following ways while within your painting:
Ink Shikigami. As an action, you can spend up to your Cursed Energy modifier to create one Ink Wolf for each cursed energy spent. Each wolf appears in an unoccupied space you can see anywhere within your painting and acts on your initiative. The wolves obey your verbal commands (no action required).
Exit Shift. You move the Exit Painting up to 80 ft as an action.
Difficult Terrain. As an action, you create a 15 ft radius area of difficult terrain anywhere within your painting. The terrain lasts until the painting ends or until you use this feature again.
Structure Generation. As an action, you create one structure from cursed ink anywhere within your painting. The structure must fit entirely within a 30 ft cube and can be any ordinary structure you choose, such as walls, platforms, towers, bridges, or buildings.
The structure’s AC equals your CE save DC and each 5 ft by 5 ft section has hit points equal to 5 x your proficiency bonus.
If reduced to 0 hit points, it dissolves into ink and disappears. Any creatures standing on the structure when it is destroyed fall or are affected at the DM’s discretion. You can create, destroy, or replace a structure while within the painting.
Trap Creation. As an action, you create one trap of your choice in an unoccupied 5 ft square anywhere within your painting. The trap lasts until triggered or until the painting ends. A creature can detect a trap with an Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check against your Cursed Energy save DC. All traps use your CE save DC.:

  • Pit Trap. When a creature enters the trapped space, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall 20 feet into the pit, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and falling prone.

  • Spike Trap. When a creature enters the trapped space, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall 10 feet into the pit, taking 2d10 piercing damage and falling prone.

  • Snare Trap. When a creature enters the trapped space, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become restrained. A creature can use its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, freeing the target on a success.

  • Rolling Stone Trap. When triggered, an ink-formed boulder rolls in a 5 ft wide 30 ft line from the trap’s space in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 bludgeoning damage and knocked prone on a fail, or half as much damage and not prone on a success.

Esoteric Art — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have improved your technique. You can now manipulate your painting as a bonus action and gain the following improvements and options:
Ink Shikigami. You can summon new types of shikigami:
Greater Ink Wolf (2 CE)
Ink Crow (3 CE)
Exit Shift. You cause the location of the Exit Painting to a new random accessible location in the subspace.
Difficult Terrain. You can now create a 30 ft radius area of difficult terrain anywhere within your painting.
Structure Generation. Each 5 ft by 5 ft section of a structure you create now has hit points equal to 10 x your proficiency bonus.
Trap Creation. Your traps now deal an additional 2 damage dice. This increases to an additional 4 damage dice at 11th level.
Ink Wave. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you create a 30 ft cone originating from you or an Ink Shikigami. A creature within the cone must make a Constitution saving throw, taking your proficiency bonus in d6s of necrotic damage and be blinded until the end of their next turn on a failed save. (This can also be used outside your subspace)
Larger Frames. You can now use Cursed Painting on Large or smaller creatures. This increases to Huge at 11th level.

Esoteric Art — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, as an action, you can spend cursed energy up to twice your CE modifier, forcing that number of creatures within 60 ft to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are sucked into your cursed paintings.

Esoteric Art — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. The inside of your domain counts as your painting’s subspace, expanding to the same size as your subspace and following the same rules, except your Ink Shikigami and Traps are imbued with your guaranteed hit. At initiative 20, two different Impasto Canvas effects of your choice happen (if you choose Ink Shikigami, they still cost Cursed Energy).

Explosive Flesh — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can make your body into a deadly bomb.

Starting at 1st level, you can make any part of you a deadly bomb. You spend cursed energy to remove and throw your body parts. You remove the part as described below. Throwing takes an action:

Attack Cost Action Effect
Tiny(Tooth, Finger, Hair) 1 CE + Con mod HP Free action You throw the body part at a point within 120ft. Creatures within 5 ft make a Dex save. On a failure, they take Xd6 force damage. On a success, they take half.
Small(Ears, Nose) 2 CE + Con mod×half your level HP Bonus action You throw the body part at a point within 100ft. Creatures within 10 ft make a Dex save. On a failure, they take Xd8 force damage and are knocked prone. On a success they take half.
Medium(Hands, Feet) 4 CE + Con mod×level HP Action You throw the body part at a point within 80ft. Creatures within 15 ft make a Dex save. On a failure, they take Xd10 force damage and are knocked prone. On a success, they take half.
Large(Arms, Legs) 6 CE + Con mod×level HP Full Turn Action You throw the body part at a point within 60ft. Creatures within 20 ft make a Dex save. On a failure, they take Xd12 force damage and are knocked prone. On a success, they take half.

After using a limb or body part in an explosion, it will be considered removed (Con mod is treated as min of 1).
The X is your CE modifier. Damage from this technique deals twice as much damage to objects and structures.

Explosive Flesh — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have gained more expertise over your technique, and can now throw your bombs faster. You can now throw a body part as an action or bonus action.

Explosive Flesh — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, your practice with your explosions allowed you to make them in an instant. You can now instantly explode one of your body parts for the normal cost, as a reaction to receiving or hitting a melee attack roll as the body part explodes on your body. All creatures make the Dexterity saving throw with disadvantage unless their passive perception is higher than your cursed energy DC.

Explosive Flesh — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, with the extensive use of your technique, your explosions became deadlier. When a creature fails the saving throw of your explosions, they gain the deafened condition for 1 minute. They can make a Constitution saving throw at the beginning of their turns, ending the condition early on a success. Also, your explosions deal three times as much damage to objects and structures and their explosion range is increased by 5ft.
At 18th level, the creature also gains the blinded condition.

Explosive Flesh — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. You can detonate any of your body parts for no CE cost. At initiative 20, you can choose a limb (arm or leg) from a creature inside your domain and detonate it.

Full turn: Action + Bonus Action + Movement

description.value:
Fa Jin — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can store and release kinetic energy using your cursed technique.

Starting at 1st level, you can store and release energy. When you miss with a melee attack, you gain a Jin charge. You can have a number of Jin charges equal to your proficiency bonus + your level.
You can spend a Jin charge or 1 Cursed Energy to either gain a +2 to a melee or cursed energy attack roll or deal an additional damage die for each charge spent.
You must declare how many Jin charges you are using before making an attack or using a technique and can use a number of Jin charges equal to your proficiency bonus at once. On a miss, you waste the Jin charges. You lose all unused Jin charges on a long rest.

Fa Jin — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you gain more flexibility when using your Fa Jin. At the beginning of your turn, you can forgo your movement or spend 1 cursed energy to gain a Jin charge. You can now also use a Jin charge to increase your movement speed by 10 feet and triple your jump distance until the end of your turn or to instantly move 10 feet per charge in any direction as a reaction without provoking opportunity attacks.

Fa Jin — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to use your cursed energy to amplify your Fa Jin. You can spend 3 cursed energy as an action to launch a blast of compressed air using Jin charges, which have different effects based on the weapon you use.

Attack Effect
Unarmed or Bludgeoning 15 feet cone, Con save, 2D6 bludgeoning damage per Jin charge, knocked prone on a failed save
Slashing or Piercing 30 feet line, Dex save, 2D10 slashing damage per Jin charge

Fa Jin — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned not only how to avoid wasting your stored energy, but how to use it more effectively, granting you the following benefits:

  • When you spend Jin charges to enhance an attack and miss, you can keep a number of Jin charges up to your Cursed Energy modifier instead of losing the charges.

  • When you spend at least 3 Jin charges for Explosive Power, you can increase the range of your compressed air blast by 30 feet, which now deals thunder damage.

  • When you spend ce to gain a Jin charge, you now gain 2 Jin charges for every ce spent.

  • As an action while touching a creature, you can give them a number of your Jin charges up to your CE modifier.

documents.name: Domain Expansion: Hall of Divine Bagua

description.value:
Fa Jin — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have learned your domain. Within your domain, you have unlimited Jin charges and at initiative 20, all creatures within your domain gain a permanent negative Jin charge, causing them to deal 1d6 less damage on their next attack or technique for each charge. These charges disappear when your domain ends.

Faceless God — Innate Technique (1st level)

Just a glance in your direction slowly leads to mental corruption.

Starting at 1st level, just looking at you slowly leads to mental corruption. As an action for 3 cursed energy, you can activate your technique for 1 minute causing madness to spread to everyone around you. If a creature ends their turn within 60 ft of you and can see you, it gains a 5% increase to Mental Corruption. You can choose a number of creatures to be immune to this effect when you activate the technique.

Corruption Rate Effect
10% -1 to AC
20% -1 to saves
25% Roll D10
30% -4 to passive Perception
40% -2 to AC and saves
50% Roll D6, Can’t maintain Concentration
60% Disadvantage on skill checks
70% Charmed by you
75% Roll D4
80% -4 to AC and saves
90% Random Direction
100% Can’t talk, only scream

Paranoia and Madness. When a creature reaches 25% Mental Corruption, they begin seeing all creatures as faceless monsters and must roll a d10 at the start of their turn. On a roll of 1-2, the target spends their action attacking the closest creature. A creature can only have up to 25% Mental Corruption at a time.

Madness Removal. Mental Corruption persists even after your technique has been deactivated. A creature without line of sight to you can make a Wisdom saving throw to reduce Mental Corruption by 5% and repeat the save at the beginning of their turn. If a creature has more than 25% corruption, they cannot reduce corruption below 25% as the madness becomes rooted more deeply within their mind. As part of a long rest, they can attempt to make a Wisdom saving throw to cleanse their mind. On a success, they can begin making saves to reduce madness as normal, down to the next 25% segment before they must complete another long rest to repeat the save and continue to process.

Faceless God — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you learn to directly inject madness into a creature. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack while your technique is active, they gain a 5% increase to Mental Corruption. You can spend additional cursed energy up to your proficiency bonus on a hit to increase Mental Corruption by 5% per cursed energy spent.

Faceless God — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, the percent of Mental Corruption you can force on a creature increases to 50% and increases by 25% again at 11th level and 18th level. The die size for Paranoia and Madness decreases with every 25% increase and at 100% it happens automatically. At 90% you fall further into madness and must make a Wisdom saving throw at the beginning of your turn, moving in a random direction on a failed save.

Faceless God — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you can spend 6 cursed energy as an action to target a creature within 30 feet that you can see and is currently afflicted by your madness. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw or take 1d10 psychic damage per 10% Mental Corruption they currently have.
A creature with more than 50% Mental Corruption makes this save with disadvantage.

Faceless God — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain gains 5% Mental Corruption. Creatures gain a -1 penalty to all rolls for every 10% Mental Corruption they have while within your domain.

Fate — Innate Technique (1st level)

The wheel of fate is yours to steer and yours alone.

Beginning at 1st level, you can weave together threads of fate. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you bind two creatures within 30 ft of you with an invisible red thread for 1 minute. If a Fate requires Touch, you must touch both targets, but not necessarily at the same time. You choose a Fate, +1 Fate per 2 additional CE, up to your proficiency bonus that affects both while within 30 ft of each other:

Fate Effect Requirement
Bonds The targets gain a +2 bonus to AC. N/A
Promised Time? The creatures both have either advantage or disadvantage on attacks against each other. N/A
Mirrored If one target rolls a 20 or 1 on their turn, the other’s next roll will be the opposite. N/A
Magnetic If targets start their turn within 30 ft of each other, they are pulled 10 ft closer. If this brings them within 5 ft, they become tangled and prone (Str save to pull away). Touch
Shared Strengths Choose a damage resistance, immunity, vulnerability or condition immunity of a target. Both targets share that strength/weakness. 6th level
Linked Suffering When one of the linked targets takes damage, they take half as much damage and the linked creature takes the other half. 6th level, Touch
Destined Death The targets both have either advantage or disadvantage on saves against each other. 11th level, Touch

An effect that would damage the soul is capable of cutting your thread and removing your technique’s effects. Additionally, you cannot manipulate the fate of a creature that is completely lacking cursed energy (such as via Heavenly Restriction).

effects.description: Conditional bonus: enable this effect while its condition applies.

description.value:
Fate — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you learn that fate is not simple. It is what makes up all connections between people and everything else. As a bonus action for 1 CE, when you look at a creature you can focus until you see the red threads of fate that connect the souls of all living creatures. As part of this bonus action, you can tell who the threads connect to if they are within sight, as well as the type of connection. This can range from familial connections, admiration, or feelings of love.
Alternatively, you can instead read the target’s personal thread of fate to learn one of the following:

  • The target’s damage resistances, immunities, or vulnerabilities.

  • The target’s CR or Level.

  • The target’s remaining hit points.

  • The target’s AC or an Ability modifier.

  • The target’s current emotions.

Fate — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to strengthen your threads of fate with cursed energy. When you apply a fate to creatures, you can increase the duration by 1 minute per additional cursed energy spent. As a reaction to the target’s turn starting for 2 CE, you can cause a creature under one of your Fates to take Xd8 bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage (your choice) equaling your proficiency bonus as random unlucky phenomena assaults them. Additionally, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.
At 11th level, your Fate Manipulation now lasts for 1 hour and you can increase the duration by 1 hour per additional cursed energy spent.

Fate — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to permanently entangle souls in the web of fate. Over an uninterrupted period of 1 week, you permanently intertwine the fates of two or more creatures together. The creatures become destined to meet by fate. You can attach this to an incredibly unique part of one of the creatures, such as Inherited Technique, Special Trait, or unique Constitution (Star Plasma Vessel) to cause it to be passed down even after the targets’ deaths. You can have a number of creatures with permanently intertwined fate equal to your proficiency bonus at once (including yourself).
Immortality. As a side effect of your technique, your fate has become set. You cannot die of old age, but still grow older. Every 500 years you must assimilate with a genetically similar human to reset your body and appearance. Failure to meet this causes you to begin to evolve beyond humanity, changing your race to Cursed Spirit.
Fate Control. As an action for 8 CE, you manifest fate for 1 minute. While active, you gain 3 fate points at the beginning of your turns. You can spend one fate point to add a -5 penalty to an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw made by a creature you can see within 30 ft (cannot stack). Unused fate points disappear at the start of your turn. While active, damage dice of Strong Destiny is doubled.

Fate — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you select a creature within your domain as your Destined Foe. While your Destined Foe is within your domain, all your attacks against them are imbued with your guaranteed hit. You can switch your Destined Foe to another creature at initiative 20.

Your innate technique features count your domain as being within range and you can ignore the Touch Requirement of Fates.

G Warstaff — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can conjure a pen-like cursed tool that lets you see the future.

Starting at 1st level, you can summon a pen-like cursed tool that allows you to see into the future of your opponents. As a bonus action for 2 cursed energy, you create an oversized pen-like cursed tool. This cursed tool has the reach and two-handed properties and you can use your CE modifier for its attack and damage rolls. On a hit it deals 1d4 + your CE modifier piercing damage and counts as a grade 4 cursed tool and can be used with martial arts die. You can dismiss the Warstaff at will and can only have one created at a time.

When you hit a creature with G Warstaff, you fulfill the condition for ink and attach a manga panel to the target, being able to view 1 second into the target's future. Hitting a target more than once adds another 1 second to the total, making you gain the benefits of the earlier seconds and the current. As a reaction or bonus action for 1 cursed energy, you can view that creature's future again and gain the following foresights until the beginning of your next turn depending on the creature’s marks. You cannot use this while blinded.

Seconds Foresight
1 Second The creature's attack rolls against you are made at disadvantage
2 Seconds You have advantage on saving throws from that creature
3 Seconds You have advantage on attack rolls against that creature
4 Seconds You know the next actions of the creature (The DM tells you at the start of their turn)
5 Seconds You know the next actions of the creature (The DM tells you at the end of your turn)
6 Seconds You know the next actions of the creature (The DM tells you at the beginning of your turn)

You can only see into a number of seconds into a creature's future equal to your proficiency bonus. The number of creatures that can be affected by this technique is equal to your CE modifier, and you can end the technique at will or it ends when the combat ends.

G Warstaff — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, with the power of reading into the future, no one surprises you anymore. As long as you can see 2 seconds into a creature's future, you take half damage on a failure, and no damage on a success against saving throws caused by that creature.

G Warstaff — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, your opponents become extremely easy to read after being affected by your technique, and you learned how to exploit that. Once per turn when you hit an attack using G Warstaff against a creature that you can see 3 seconds into the future, you can turn that attack into a critical. You cannot roll for a black flash using this feature.

G Warstaff — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you can glimpse your own future, knowing exactly what to do and when. When you roll with advantage against a creature because of your technique, your critical range is increased by half your CE modifier(rounded down).
Whenever a creature rolls with disadvantage against you because of your technique, the roll’s critical fail range is increased by half of your CE modifier(rounded down). For example, if you have a +4 CE modifier and they roll a natural 3 on their roll, it counts as a critical failure.

G Warstaff — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. All creatures in your domain count as having 6 seconds marked and at initiative 20, you can see 6 seconds into the future of all creatures.

Golden Hour — Innate Technique (1st level)

You have the unique ability to manipulate time when you strike a pose.

At 1st level, you can strike a pose and move so quickly it seems as if time has stopped. As a bonus action for 1 cursed energy you can stop time until the end of your turn. During stopped time, you cannot use cursed energy, and are affected by the following:

  • You have advantage on all attack rolls against creatures in stopped time.

  • Ranged attacks you make become affected by stopped time and are suspended in mid-air, but finish when time resumes.

  • Other creatures in stopped time automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saves and cannot use reactions. (A creature can use their reaction against a ranged attack you have made once time has resumed.)

Golden Hour — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you can instead spend up to twice your proficiency bonus in cursed energy as a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) to strike a majestic pose and immediately take one turn per three CE spent in stopped time. Doing so places extreme stress on your body. Once time resumes your movement speed is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn.
When you stop time, your speed increases by 10 ft until time resumes. This increases by 5 ft at 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

description.value:
Golden Hour — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have begun to master your technique. You have learned to use your technique for longer. As an action for 4 cursed energy instead of stopping time you can empower yourself for longer, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

  • Your speed is doubled.

  • You gain a +3 bonus to AC.

  • You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws.

  • You gain an additional action on each of its turns. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.

You cannot stop time until this feature ends.

Golden Hour — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have gained the limited ability to reverse time. As a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) for 8 cursed energy you can strike a supreme pose and rewind time by 6 seconds, taking all creatures and objects within 100 ft back in time 1 round to the start of your previous turn.
Any damage taken or cursed energy spent (other than this technique) during that round is undone and all creatures are taken back to where they were 6 seconds ago as long as it is within the 100 ft radius of the rewind.

Golden Hour — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have created a domain imbued with your perfected technique. At initiative 20, you can stop time and immediately take one turn as your domain empowers you. Whenever you stop time in your domain using your technique, you stop time for an additional turn.

Hair Manipulation — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique allows you to form your hair into a variety of shapes.

Beginning at 1st level, you have learned to move your hair into different forms using cursed energy. When you take the Attack action, you can spend 1 CE to replace an attack by shaping your hair into a barbed stinger. Make a melee cursed energy attack against a creature within 10 ft of you. On a hit you deal 1d10 + your CE modifier piercing damage. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this attack at 3rd level. This increases to a +2 bonus at 6th level, +3 bonus at 11th level and +4 bonus at 18th level.

Hair Manipulation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have learned to form your hair into drill bits and shoot them off as projectiles. When you take the Attack action, you can spend 1 cursed energy to replace an attack with a ranged cursed energy attack roll with a range of 30ft. This attack deals 1d6 + your CE modifier piercing damage. The range of this technique increases to 60 ft at 6th level.

When attacking with a drill, you can spend an additional 2 cursed energy to make the drill explode in a 5 ft radius upon the point of impact causing creatures in range to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take an additional 3d6 fire damage. On a success, they take half as much damage. The fire damage increases to 5d6 at 6th level, 8d6 at 11th level and 10d6 at 18th level.

Hair Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level you have learned to make more complex constructs from your hair. As an action for 3 CE, you form your hair into either a Jet or Helicopter for 1 minute and can spend 1 CE to keep the form active for 1 minute:

Helicopter Hair. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can take the Dash action as a bonus action. When you take the attack action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to replace one attack by extending your blades and attempting to slash an enemy. Make a melee cursed energy attack, on a hit you deal 6d8 + your CE modifier slashing damage. This damage increases to 8d8 at 11th level, and 10d8 at 18th level.
A creature that hits you with an Opportunity attack takes slashing damage equal to your CE modifier. This becomes twice your CE modifier at 11th level.

Jet Hair. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. When you take the dash action while flying, you not only do not provoke opportunity attacks, but can also choose to move in a straight line and crash through creatures. All creatures in your path must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take Xd8 bludgeoning damage and are pushed back 30 ft away from you and knocked prone. If they impact a solid surface, they take 1d4 bludgeoning for every 10 ft you traveled in a straight line before crashing into them. On a successful save they take half as much damage and are not pushed or knocked prone. (X = CE modifier)

At 11th level, taking the Dash action while flying you instead move up to twice your flying speed. This increases to three times your flying speed at 18th level.

Hair Manipulation — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, your hair has become almost indestructible, allowing you to grow it to longer lengths and activate your techniques more freely. The melee reach of your techniques increases by 5 ft and your hair counts as a Grade 1 Cursed Tool. At 18th level, your hair counts as a Special Grade Cursed Tool.

Once per turn you can spend 2 additional CE to activate one of your technique features requiring an attack roll as a bonus action. An attack roll made using this special free action is made at advantage. Alternatively, once per turn you can spend 4 CE to activate one of your technique features requiring a saving throw as a bonus action. A saving throw forced by this special free action is made at disadvantage.

Finally at 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. Creatures other than you take 2d10 slashing damage for every 5 ft they move within your domain as infinitesimally small and sharp hairs cut into them with their every movement. Your domain counts as difficult terrain for creatures other than you.

Heart Catch — Innate Technique (1st level)

A simple yet effective technique, powered by the heart.

Starting at 1st level, you create a pair of translucent hands as a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy. These hands stay within 15 ft of you and each count as medium constructs. You can replace any attacks you make on your turn with an attack from your Love Hands. These hands deal your unarmed damage, and have advantage on grappling and shoving. The hands have an AC equal to your Cursed Energy save DC, HP equal to twice your cursed energy score and you take 1/10th of damage they take. This increases to three times your cursed energy score at 6th level and four times at 11th level.

Heart Catch — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your love hands improve. Your hands gain the following benefits:

  • Your hands AC increase by your proficiency bonus

  • Your hands gain a damage bonus equal to your CE modifier

  • The range of your hands increases to a total of 30 feet

  • Grappled creatures are also restrained

  • You can use cursed feats and abilities using your hands

Heart Catch — Innate Technique (6th level)

Beginning at 6th level, you can use your Love Hands to guard a creature within 5 ft of both hands, granting them three quarters cover. Alternatively, you can have each hand guard a different target to grant them half cover.

Heart Catch — Innate Technique (11th level)

Starting at 11th level, on a hit you can spend 5 Cursed Energy to force a creature you hit with a melee attack to become Charmed. A creature charmed in this way can only target you with attacks and harmful effects for 1 minute and must make a Wisdom save at the start of their turn to end the condition.

Heart Catch — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have learned the true meaning of love. At initiative 20 all creatures in the Domain are restrained and charmed until the end of their next turn. Additionally, your Love Hands automatically hit all attack rolls and creatures automatically fail grapple and shove checks as well as saving throws made by the hands.

Ice Formation — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique is beautiful in its simplicity, and the ability to make and control ice.

Beginning at 1st level, your innate technique has allowed you to mess with the temperature around you, creating extreme levels of cold. As an action for 1 cursed energy, you can force creatures in a 10ft cone to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 1d10 cold damage and are restrained as ice covers part of their bodies. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not restrained.
The creature can make a Strength saving throw at the beginning of its turns to break the ice and end the restrained condition.
All ice created by your technique will last until you end it as a free action, a creature breaks it, or you are poisoned, incapacitated, or unconscious.
At 3rd level, the damage of this feature increases to 2d10, to 3d10 at 6th, to 4d10 at 10th, to 5d10 at 14th, and to 6d10 cold damage at 20th level.

Ice Formation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, being stuck on your ice feels like staying in a cold mountain while you wait for death. A creature inside your ice is under one level of Exhaustion. Any creatures within 5ft of your ice that don't have resistance or immunity to cold damage have their movement speed halved.

Ice Formation — Innate Technique (6th level)

When you reach 6th level, you have learned how to unleash thick layers of ice through the mist. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you can send a cloud of freezing mist to a spot within 60 feet of you. Every creature in a 30-foot radius sphere in that spot must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 6d8 cold damage and are restrained by an ice layer. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not restrained.
The creature can make a Strength saving throw at the beginning of its turns to break the ice and end the restrained condition.

Ice Formation — Innate Technique (11th level)

Once you reach 11th level, you learn a great execution method that makes sure your enemies won't escape. As an action for 8 cursed energy, you fall prone until the beginning of your next turn to create ice on the ground. You telepathically manipulate the ice created, launching one for every creature within 30 ft of you of your choice. Make a cursed energy attack roll, on a hit they take 1d10 cold damage and become restrained.
The creature can make a Strength saving throw at the beginning of its turns to break the ice and end the restrained condition.
Hitting or missing, giant spikes of ice will fall from the sky on top of the targeted creatures, forcing them to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 6d8 cold damage and 6d8 piercing damage. On a success, they take half as much damage.

Ice Formation — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

If you achieve 18th level, you hone your technique to a fine edge, allowing you to use your Domain Expansion. While inside it, every creature except you takes 10d8 cold damage and is restrained at the end of their turn. A creature can make a Strength (Athletics) check at the beginning of their turn to break out.

Idle Transfiguration — Innate Technique (1st level)

The soul is an interesting thing and your technique manipulates it.

Starting at 1st level, your touch can alter a creature's very own being, their soul. Whenever you hit a creature with a natural weapon, unarmed strike, or touch them, you can deal an additional 1d6 Necrotic damage.
In addition, as an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can force a creature within your reach to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they will take 1d10 Necrotic Damage, which increases to 2d10 at 3rd level, 3d10 at 6th level, 4d10 at 11th level, and 5d10 at 18th level. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage. This damage reduces a creature’s hit point maximum until they finish a long rest.
If Necrotic damage from any features of Idle Transfiguration reduces a creature's total hit points to 0, the creature will become one of your Transfigured Creatures. This does not work on Constructs.
Transfigured Creatures. You can have a number of transfigured creatures equal to your level x your Cursed Energy modifier. Transfigured creatures will follow your orders, act at the end of your turn and their creature type is undead. On a short or long rest, you can modify a transfigured creature’s size from tiny to huge.

  • Ability Scores. The creature’s mental scores will be decreased to 4. You can redistribute the points removed from their mental stats into their physical scores, even beyond 20.

  • Primitiveness. Transformed creatures lose all supernatural abilities like cursed technique as well as proficiencies, and their AC is 10 + Dexterity modifier. They can only use natural weapons or unarmed attacks. They roll a d6 in place of the normal damage of their unarmed strike.

You can command with simple orders such as to attack a creature as a bonus action. Complex orders like area control are an action. You can store transfigured creatures, extracting any number as an action.

Idle Transfiguration — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Beginning at 3rd level, you can safely alter yourself or an ally.
Ally Alteration: You can use your alteration on willing creatures, to alter them as you see fit. You alter a willing creature during a short or long rest, granting them one or more of the following benefits:

Alteration Description
Heightened Smell The creature gains advantage in perception checks involving smell.
Heightened Hearing The creature gains advantage in perception checks involving hearing.
Heightened Sight The creature gains advantage in perception checks involving seeing.
Darkvision The creature gains darkvision up to 60 feet, if the creature already has darkvision it will extend its range by 30 feet.
Hardened Skin The creature gains resistance to either: bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing.
Gills The creature gains a swimming speed equal to its walking speed and can breathe underwater.

You can grant a number of different alterations to the same creature equal to your proficiency.

Self-Alteration: You have learned how to shape your own form in many different ways. As a bonus action, you can gain new body parts. You can choose one of the following:

Alteration CE Cost Description Restrictions
Sword Arms 2 Your unarmed strikes deal slashing and count as light, finesse, martial melee weapons No Spike Hands or Wings
Spike Hands 2 Your unarmed strikes deal piercing damage, and increases damage by your Proficiency No Sword Arms or Wings
Arm Shields 2 +2 bonus to AC. No Wings
Long Arms 2 Increase melee reach by 10 feet No Wings
Horse Hooves 3 Increase movement by 10 feet and Bonus Action dash. N/A
Spiked Skin 2 As a reaction to a melee attack within 5 feet, you can deal Piercing damage equal to 4x your Proficiency. N/A
Wings 4 You gain a 60 ft fly speed. While at least 15 feet away, you gain a +2 bonus to AC No Spike Hands, Sword Hands, Arm Shield, or Long Arms

At 6th level, you gain the following Self-Alteration option:
Size Change. For 2 CE, you increase or decrease your size by 1 category for 1 min (does not stack). While enlarged you have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws and your unarmed strikes deal 1d4 extra damage. While reduced you have advantage on Dexterity checks and saves and a +1 to AC. You can revert as a bonus action.

description.value:
Idle Transfiguration — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned how to create a near perfect clone of yourself. As an action for 6 Cursed Energy, you create a copy of yourself, giving it half of your current and max Hit Points and Cursed Energy. It is identical to you, controlled by you, acts at the end of your turn, and you can view through its senses. Your clone cannot use your Innate Technique features except Self-Alteration. You can't make another clone until it dies or you touch it and rejoin, granting you back the rest of your max HP and Cursed Energy.

Idle Transfiguration — Innate Technique (11th level)

Starting at 11th level, you can use Self-Alteration as a free action on your turn. As an action for 5 Cursed Energy you can spend 2 or more Transfigured Creatures, fusing together for one of the following:
Body Repel. You create a barrage of Transfigured creatures being launched at high speeds. You make a ranged Cursed Energy attack with a range of 60/120 feet that deals 4d8 necrotic damage on a hit. For every additional Transfigured Creature, you deal another 1d8 necrotic damage and can split the damage die between different targets to make multiple attacks.
Polymorphic Soul Isomer. You create a Polymorphic Soul Isomer for 1 minute. When using this technique, you can add another Transfigured Creature to the fusion. Each transfigured creature counts as one soul.

Finally, at 18th level, you have studied your powers and have finally learned your most powerful technique. You create a large dimension filled with your body parts, making escaping death impossible. At initiative 20 creatures within your domain suffer twice your Transfiguration touch damage.

Illusive Mirage — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique lets you curse people and make them see illusions.

At 1st level, your technique allows you to curse creatures and make them see other people's faces in a distorted way. You are also able to track those you have cursed. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you can curse a creature within 60 feet. The target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the next person they see has a distorted face. Upon seeing this distortion for the first time, the creature must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, the creature is confused and has disadvantage on attack rolls and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma checks until the end of their next turn. A sorcerer can repeat the Charisma save at the end of their turns to end the curse.
When a creature fails their Charisma saving throw, you gain the ability to track them up to 400 feet away. While a creature is cursed, you know its general location. The cursed creature keeps seeing the distorted face until they succeed the save or leave your tracking range.

At 6th level, you can target a number of creatures up to your Cursed Energy modifier as an action, spending 2 CE for each. Additionally, a creature that fails its save also has disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saves and loses concentration on any technique or feature it was concentrating on.

Illusive Mirage — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you’ve learned how to distort your own body to confuse your opponents. You learn the 3 following distortion techniques:
Phase Fist. As part of making a melee attack, you can spend 3 cursed energy to create a duplicate of your weapon. Make a melee cursed attack roll at disadvantage, afterwards you make your normal attack against the same target. If the phase attack misses the actual attack will deal double the damage dice on a hit and if the phase attack hits the main attack will instead be made at advantage.
Blurring. As an action for 3 cursed energy, your body becomes blurred, shifting and wavering to all who can see you. For a number of rounds equal to your Cursed Energy modifier, a creature that can see you has disadvantage on attack rolls against you. An attacker is immune to this effect if it doesn't rely on sight like blindsight or can see through illusions like with true sight.
Distorting Disguise. For 3 cursed energy, you make yourself (including your clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings) look different for a number of hours equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. The changes of this feature fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, if you use this technique to add a hat to your outfit, objects pass through the hat, and anyone who touches it would feel nothing or would feel your head and hair. If you use this spell to appear thinner than you are, the hand of someone who reaches out to touch you would bump into you while it was seemingly still in midair. To discern that you are disguised, a creature can use its action to inspect your appearance and must succeed on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your cursed energy save DC.

Illusive Mirage — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have now learned a new way to distort the surroundings of those you have cursed. As an action, you may choose an object within the range of your cursed illusion that you can see to distort its appearance, this can include changing its opacity, luster, visible texture, or its seen value. A creature can attempt to discern the illusion by rolling an investigation check against your cursed energy save DC. You can spend an additional 3 CE to make the object invisible. If a creature runs into a medium or larger invisible object, they take 1d6 bludgeoning and lose their reaction.
The cost of the technique depends on the size of the targeted object:

Size CE Cost
Tiny 1
Small 2
Medium 3
Large 4
Huge 6
Gargantuan 10

activation.condition: You can spend an additional 3 CE to make the object invisible.

description.value:
Illusive Mirage — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have decided that affecting the area around people can lead to strategic victory. As an action for 10 cursed energy, you can manipulate the surrounding terrain around you in a 150 ft radius in the following ways:

  • Rough Ground. You make the terrain appear difficult to traverse, when a creature attempts to walk in this area they must spend twice as much movement per 5 ft of travel.

  • Obstructing Illusion. As an action, you make a false structure or wall within range. A creature is convinced that the structure is real, meaning that they cannot target you with features that require line of sight.

A creature can attempt to see through the illusion by rolling an Investigation or Perception check (using their Cursed Energy score if they are a Sorcerer) against your Cursed Energy save DC. A creature automatically succeeds if they have an ability like true sight.

Illusive Mirage — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. At initiative 20, you can force all creatures to fall under an illusion of your choice. Additionally, you can use your reaction to trick a creature that attacks you to target a random creature within range. They must roll a dice to see who is targeted with the dice depending on the number of creatures within range. On a 1, you are still targeted. On a higher roll, a different creature is targeted. If there are no other creatures in range, roll a d2. On a 2, the attack targets a random direction, missing you completely.
