Inverse — Innate Technique (1st level)

You invert damage taken based on a specific threshold.

Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to invert the damage you take. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to activate Inverse for 1 minute. While Inverse is active, when you take damage, it is modified based on a damage limit and threshold. The damage limit equals your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy score, and the threshold is equal to your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy modifier.
When you take damage that exceeds your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the remaining difference as damage. However, when the damage is below your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the resulting number as damage instead. For example, if your set limit is 100 and you take 90 damage, you would subtract the damage from your limit if it exceeds the threshold (e.g., 90 - 20 = 70), and take the remaining 70 damage. Conversely, if the damage is below the threshold (e.g., 10 damage), you subtract that amount from your set limit (100 - 10 = 90), and take 90 damage instead. If the calculation results in a negative number, the damage remains unchanged.
You can extend the duration of Inverse by spending 1 cursed energy to maintain the effect for an additional minute.

Inverse — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you’ve learned to further manipulate the damage you take based on its intensity. If you take damage that is below your threshold, you are considered vulnerable to the damage dealt. However, if the damage exceeds your threshold, you gain resistance to the damage, even if it would normally bypass resistances or immunities.
For example, if your threshold is 15 and you take 10 damage, you treat that as vulnerability. But if you take 18 damage, you instead halve it due to your resistance, even if that type of damage would normally ignore resistances.

Inverse — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you’ve become adept at manipulating damage based on its intensity, even when making saving throws. When you are forced to make a saving throw against an effect that deals damage, the difficulty of the save depends on whether the damage is above or below your threshold.
If the damage is above your threshold, you have advantage on the saving throw, regardless of the damage type. If the damage is below your threshold, you have disadvantage on the saving throw, as weaker attacks become more dangerous to you.
For example, if your threshold is 15 and you would take 18 damage from a fireball, you gain advantage on the saving throw. However, if you take 10 damage from the same attack, you would roll with disadvantage instead.

Inverse — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, staying with your technique active for long periods of time can become a disadvantage at times, so you have trained to have easier access to your technique. You can now use your technique as a reaction to damage and can deactivate your technique as a reaction.
In addition, you now have additional reactions equal to half of your proficiency bonus(rounded up) that can be used only for the inverse technique. At 18th level, this becomes a number of reactions equal to your proficiency bonus.

Inverse — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. Within your domain, you can activate Inverse as a free action an infinite number of times for no cost. At initiative 20, creatures of your choice have their senses inverted. Each creature rolls a d4 (1: taste, 2: smell, 3: touch, 4: sight) having a sense inverted and unable to be used. A creature can make a Cursed Energy check at the end of their turn to regain their lost sense.

Laplace’s Demon — Innate Technique (1st level)

A thought experiment proposing an intellect so vast it knows the position and momentum of every particle, allowing it to predict the future and recall the past.

Starting at 1st level, you have extreme control of your emotions with a logical mindset allowing you to use Intelligence as your Cursed Energy modifier. You can spend 1 CE as a bonus action to overclock your brain for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits:

  • You can spend 2 CE to take an action as a reaction.

  • You gain advantage on Intelligence checks.

  • You add your Intelligence modifier to AC and Dexterity saves.

  • You gain the 2000 IQ Skill feat.

Laplace’s Demon — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Starting at 3rd level, you can accelerate your brain to predict the future and past with frightful accuracy.
When you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can spend 1 CE as a reaction to replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check you make, or a saving throw you force another creature to make with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll.
Each foretelling roll can be used only once. When you finish a long rest, you lose any unused foretelling rolls. When you complete a short rest, you can spend 1 CE to gain another foretelling roll. You can only have one foretelling roll from a short rest at a time.

Laplace’s Demon — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to overload the minds of others instead of your own. As an action for 4 cursed energy you can touch a creature and force them to make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure they take 5d10 psychic damage and are stunned until the end of their next turn, on a success they take half as much damage and aren’t stunned.

Laplace’s Demon — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to push the effects of your technique to their maximum limit. As an action, you can spend 8 cursed energy to enter a state of elevated intellect and foresight for 1 hour. All rolls you make are at advantage and all rolls against you are at disadvantage as you are able to see through the truth of the world in its entirety. As a reaction, you can add your Intelligence modifier to an attack roll, skill check or saving throw made by you or a creature within 15 ft of you.

Laplace’s Demon — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain gain a cumulative -2 penalty to all rolls against you as you begin to see the state of every atom.
While inside the domain:

  • You know the hit points, cursed energy, effects, conditions, resistances, immunities, and vulnerabilities of all creatures within the domain.

  • Invisible creatures are always visible to you.

  • Creatures cannot gain advantage against you from being unseen or hidden.

Limitless — Innate Technique (1st level)

A technique whose power is only matched by its complexity,
Limitless allows manipulation over space.

Beginning at 1st level, you gain the ability to use your manipulation over space to protect yourself effectively. As a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can encase yourself in a field of mathematical infinity costing 1 Cursed Energy at the start of your turn. When you are targeted by a weapon, spell, Cursed Energy attack roll or any saving throws from sources outside your body you roll a d6. On a 4 or higher, any attacks or spells made against you automatically fail to touch or harm you in any physical way. At 6th level, this becomes 3 or higher, and 2 or higher at 11th level.
You can spend 1 Cursed Energy to automatically roll a 6 on an Infinity roll. At 11th level, you can spend 2 Cursed Energy at the beginning of each of your turns to automatically roll a 6 on Infinity rolls and you can activate Infinity as a reaction to being targeted by an attack or effect that you can see.
When you take the Dodge action while Infinity is activated, you gain advantage on the d6 roll, and you can grant its benefits to any creatures within your reach.
This feature does not work against poison or attacks that you cannot see until 6th level.

Limitless — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you can create another impossible concept, negative numbers which manifests as negative space. As an action for CE up to your modifier, you pick an unoccupied space within 30 feet you can see and create a 5 ft sphere until the beginning of your next turn as space corrects itself. This pulls targets within a radius of 5 feet for each CE spent, forcing a Strength saving throw. On a failure, they take 2d8 + 1d8 for each CE in force damage and are dragged into the blue and grappled. At 11th level, on a failure of 5 or more they take maximum damage and are restrained. On a success they take half as much damage. A creature can repeat the save at the end of their turn.
When you spend at least 5 CE on Blue, you can use its Maximum Output form to make it last for up to a minute while concentrating. As bonus action, you can move the sphere 30 ft in any direction. All creatures currently stuck in the sphere are also moved and a creature that starts their turn in range must make the saving throw. You can end the technique at will.

Limitless — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, your control over blue and space has increased. As an action, you can teleport yourself or another willing creature you touch 10 ft per Cursed Energy used.
You can teleport an additional creature by doubling the cursed energy cost. Additionally, with the use of a binding vow, you can instead teleport a creature to a 5 ft circle you have prepared. You can teleport a willing creature you touch to one of these circles as an action for 5 cursed energy. You can only have one circle per binding vow.

Limitless — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to push infinity to an aggressive mode through offensive training. As an action, you can spend CE up to your Cursed Energy modifier to amplify Infinity. All creatures within 10 ft must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, they are forced 10 ft directly away from you and take 2d8 force damage per cursed energy spent. On a successful save they take half as much damage and are not pushed away.
If used at Maximum Output, a creature within 5 ft makes this save at disadvantage.
Alternatively, you can choose one target within 5 ft of you and 10 ft away from a wall or solid structure, and spend CE up to your CE modifier as an action to crush them against it. The target must make a Strength saving throw, being forced against the wall and taking 3d8 Force damage for each Cursed Energy spent and be restrained until the start of your next turn on a failed save. On a success, they are pushed 5 ft back and take half as much damage. If you are more than 10 ft away from the target, the technique ends.
If used at Maximum Output, you can spend CE up to your modifier at the start of your turn to maintain the technique, forcing the creature to repeat the save.

Limitless — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level you have learned how to expand your own domain, showing the dangers of the Unlimited Void. You can create a void in space that causes victims to receive all kinds of stimuli and information endlessly, restricting their thought processes and actions. At initiative 20, every creature within your domain that is not touching you must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, they take 12d8 psychic damage, their Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores become 1 and they are unable to cast spells, attack, use magic items, understand language, or communicate in any intelligible way, and fall unconscious for 1 minute. At the end of every minute, the creature can repeat this saving throw, ending these effects on a success. This effect can also be ended by Greater Restoration or Wish.

Love Rendezvous — Innate Technique (1st level)

Love Rendezvous is a technique based on the Southern Cross. It marks creatures or objects with cursed energy and makes the lowest star have to pass through the other ones before they can move.

Starting at 1st level, you have a very complex technique, and you have learned the basics of how to use it. As a free action when you touch a creature or object(this can be done with yourself) with cursed energy or as part of hitting an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 cursed energy to mark the target's cursed energy with a star of your choice. Only one star can be placed in one creature's cursed energy at a time, however the same star can be applied to different people's cursed energy at a time. You can mark a number of creatures with the same star up to your Cursed Energy modifier. If you mark a creature, everything that has their cursed energy will be marked as well, like Shikigami, cursed tools etc.
The following stars are available to mark:
★Imai, ★Acrux, ★Mimosa, ★Ginan and ★Gacrux.

When you mark a creature, a sparking light will appear above their head. They can also find the star's name marked on their body with a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Anyone appointed with a star must follow a sequential order if they want to attempt approaching another star. When they make their movement, they must move directly towards the next star in order and touch them, which allows them to move on to the next star in order. Failing to do this will make them restrained until the beginning of their next turn and every single creature or object marked with the same star will be attracted to the point with the highest cursed energy, being all rapidly thrown at that point. The highest cursed energy point will take 1 dice of bludgeoning damage per 5ft the other stars have travelled and their size, while the objects and creatures that crashed into it will take half as much damage. See the following chart for measure of damage:

Size Damage Dice
Tiny 1d4
Small d6
Medium d8
Large d10
Huge d12
Gargantuan 2d12

The order of the stars is as follows: ★Imai → ★Acrux → ★Mimosa → ★Ginan → ★Gacrux

If there is no possible path for a target to follow the order, the target isn’t affected by the technique until such a possible path is created. The target is immediately affected again once such a path exists. For example, if Gacrux is placed in front of Ginan for a creature marked with Acrux, then the technique no longer functions for that creature, as there is no way to touch Ginan without approaching Gacrux. Once the creature passes Gacrux, thus opening a path for them to get to Ginan, the technique functions for them once more, and they must touch Ginan before approaching Gacrux.

The stars last for 10 minutes or until you remove one or more of them.

Creatures won't know they're being affected by the technique until they suffer the consequences from not following the order. After that, they can make a Perception check to find the star. After they discover the star, they can make a Wisdom (Insight) check at disadvantage against your cursed energy DC to try to understand your technique. Unless they have the Cursed Energy Perception feat or are familiar with the southern star constellation, which allows them to ignore disadvantage to the roll.

Love Rendezvous — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you learned how to mark creatures in a quicker and more effective manner. You can now mark creatures with stars as a reaction. Also, you gain a number of additional reactions equal to your Cursed Energy modifier that can only be used to mark other creatures.

Love Rendezvous — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, your technique's attraction has grown stronger. The damage of creatures colliding now ignores resistance to bludgeoning damage. This becomes force damage at 11th level and ignores resistance to force damage at 18th level.

Love Rendezvous — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you became better with your technique, now being able to have more stars. The amount of stars you can put of the same type is increased to twice your Cursed Energy modifier.

Love Rendezvous — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you can mark any creatures within your domain with any of your available stars. As an action, you can cause a creature marked with one of your stars to move up to 30 ft towards another marked target, taking collision damage if they impact and counting as part of your guaranteed hit. Any marks created by your domain disappear when your domain ends.

Miracle — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique erases your memory of everyday little miracles to store them for when needed.

Starting at 1st level, your technique brings you strength when you witness good fortune. When you witness this, you gain a Miracle. You can have up to six Miracles at once, which are stored as marks somewhere on your body. You gain 2 Miracles for every miracle you witness at 11th level and 3 Miracles at 18th level.

Miracle Description
Lucky! Everyone loves a Jackpot! When you or an ally you can see rolls the maximum amount on a roll, you gain a Miracle.
Equal Numbers! Equal Numbers are supposed to be lucky, right? When you or an ally you can see rolls two equal numbers one after the other, you gain a Miracle.
Treasure! Finding free stuff is always cool! When you or an ally you can see find an item worth $1,000 or more, you gain a Miracle.
Overcoming Hardship Overcoming hardship is something rare in this harsh world, so every chance we get is a miracle. When you or a creature you can see succeeds on a roll they had disadvantage on, you gain a Miracle.

Miracle — Innate Technique (1st level)

Once per round when you take damage, you can spend a Miracle to reduce the incoming damage by Xd4 equal to your CE modifier. You add your proficiency bonus to the rolled amount and reduce the damage by that much. You can also do this as a reaction for a Miracle and 1 CE.
When used this way, the d4 increases to a d6 and you add your proficiency bonus twice.

Miracle — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you can self-consciously alter fate. As a reaction to failing a roll you can spend 1 Miracle and 1 CE to add a d6 to the roll, potentially turning it into a success. This increases to a d8 at 6th level and a d10 at 11th level.

Miracle — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned that out of difficulties, miracles grow. Your technique lets you fend off death by some miracle. When you are hit by an attack or fail a saving throw that would reduce you to 0 hit points or kill you outright, you can spend 2 Miracles and 2 CE to instead succeed the save or survive the attack and take no damage or additional effects. Completely escaping harm by seemingly dumb luck.
While you have at least 1 Miracle, you make death saving throws at advantage.
At 11th level, you can use this feature against an attack or effect that would reduce you to 1/2 or below your hit point maximum.

Miracle — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level you realize there is no bad future for you, only a path to fortune paved with miracles! If you roll 20 or higher using Miraculous Outcome, it is considered a critical success as if you had rolled a natural 20 (cannot roll for Black Flash or gain Miracle).

documents.name: Domain Expansion: Luck of the Draw

description.value:
Miracle — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. Your domain costs 2d20 CE to expand and lasts 1d4 minutes. If you lack the Cursed Energy, you must reattempt on your next turn and reroll the 2d20. If you expand your domain as a reaction to another Domain Expansion, you can choose to spend 20 CE or to roll 2d20.
At initiative 20, you gain 3 Miracles and have no limit on your max amount of Miracles. Within your domain, you can spend a Miracle on yourself or another creature when they make an attack or use a technique to imbue it with your guaranteed hit.

Missile Fist — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can launch a barrage of giant fists against your opponents.

Starting at 1st level, you can spend 1 cursed energy as a bonus action to materialize giant fists of cursed energy. Until the end of your turn, you can replace any of your attacks with a Missile Fist, making a ranged Cursed Energy attack against a creature within 20 ft. A Missile Fist does 1d8 + your CE modifier necrotic damage on a hit. As part of the bonus action you use to activate this technique, you can make one additional Missile Fist attack. If you use Missile Fist against a creature within 5 ft, you can instead make a melee Cursed Energy attack that can use your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

The damage of your Missile Fist increases to 2d8 at 6th level, 3d8 at 11th level, and 4d8 at 18th level.

Missile Fist — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, when you use your Missile Fist, you can spend additional cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to make an additional Missile Fist attack per cursed energy spent. Additionally, the range of your Missile Fists increases to 30 ft. This range increases by 20 ft again at 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

If you hit a creature that is Large or smaller with a Missile Fist, instead of dealing damage, you can choose to grapple it for 1 minute. If you hit a grappled creature that is Large or smaller with a Missile Fist, instead of dealing damage, you can choose to restrain it for 1 minute. A creature can make a Strength saving throw against your CE save DC at the end of their turn to escape your technique. On a success, they can remove one of the Missile Fists, removing either the Grappled or Restrained conditions. These conditions end if you become Incapacitated.

Missile Fist — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned that a strong offense is the only thing that matters. As an action for 3 CE, you create a 30 ft cone of Missile Fists. All creatures within the cone must make a Strength saving throw.
On a failed save, they take 2d8 necrotic damage for every attack you can make as an action and they are knocked prone. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and is not knocked prone. You can spend your bonus action to increase the damage by 2d8. You can spend cursed energy up to your CE modifier to increase damage by 2d8 per CE.

Missile Fist — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you can combine your Missile Fists into a larger, more brutal attack. As a Full-Turn Action Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) for 6 CE, you create a wave of Missile Fists. A creature within 50 ft must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 3d8 + 3d8 necrotic damage for every attack you can make as an action (counting as an additional Missile Fist for range) and is knocked prone. If the target is a creature, the target takes an additional 4d10 bludgeoning damage from being crushed. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much necrotic damage and no bludgeoning damage. If the target is an object or structure, it instead takes maximum damage.
All creatures within 5 ft of the target (+5 ft per Missile Fist) must make a Strength saving throw or similarly be crushed, taking the necrotic damage of the Missile Fist wave on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful save. Objects and structures automatically fail this save. You can spend cursed energy up to your CE modifier to increase the damage by 3d8 per CE spent, counting as an additional Missile Fist.

At 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures take 8d8 necrotic damage and are knocked prone by giant Missile Fists. As an action, you can target any creature of your choice within your domain with a single Missile Fist without spending cursed energy.

Moon Dregs — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique forms a poison unique to you and comes with your own shikigami to help manifest it.

Starting at 1st level, you can use your action to summon a Jellyfish shikigami, which lasts for 8 hours and uses your proficiency bonus. You can spend 1 additional cursed energy to change the shikigami’s size between tiny and large as an action. Moon Dregs only takes the dodge action unless you command Moon Dregs using your bonus action each turn. You can summon Moon Dregs for free once per long rest and again for 5 cursed energy. When Moon Dregs is destroyed, it cannot be summoned again for 1 minute.

Moon Dregs — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your cursed energy has toxic properties which seep into Moon Dregs and empower it. Once per turn, when you or Moon Dregs hit a creature with a melee attack on your turn, you can spend 1 cursed energy to cause the attack to deal an extra 2d6 poison damage. This increases to 4d6 at 6th level, 6d8 at 11th level and 6d10 at 18th level. This damage is not amplified by a critical hit.

You can replace any of your attacks on your turn with an attack from Moon Dregs.

Moon Dregs — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, your cursed energy has become more corrosive and noxious, further seeping into Moon Dregs. When you use Poisonous Cursed Energy, a creature must make a Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. They can repeat the saving throw at the end of their turns, ending the effect on a success. While poisoned in this way, the target has a temporary level of exhaustion.
Moon Dregs can now make two attacks when it takes the attack action and can grant a creature three quarters cover while occupying a creature’s space, and full cover at 11th level.

Moon Dregs — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you can add your Cursed Energy modifier to Moon Dregs’ AC as well as its Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores. Moon Dregs now makes three attacks when it takes the Attack action.

Moon Dregs — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have created a domain embedded with your technique. The air is filled with toxins and appears as if you are underwater, counting as difficult terrain unless you have a swim speed. Creatures are still able to breathe normally.
At initiative 20, all creatures in your domain take 8d6 poison or acid damage. Moon Dregs attacks are imbued with your guaranteed hit and there are a number of tiny jellyfish shikigami swimming around equal to your cursed energy modifier that are also imbued with your guaranteed hit. You can command them as an action. They count as Moon Dregs, can only make 1 attack, and have 30 hitpoints.

description.value:
Mythical Beast Amber — Innate Technique (1st level)

You hold a technique that changes the very essence of your energy to electricity. However, its true power is unknown even to you.

Starting at 1st level, you may not know your cursed technique yet, but you have gained insane mastery over your energy. Once per turn when you deal damage with a melee attack, you can spend 1 cursed energy to add 1d10 lightning damage to the total amount. This increases to 2d10 at 3rd level, 3d10 at 6th level, 4d10 at 11th level, to 5d10 at 14th level, and to 6d10 at 18th level.

Mythical Beast Amber — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your cursed energy is always electrifying your whole body, making your reactions instant. Your eyes gain marks of lightning around them, as a sign of your energy always refilling you. You can now add your Cursed Energy modifier to your initiative rolls.

Mythical Beast Amber — Innate Technique (6th level)

When you reach 6th level, your control over your technique has improved to the point where you are able to separate the charges of electricity. After hitting a creature with Electric Energy you can mark the creature with a positive charge for 1 minute. You can have a number of charges on a target equal to twice your Cursed Energy Modifier. As an action you can expend charges to release a lightning bolt at one creature within 60 ft which heads straight for the accumulated charges dealing a number of d12s equal to the number of charges.
Starting at 11th level, this gains the limb-removing effect of the Limb Damage Table.

Mythical Beast Amber — Innate Technique (11th level)

Once you reach 11th level, you have finally learned your innate technique and its terrible cost. Once activated, this technique reconstructs the user's flesh in order to manifest phenomena that can be created by electricity, which is converted from the user's cursed energy. However, since the technique causes the user's body to surpass the limits of a human, it can only be used once before their body collapses following the technique's conclusion. As an action for 8 cursed energy, your body will start getting filled with electric cursed energy, making you constantly grow in power for a short period of time. You start at Stage 1 and every 5 rounds, you gain the next stage. As a bonus action, you can spend CE to expedite your transformation by 1 round per 2 CE. You can deactivate your form at any moment as a bonus action, however, depending on what stage you reached, your deactivation causes more backlash. After your fifth round in Stage 5, it instantly ends, making you die instantly:

Stage Benefits Deactivation Side Effects
Stage 1 +2 to Str, Dex, and Con ignoring limits. Immunity to lightning. +20 feet of movement. You must make a DC:10 Constitution saving throw, on a failure you will gain 1 level of exhaustion. On a success, you suffer nothing.
Stage 2 +3 to Str, Dex, and Con ignoring limits. Immunity to lightning. +40 feet of movement. +1 Attack. You must make a DC:15 Constitution saving throw, on a failure you will gain 2 levels of exhaustion. On a success, you suffer only 1.
Stage 3 +4 to Str, Dex, and Con ignoring limits. Immunity to lightning. +60 feet of movement. +1 Attack, +1 BA. You must make a DC:20 Constitution saving throw, on a failure you will gain 3 levels of exhaustion. On a success, you suffer only 2.
Stage 4 +5 to Str, Dex, and Con ignoring limits. Immunity to lightning. +80 feet of movement. +1 Action, +1 BA. You must make a DC:25 Constitution saving throw, on a failure you will gain 4 levels of exhaustion. On a success, you suffer only 3.
Stage 5 +6 to Str, Dex, and Con ignoring limits. Immunity to lightning. +100 feet of movement. +2 Action, +1 BA. You must make a DC:30 Constitution saving throw, on a failure you will gain 6 levels of exhaustion. On a success, you suffer only 5.

Your body will slowly alter itself while in this form, gaining the following as it progresses.
Cursed Claw(Stage 1). When you activate this form, your cursed energy will surround your hands and increase your overall attack power. Your unarmed strikes now deal one of the following damage types: Thunder, Lightning, Fire, Force, or Cold, and will deal one additional damage dice + 1d10 Lightning damage.
Loud Blast(Stage 2). When you reach Stage 2 in this form, your mouth will start to get covered with cursed energy, allowing you to emit loud energy blasts from your mouth. As an action, make a cursed energy attack roll against a creature within 30 ft. On a hit it deals 6d10 lightning damage. Hit or miss, all creatures within 15 ft of the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they take 6d6 thunder damage and are deafened until the beginning of your next turn. On a success, they take half as much.
Lightning Armor(Stage 3). When you reach Stage 3 in this form, your torso and legs will start to get filled with cursed energy. You will gain damage reduction equal to your Cursed Energy modifier.
X-Ray Vision(Stage 4). When you reach Stage 4 in this form, your head is completely filled with cursed energy, even granting you new eyes. You will gain 120 feet of truesight, and will also be able to see all the features one creature of your choice has as a bonus action.
Cursed Beam(Stage 5). When you reach Stage 5 in this form, your very cursed energy has been improved. As an action for 6 cursed energy, you launch a huge cursed energy beam in a 30-foot line, forcing every creature in that line to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 10d10 force damage and are blinded until the beginning of your next turn. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not blinded. You can spend up to 4 additional cursed energy, with each one adding 1d10 force damage and a +1 to its DC.

Mythical Beast Amber — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level, you have honed your control over your energy into a domain expansion. Starting at initiative 20, all creatures in your domain gains 3 positive charges without a charge limit.

New Shadow Style — Innate Technique (1st level)

You are born with no innate technique, but in order to make up you learn a special secret. A domain for the weak.

Beginning at 1st level, you gain the Simple Domain feat with the following benefits:

  • You can activate Simple Domain for free a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each long rest

  • You can activate Simple Domain as a bonus action

  • The area of Simple Domain can be up to 15 feet instead of 10

New Shadow Style — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have learned the fastest technique of the New Shadow Style. As an action for 3 CE while wielding a melee weapon, you can make one attack roll with advantage against a number of targets equal to your proficiency bonus within half of your movement speed and reach. You end your turn behind the farthest target without provoking opportunity attacks.

New Shadow Style — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, you enter a crouched stance. When a creature willingly moves in or out of your Simple Domain you can make a weapon attack against them. On a hit, you can choose to either spend CE up to your cursed energy modifier to deal an additional damage die for each CE spent, or you can gain a bonus to your AC and saving throws equal to the CE spent until the beginning of your next turn. You can only make this attack once per round per creature, meaning you can use it once against each creature.

New Shadow Style — Innate Technique (11th level)

Starting at 11th level, you can spend 1 cursed energy as a bonus action to imbue your weapon with your simple domain for 1 minute. You can add your Cursed Energy modifier to attack and damage rolls of melee weapon attacks or unarmed strikes. When you use this technique, you ignore any penalties for using a broken weapon.

New Shadow Style — Innate Technique (18th level)

Finally, at 18th level, you manage to reach the peak of New Shadow Style. Your Simple Domain gains the following benefits:

  • Simple Domain costs no cursed energy.

  • You can freely move and maintain Simple Domain.

  • The range of any of New Shadow Style techniques can be increased to up to 60 feet as a bonus action until the end of your turn

When you expand the range of your Simple Domain over a creature, you can make two weapon attacks against a single creature as a free action (regardless of range). You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each long rest.

Pachinko Fever — Innate Technique (1st level)

Did you know most gamblers stop before their big hit? Let's hope you don’t, as failing may mean death, but your luck has got you.

Beginning at 1st level, luck has sided with you, and you can use it against your foes. Once per long rest you can force one of your rolls to be critical (cannot roll for black flash).

Pachinko Fever — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 3rd level, you gain access to your domain expansion. Once per long rest you can expand your domain for free bringing you and all creatures of your choice within 175 feet to a demiplane that resembles a subway station as music starts playing. This domain is Non-Lethal with Anti-Domain Clash as listed in Non-Lethal Domains and cannot be reacted to unless the opposing user has a domain with at least 400 refinement points and has higher refinement than you.
You gain three types of Pachinko attacks that can be used as a bonus action, each attack increases the "expectation" by a percentage.

  • Green Balls. As a bonus action for 1 cursed energy, make a ranged cursed energy attack roll against a target within 30ft. It deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage on a hit and raises expectations by 10%.

  • Red Rod. As a bonus action for 3 cursed energy, make a melee cursed energy attack roll against a target. It deals 1d8 bludgeoning damage on a hit and raises expectations by 25%.

  • Golden Train Door Attack. As a bonus action for 4 cursed energy, make a melee or ranged cursed energy attack roll against a target within 30ft. On a hit, the target takes 1d12 bludgeoning damage and must make a Strength saving throw or be restrained until the end of your turn. This attack increases expectations by 50%.

You can consume the expectation at any time by using your bonus action to place your bet and causing an event to take place.
There are 4 possible types of events. To know which event will happen, you must roll a d20 + your expectation bonus. You get a +1 bonus for every 10% Expectation, to a maximum of +19 at 190%.

Number Event Type Description Jackpot Dice
1-9 Transport Gate Will they make it in? d12
10-14 Seat Argument Can she get the seat? d10
15-18 Tight Squeeze Can they get to the bathroom? d8
19-20 Last Train Can they catch the train? d6

Once an event starts, roll a d10 to see how many rounds the event lasts. If your domain ends, you immediately roll.

Number Rolled Multiplier
1-12 3
13-15 4
16-17 5
18-19 10
20 Rainbow

At the end of the event, you must roll a d20 (also adding expectation to this roll, +1 per 10%) to find out if you win the multiplier bonus or the rare "Rainbow" bonus. You can reroll all jackpot dice an amount of times equal to your multiplier, if "Rainbow" lands you have an automatic jackpot in that event. At the end of the event you will roll 3dX, with the value of the dice defined by the event. If 3 of the same numbers land, you win a jackpot. When you hit a jackpot the domain expansion is undone without the effects of Technique Burnout, your cursed energy becomes infinite, and you become immortal.
You gain the following benefits for 4 Rounds:

  • Your cursed energy completely refuels at the beginning of your turn.

  • You will receive the effects of Reverse Cursed Technique as if you have spent cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier at the beginning of your turns. In addition, you cannot go below 1 hit point and heal all injuries.

  • You regain one free use of Idle Death Gamble.

After spending all of your uses, you can use your domain again for 20 Cursed Energy.

description.value:
Pachinko Fever — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, after activating Idle Death Gamble and getting a Jackpot, you gain advantage when making your Event roll or Multiplier roll within your next domain.

Pachinko Fever — Innate Technique (11th level)

When you achieve the 11th level, after entering your jackpot, you start gathering fever points. Once per round when you are lowered to one hit point, you gain a fever point. You can have a number of them up to your proficiency bonus and unused fever points disappear at the end of combat. You can use one of your fever points to gain one of the following effects:

  • You can choose to land a critical hit (cannot black flash)

  • You gain an additional action

  • Add a +10 to a saving throw or ability check

Pachinko Fever — Innate Technique (18th level)

At 18th level , you now roll 3d20 when deciding your multiplier, and can choose which roll you want. Your reverse cursed technique makes you regain hit points as if you had spent a number of cursed energy equal to twice your Cursed Energy modifier, and you can use Reverse Cursed Technique as a free action while you have the jackpot bonus.
In addition, your jackpot duration is now a number of minutes equal to your Cursed Energy modifier (min of 1).

Pain Killer — Innate Technique (1st level)

While you cannot heal, you can stop injuries from getting worse.

Starting at 1st level, you can use your technique to stop injuries from getting worse. As a bonus action for 1 CE, you can make a symbol with your hand and touch a creature within 5 feet. If a creature is taking damage over time, you cause that damage to stop and the creature gains temporary hit points equal to your CE modifier + your level for 1 hour. This does not stop new effects from affecting the target. You also gain proficiency in Medicine.

description.value:
Pain Killer — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you can use Pain Killer on all willing creatures within 5 feet as a free action on your turn, spending 1 CE for each creature. This increases to 10 feet at 6th level and 15 feet at 11th level.

Pain Killer — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, when you use Pain Killer on a creature, they also lose one condition of your choice and if they are making death saves they are immediately stabilized. You now gain Expertise in Medicine.

Pain Killer — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, when a creature that you can see within 10 feet would take damage, as a reaction for 4 CE you can halve the damage.

Pain Killer — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you and all creatures of your choice fall under the effects of Pain Killer. You can use Analgesic as a free action for no cursed energy without a reaction, but only once per damage instance.

Paralyzing Gaze — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique allows you to paralyze others with a mere gaze.

Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to slow anyone you have within line of sight. As an action for 2 CE, you force a creature within 60 ft to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, their movement speed is halved and their attack rolls and AC are reduced by your Cursed Energy modifier until the beginning of your next turn. At the beginning of your next turn, you can spend 1 CE as a bonus action to maintain the technique. If you lose line of sight, the technique automatically ends.
Using your technique places extreme strain on your eyes. Your eyes have a number of hit points equal to 1/3rd of your maximum hit points(rounded up). Your eyes take 1 damage for every 1 a creature rolls above your save DC to resist your technique. Your eyes regain 1 hit point at the beginning of your turn, unless at 0 hit points. Any HP you regain affects your eyes as well. If your eyes reach 0 hit points, you are blinded and they can’t regain hit points unless by Reverse Cursed Technique or long rest.

Paralyzing Gaze — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have trained your peripheral vision to lock down multiple targets at once. When you use Immobilizing Eyes, you instead spend a Full-Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) to affect a number of creatures up to your Cursed Energy modifier, spending 1 CE for every creature beyond the first. You must spend 1 CE for each targeted creature to maintain your technique against them.

Paralyzing Gaze — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, whenever a target you can see makes an attack roll while within 60 ft or the attack is against you, you can spend 2 CE to force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they have disadvantage on the attack roll. A creature under the effects of Immobilizing Eyes automatically fails this saving throw.

Paralyzing Gaze — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to completely paralyze targets with your technique. Your eyes' hit points increase to 1/2 of your maximum hit points (rounded up). As an action for 6 cursed energy, you force a creature you can see within 120 ft to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are paralyzed and have their AC reduced by your Cursed Energy modifier. You must maintain concentration on the technique as if concentrating on a spell and at the beginning of your turn by spending 2 CE as a bonus action. However, focusing your power to this extent leaves you vulnerable. The target can make an Strength (Athletics) check at the end of their turn. On a success, your eyes take 2 damage for every 1 they rolled above your Cursed Energy save DC (damage to your eyes does not force a concentration check). A creature paralyzed by this technique cannot be physically moved, even remaining suspended in the air.

Paralyzing Gaze — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, three creatures of your choice within the domain suffer the effects of Immobilizing Eyes. At each initiative 20, you can change the target for your domain’s guaranteed hit effect. The domain takes the appearance of several mirrors that reflect your gaze from every angle, making line of sight impossible to break within the domain.

Prayer Song — Innate Technique (1st level)

Through dance and the beat engraved in your body, you gain the ability to buff yourself and debuff your opponent even without a domain.

Starting at 1st level, as a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy you can start catching the beat of a fight. The effects depend on how long it has been active and end if you are stunned, paralyzed, grappled, restrained, or knocked prone.

Turns Active Effect
1 Your AC and Dex Saves increase by +2
2 Your Enemies AC decreases by -2
3 You can add your Cursed Energy modifier to your attack rolls
4 Your opponent has disadvantage on attacks and you have advantage on saving throws
5 Your attacks deal additional damage equal to your proficiency

Prayer Song — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you give certain blows more of a kick. Once per turn for 1 CE, you deal 2 additional damage dice on an attack.

Prayer Song — Innate Technique (6th level)

Beginning at 6th level, you learn to make openings and stop your enemy’s tempo. As a reaction while dancing, you force a creature you see to reroll an attack roll, damage roll, or saving throw.

Prayer Song — Innate Technique (11th level)

Starting at 11th level, your abilities improve and find new heights. Only you gain these benefits against a creature you are fighting.

Turns Active Effect
1 Your AC and Dex Saves increase by +3
2 Your Enemies AC decreases by -3
3 You can add your Cursed Energy modifier to your attack and damage rolls
4 Your opponent has disadvantage on attacks and you have advantage on saving throws
5 Your attacks deal additional damage equal to your proficiency
6 Your opponent has their damage decreased by your proficiency
7 You gain an extra attack when you take the attack action
8 Your opponent's AC drops by a total of 5, and gains a -5 to saves.
9 Your critical range increases by 2.
10 Your opponent can only take an action, bonus action, or movement on their turn.

Prayer Song — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you gain the pinnacle of your technique. When inside your domain, you always count as if ten turns passed with Prayer activated.

Projection Sorcery — Innate Technique (1st level)

You were born with one of the praised techniques of the Zenin Clan, turning animation into reality.

Beginning at 1st level, you learn the projection technique, which gives you the possibility to divide 1 second into 24 frames which allows you to move faster. As a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy, your walking speed increases by 10 feet and you will gain an additional attack on your Attack Action. However, this cursed technique is not perfect as you cannot change your movement course once you start, so when your turn ends you pick the spot you want to move to, due to your speed it will be impossible to change course. If you do not end your turn in that space, your speed becomes 0 until the end of your next turn. You must spend 1 Cursed Energy at the beginning of your turns to keep this cursed technique active.

effects.name: Projection (toggle)
effects.description: Conditional bonus: enable this effect while its condition applies.

description.value:
Projection Sorcery — Innate Technique (3rd level)

When you get to 3rd level, for every consecutive turn with Projection active your movement speed increases by 10 feet. If you charge in a straight line building momentum you can deal an additional d6 for every 10 feet on your next melee attack.

effects.name: Acceleration (toggle)
effects.description: Conditional bonus: enable this effect while its condition applies.

description.value:
Projection Sorcery — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, you have learned how to affect creatures with the 24 FPS rule, making them become stuck in one frame of animation. While your cursed technique is active, when you hit an unarmed strike on a creature you can choose to deal no damage by spending 2 Cursed Energy, forcing the creature to make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure they will be stuck in one frame of animation, making them stunned until the beginning of your next turn. The creature loses its stunned condition early if it is hit by an attack which will automatically count as a critical. This critical ignores damage resistance and treats damage immunity as resistance.

Projection Sorcery — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, due to your advanced studies, you can now reach a higher speed level than any sorcerer ever could. While your cursed technique is active, you will gain the following benefits:

  • You gain +30 feet to your walking speed.

  • You gain +20 feet to your walking speed at the beginning of your turns.

  • You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws.

  • Your Dexterity score increases by +2 ignoring your maximum.

description.value:
Projection Sorcery — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level, you reach the pinnacle of Projection Sorcery. All creatures in your domain take 8d10 Necrotic damage when they move or take any type of action, since their cells don't follow the 24fps rule.

description.value:
Puppet Manipulation — Innate Technique (1st level)

You gain the ability to control puppets with your Cursed Energy,

Beginning at 1st level, you gain mastery over puppets. You gain proficiency in Tinkerer’s Tools, and over a long rest, you can create a puppet. As an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can imbue a Puppet, this puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits. You can summon as many puppets as you want. Any Puppets can only take an action if you use your bonus action to command it. It cannot use its reaction unless you use your reaction to command it to. The puppet can use bonus actions on its own. You can speak, hear, and see through any of your Puppets. In case you have more than one puppet at once, you need to control them at the same time. Whenever you gain a puppet, use the following for its sheet:

  • Your Puppet's starting Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity scores are 15, 14, and 13 + bonus points to distribute between them equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. The Puppet's mental scores equal to your own.

  • Your Puppet is a Medium Construct.

  • Your Puppet has its hit dice based on what material they are made from, if the case is wood is a d4, stone is a d6, iron is a d8, and modern metal hit die is a d10. Your puppet has the same amount of hit die as you.

  • Your Puppet has a 30 feet walking speed.

  • You control your Puppet from afar, watching its every move and controlling it to dodge attacks. Your Puppet's AC is equal to 10 + its Dexterity modifier.

  • Your Puppet uses your proficiency bonus and is immune to the charmed and poisoned condition.

  • Your Puppet gains proficiency in Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity saving throws.

  • Your Puppet deals 1d6 + Strength modifier in bludgeoning with unarmed strikes.

Trait Level Traits
Minor Enhanced Defense. Your Puppet's defenses were increased so that he could fare better against attacks. Its armor class is increased to 10 + its Dexterity modifier + your Cursed Energy modifier. Basic Weapon Training. Your puppet gains proficiency in simple weapons and shields. Faster Movement. Your puppet is fast and cannot be caught so easily. Your puppet gains a +10 ft bonus to its walking speed. Stronger Strikes. Your puppet gains better natural weapons, changing its unarmed strikes to deal 1d8 piercing, slashing, or bludgeoning damage, based on the new weapons. Your puppet's unarmed strikes will now overcome resistance. Your puppet can use dexterity or strength for these attacks. Heightened Senses. Your puppet is always sharp and is a perfect detection machine. He will gain 60 ft. of Darkvision and will gain advantage in perception checks against living things.
Lesser Improved Reach. Your puppet's arms elongate, its agility heightens, or it grows tentacles, and your puppet's melee reach increases by 5 feet. Advanced Weapon Training. Your puppet gains proficiency in martial weapons. Hardened Shell. Your puppet's shell is thicker, scalier, or harder than normal. Your Puppet will gain resistance against non-magical Bludgeoning, Slashing, or Piercing damage. Deflect Missiles. Your puppet has developed quick reaction skills, and can now defend itself from high-speed ranged projectiles. Using its reaction, your puppet can reduce an incoming projectile damage by 1d12 + your level. Minor Magic. Your puppet learns to cast one cantrip, and one 1st level spell, both from the wizard spell list(no healing). It uses its Cursed Energy modifier for the spellcasting ability and must take a long rest before casting the 1st-level spell again.
Advanced Colossus. Your puppet's body increases in size in all dimensions, changing its size to Large. This functions like the enlarge/reduce spell. Flying Behemoth. Your puppet gains wings, jets, or some other way of flight, giving it flight speed equal to its movement speed. Major Magic. Your puppet learns to cast one cantrip, one 1st level spell, one 2nd level spell, and one 3rd level spell, all from the wizard spell list (no healing). It uses its Cursed Energy modifier for the spellcasting ability, casts the three spells at 3rd level, and can only use each spell once before they must take a long rest to use it again. Armor Training. Your puppet gains proficiency in all armor. High Caliber Striker. Your puppet's natural weapons improve further, growing stronger, harder, or sharper. Your puppet's unarmed strikes now deal 2d8 piercing, slashing, or bludgeoning damage. Your puppet can use dexterity or strength for these attacks.
Absolute Mech. Your puppet's body increases in size in all dimensions, changing its size to Gargantuan. However, to control this puppet you must be inside it, but you are under full cover, and the puppet's Hit dice is a d12. Energy Cannon. As an action, you generate a large amount of cursed energy in the palm of one hand, blasting it at a target for 6 CE. Make a ranged attack with Dex + Proficiency + 3, This attack deals 20d6 Necrotic damage and recharges on a 5-6 d6. Energy Volley. As an action, you create 5 orbs made of cursed energy and blast them. Choose targets for each orb and make a ranged Cursed Energy attack with a +3 for 4 CE. On a hit, this attack Deals 6d6 Necrotic damage. Recharges on a 5-6 d6.

Puppet Manipulation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have begun to slowly improve your puppet. You will gain a Lesser Puppet and can summon it as an action for 3 Cursed Energy, though this Puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits and 2 Lesser Traits.

Puppet Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, through the constant use of your puppet, you have begun to fix some of its downfalls. You will gain an Advanced Puppet and can summon it as an action for 6 Cursed Energy, though this Puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits, 2 Lesser Traits, and 2 Advanced Traits.

Puppet Manipulation — Innate Technique (11th level)

When you reach 11th level, you have perfected your puppet for its desired uses. You will gain a Master Puppet and can summon it as an action for 10 Cursed Energy, though this Puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits, 2 Lesser Traits, 2 Advanced Traits, and 2 Absolute Traits.

Puppet Manipulation — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level, you reach the peak of your technique. Your manipulation is now no longer limited to puppets. You can now manipulate the creatures in your domain like puppets in a puppet show.
At initiative 20, all creatures take an action of your choice that does not cost cursed energy.

Ratio — Innate Technique (1st level)

You were born with a powerful technique that creates a weak spot on a 7:3 ratio

Beginning at 1st level, you gain a +1 to critical range. Additionally, you roll an additional damage dice on a critical hit.

Ratio — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Once you reach 3rd level, you have learned your technique that creates weak spots in enemies. Whenever you hit an attack, you can spend 1 cursed energy to roll a d10. If you roll a 3 or 7 the attack becomes a critical hit.
You now roll 2 additional damage dice on a critical hit.

Ratio — Innate Technique (6th level)

When you reach 6th level, as an action for 4 Cursed Energy, you make an attack to destroy the ground around you in a 30 ft circle, applying your critical hit to the rubble. The area becomes difficult terrain and every creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take your attack’s damage + 3d10 bludgeoning damage. On a success, they take half as much damage.
You now roll 3 additional damage dice on a critical hit.

Ratio — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have become more lethal and precise with your Ratio. When you use Ratio, you now roll 2d10 instead of one and you can spend additional CE up to your Cursed Energy modifier to roll an additional d10 per CE spent. You roll 4 additional damage dice on a critical hit.

Ratio — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level, you have honed your skill with your technique to a fine edge. In your domain, all of your attacks count as critical hits and you deal an additional 5 damage dice on a critical hit.

description.value:
Regalia — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your very soul has become a cursed tool that has been sealed within. You have the ability to manifest it using cursed energy.

Starting at 1st level, you can manifest your Regalia as an action for 2 CE for a number of hours equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. Your Regalia takes the form of a simple or martial melee weapon of your choice, such as Dagger or a Shortsword. You are proficient with the weapon and gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls using your Regalia. Once per turn on a hit you can spend 1 CE to deal an additional 1d8 necrotic damage. This becomes 2d8 at 3rd level, 3d8 at 6th level, 4d8 at 11th level and 6d8 at 18th level.
Your Regalia disappears if it is more than 30 feet away from you and cannot be wielded by other creatures.

Regalia — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have learned greater control over your Regalia. For 1 CE, you can make one of your attacks with your Regalia into a cutting wave of cursed energy. This creates a 5 ft wide 30 ft long line. Creatures in range must make a Dexterity save, taking the damage of your regalia in necrotic damage on a failed save.

Regalia — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, the seal further loosens, granting you more abilities.
Your Regalia now has a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls. This increases to a +3 bonus at 11th level and +4 at 18th level.
Your Regalia now has a pool of hit points equal to 5 times your level. When you take damage, you can spend 1 cursed energy as a reaction to damage to cause that damage to instead target the regalia’s pool.

If this hit point pool is reduced to 0 hit points, you take any remaining damage and your regalia breaks and must be resummoned. When broken, your regalia can be resummoned a number of times equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. Otherwise, you cannot summon your regalia until you complete a long rest.

Regalia — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, your control over your Soul Regalia has loosened nearly all of the seal. Your regalia is now a special grade cursed tool. Work with your GM to decide what its ability is.
As an action, you can spend 10 cursed energy to cause your regalia to hover for 1 minute. Your regalia has an AC equal to 12 + your cursed energy modifier + your proficiency bonus and hit points equal to its pool while hovering. The regalia is destroyed if reduced to 0 hit points. You gain the following actions:

  • As an action you can command the weapon to move up to 100 feet and can make any attacks on your turn originate from the Regalia as if you were wielding it. You can use your cursed energy modifier for attack and damage rolls for these attacks.

  • As an action, you can cause your regalia to move in a 100 foot line attack, appearing at the end of the line if it is a melee weapon. All creatures within range must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking your regalia damage on a hit.

After the minute is up, the Soul Regalia moves 100 ft towards you, attempting to return. If unable to, it falls to the ground.

Regalia — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, the seal is completely removed as you have perfected a domain expansion that you put your soul into. The domain is filled with numerous types of Lesser Regalia in the form of random weapons. At initiative 20, the Lesser Regalia will attack any enemies within the domain, dealing 8d10 necrotic damage. Additionally, you can use Soul Bound Treasure as an action without spending any cursed energy. In your domain it has immunity to all damage and you can use one of its actions once per turn as a free action.

Retrograde — Innate Technique (1st level)

The act of regression is the basis of your technique.

Beginning at 1st level, when you make an attack roll or saving throw against an effect that you can see or are targeted by an attack roll, you can spend 1 cursed energy as a reaction to reverse time a few seconds, allowing you to reattempt a failed roll or make the attack reroll.
At 3rd level, this feature also grants you a +2 bonus to the second attempt this feature grants you. This increases to +3 at 6th level, +4 at 11th level, and +5 at 18th level. Also at 3rd level, you can use this feature on a creature within 30 ft of you that you can see for an additional 2 CE. Other creatures do not gain the bonus to rolls.

Retrograde — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you can spend 3 cursed energy as a bonus action. You physically regress to the previous point you were standing at the start of your turn, tracing the path you moved. This completely reverses your movement and actions even defying the laws of physics, such as jumping up backwards or running on nothing if the ground or platform was removed. Any opportunity attacks for this reversed movement are made at disadvantage.

At 6th level, you can spend 3 additional cursed energy to continue regression to the point you started your previous turn.

If your movement is blocked, you can force your way through. If your path is blocked by a creature, they must make a Dexterity save or take your proficiency bonus in d8s of bludgeoning damage and are pushed to a different space out of your path if their size is Large or smaller (your choice). If your path is blocked by a structure or object that is not fixed in place, you can make a Cursed Energy check to move it (DC 10 + 3 for every size category above Medium). On a success, you move it out of the way. Otherwise you take 5 bludgeoning damage and the structure or object takes 10 times your proficiency bonus in bludgeoning damage. If this destroys the object, you continue moving, otherwise you stop moving.

Retrograde — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you can use Reversion without using your reaction a number of times equal your proficiency bonus each round. Additionally, when you use Reversion you can spend an additional 3 CE to instead roll at advantage.

Retrograde — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, rather than reversing events you have learned to use a conceptual curse that inverts causality to rewrite the flow of events so your attack always lands first. After an attack or damaging effect made by a creature within 30 ft damages you, you can spend 8 CE as a reaction. Time is then rewound to before the attack is made or the effect happens.
You can immediately make one attack against the creature that ignores range and is guaranteed to hit by reversing causality, causing the triggering action to be wasted.

Retrograde — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, choose one creature within your domain. The first thing that creature does on their turn (Eg. using movement, taking an action, etc) is automatically reversed back to their original point and the movement or action is wasted. At initiative 20, you can target a different creature by switching the effects of your domain to that creature.
Additionally, all creatures of your choice are under the base effects of Reversion. When you use Reversion on your own attack rolls, they are guaranteed to hit.

Rockstar — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can amplify sound and launch it as a blast of energy.

Starting at 1st level, you gain proficiency in Performance and one instrument of your choice. While holding an instrument you are proficient in, you can spend 1 CE as an action to play it and launch a Sound Blast at a target within 30 feet. Make a ranged Cursed Energy attack roll, on a hit you deal 2d10 thunder damage and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed back 10 feet. This technique's damage increases to 3d10 at 6th level, 4d10 at 11th level, and 6d10 at 18th level.

Rockstar — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, when you use your action to launch a Sound Blast, you can launch up to two Sound Blasts, spending 1 Cursed Energy for each. At 11th level you can make up to three Sound Blast attacks as part of your action.

Rockstar — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to apply your Sound Blast to an area. As an action for 5 cursed energy, you can launch a Sound Wave in a 15 feet cone. All creatures within range must make a Constitution saving throw or take your Sound Blast damage + additional d10s equal to your proficiency bonus and be pushed back 20 feet and deafened until the end of their next turn on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful save.

The range of your Sound Blast now increases to 60 feet. The range of your Sound Wave increases to 30 feet at 11th level.

Rockstar — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you can spend 8 cursed energy to start a solo. For the next minute, your attacks deal an additional 2d10 thunder damage and if a creature fails its saving throw against your technique it gains disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check.
You can also spend additional cursed energy up to half your proficiency bonus to deal an additional 2d10 thunder per CE spent. A hostile creature that ends its turn within 15 feet of you during your solo takes thunder damage equal to your CE modifier + your proficiency bonus.

Rockstar — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain take your Sound Amplification damage and are deafened for 1 minute.

Rot — Innate Technique (1st level)

Utilize your toxic dark blood to devastating effectiveness.

Starting at 1st level, you possess toxic blood. You gain resistance to poison and acid damage and have advantage on saving throws against the poisoned condition. When you have less than your hit point maximum, you can cause your unarmed strikes or melee weapon attacks to deal an additional 1d8 acid damage once per turn. This increases to 2d8 at 3rd level, 3d8 at 6th level, and 4d8 at 11th level.

Once as part of a long rest, you can spend $100 and hit points up to your proficiency bonus to fill a Blood Bag with your own blood. This Blood Bag counts as a source of hit points for your Rot features. A Blood Bag lasts 5 days outside of refrigeration before it goes bad. You can have a number of Blood Bags equal to your Constitution modifier at once.

Rot — Innate Technique (1st level)

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your blood in a manner fit for battle. When you use a Rot technique or feature, you can ignore the HP cost if you have an alternate source of blood. You gain four techniques and two additional techniques at 6th and 11th level:

  • Blood Spit. As an action for 1 CE and 2 HP, you force a creature within 15 feet to make a Constitution save or take 2d6 acid damage and be blinded until the end of their turn on a fail.

  • Rot Burst. Once per turn on a hit with a melee attack, you can spend 1 CE and 1 HP to deal an additional 2d8 acid damage.

  • Rotten Blood Beam. As an action for 3 CE and 4 HP, you can make a ranged cursed energy attack against a target within 30 feet. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 piercing and 2d10 acid damage and must make a Constitution saving throw or have their movement reduced by 10 feet until the end of their next turn.

  • Corrosive Wave. As an action for 3 CE and 5 HP, you launch waves of your rotten blood in a 15 feet cone. Creatures in range must make a Constitution saving throw or take 5d8 acid damage or half as much damage on a success.

  • Blood Shield. As a reaction, you spend CE up to your modifier and twice that amount in HP. For each CE spent, the Blood Shield gains 10 hit points, which absorbs the damage and you take remaining damage. If this reduces a melee attack to 0, the attacker must make a Constitution save or take 2d8 acid damage.

  • Homing Blood Missile. As an action for 4 CE and 5 HP you can shoot a seeking blood missile at a target within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes 5d10 + your CE modifier in acid damage. You can reroll the attack roll using your bonus action or reaction.

  • Blood Soak. As a bonus action for 3 CE and 3 HP, you can coat your limbs in your blood. For the next minute, your walking speed increases by 10 ft and your unarmed strikes deal 2d6 + CE modifier acid damage on a hit.

  • Crimson Spear. As an action for 2 CE and 3 HP, you form your blood into a spear. Make a ranged cursed energy attack roll with a range of 30/90 feet. On a hit the target takes 1d6 piercing and 2d10 + CE modifier acid damage.

  • Crimson Rain: As an action for 2 CE and 3 HP, you pick a point within 60 ft. Creatures within 15 feet must make a Dexterity Saving throw taking 1d10 piercing and 2d10 acid damage on failed save or half as much on a success.

Rot — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level you have learned to use your blood infectiously. As a bonus action for 3 Cursed Energy, you can cause all creatures that have taken damage from your technique in the last minute to form black floral patterns on their body as they have been infected with your blood.
At the beginning of your turn, they take your Rotten Blood damage. This lasts for 1 minute unless you spend 3 cursed energy to continue the effect or end it as a free action.
At 6th level, creatures also gain the poisoned condition for the duration and Decay also reduces a creature’s hit point maximum. A creature’s maximum hit points return to normal after a long rest.

Rot — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have proved your mastery over your technique. Your technique now ignores resistance to acid damage and a creature that fails a saving throw against your technique is poisoned for 1 minute and can make a Constitution save at the end of their turn to end the effect on themselves.
You gain immunity to poison and acid damage as well as the poisoned condition. At 18th level, your technique treats immunity to acid damage as resistance.

Rot — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you learn to condense your blood into wings resembling veins as a bonus action for 8 CE, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

  • Your movement is quadrupled

  • You gain a flying speed equal to half your movement

  • You gain advantage on Dexterity saving throws

  • You can replace an attack on your turn with a Rot Technique or one line of blood attack.

  • As a free action on your turn, you can unleash lines of blood.

These lines of blood take the shape of three ranged Cursed Energy attacks against a target within 60 feet. Each attack deals 4d10 + your CE modifier acid or necrotic damage. You can also replace an attack on your turn with a line of blood attack. While using Wing King, you cannot use Decay.

Schrift X — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can create cursed seals that allow for permeation and your eyes are also cursed with a seal due to this technique.

Starting at 1st level, you have a cursed mark somewhere on your body that molds your cursed energy automatically. When you make a ranged weapon attack, you can choose to use your Cursed Energy modifier for the attack or damage rolls. When you make a ranged attack, you can spend 1 ce to ignore cover by phasing through a solid object. You can only pierce through 5 feet of one object. This increases to two objects at 3rd, three at 6th, and four at 11th.

Schrift X — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your technique has evolved and a cursed seal forms on your eye, providing near perfect accuracy. As an action for 3 cursed energy, you automatically hit a creature within range with a ranged weapon attack without rolling and deal an additional 2d6 necrotic damage. This increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 5d6 at 11th level, and 7d6 at 18th level.
You can use this technique only if you haven't moved this turn, and after you use it, your speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

Schrift X — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to apply your cursed seals onto others, allowing for even more accurate and deadly shots. When you use a mark, any previous marks you have active ends.

  • Critical Mark: As a bonus action for 3 CE, you can mark a target of your choice within 30 feet for 1 minute. If you hit the marked target with an attack, your next attack against the target is made at advantage. On a hit, the attack deals critical damage and the mark ends.

  • Multi-Mark: As a bonus action for 3 CE, you can mark a number of targets up to your CE modifier within 30 feet for 1 minute. As an action, you can make a ranged attack and activate the marks, causing the attack to split and attack each marked target within range of your attack. You make a ranged weapon or cursed energy attack roll against each creature, dealing your normal damage on a hit and the mark ends.

Schrift X — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to use your cursed seal to cause yourself to phase instead of your attacks. As a bonus action for 6 cursed energy, you release the cursed seal over your eye to activate your technique. You gain immunity to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing and resistance to all other damage other than psychic for 1 minute and must maintain concentration.

While Intangibility is active, you cannot use your innate technique features. only allowing for normal attack actions. You can end the technique at any point as a free action to close your left eye.

Schrift X — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level you have achieved the pinnacle of your innate technique. Within your domain, all your attacks benefit from Piercing Schrift and are a guaranteed hit. At initiative 20 every creature within your domain is given a Cursed Mark of your choice.
