Seance — Innate Technique (1st level)

You summon the dead into yourself or a willing vessel.

Starting at 1st level, you have a very powerful and dangerous technique, and you begin to learn its basics. As a Full Turn Action you can spend 2 CE per information you Seance. You can target yourself or another willing creature within 15 ft for the seance of a dead humanoid with a CR or level no more than 1 higher than your level. You must have a small body part such as a finger of the deceased humanoid that you or the willing participant must consume.

You or the target of the seance must spend 1 cursed energy at the beginning of the target’s turns while the technique is active to maintain its form, with the technique ending once the cursed energy runs out. You cannot use an alternate source of cursed energy, even with a binding vow. You lose access to your Innate Technique features while affected by this technique.

Physical Information. The target of the seance gains the appearance, racial traits, features, proficiencies, and Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores of the deceased humanoid and temporary hit points equal to your proficiency.

Soul Information. The target gains access to the full information the body has including all memories and one of their Cursed Technique or Innate Technique features. While it is useful, this is also a dangerous method of utilizing this technique. At the beginning of their turns, the target must make a Charisma saving throw against the deceased person (DC 8 + their proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier). On a failure, the dead humanoid takes control until the target’s cursed energy runs out.

Seance — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have increased the potency of your seance.
When channeling Physical Information, the target gains temporary hit points equal to your level + your proficiency.
When channeling Soul Information, the target gains access to two Cursed Technique or Innate Technique features of your choice and does not lose access to their own Innate Technique features. The target cannot use Innate Technique features from different techniques at the same time.

Seance — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned how to create a prolonged ritual to make your technique more powerful. When you use your technique, you can start a ritual instead of immediately shapeshifting. You must make a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) every turn for 1 minute to perform this ritual while maintaining concentration. If you lose concentration, the ritual stops and you must start over. After you have finished the ritual, you or a willing creature within 30 ft can transform into the dead humanoid if the CR or level is equal to or lower than your level + your proficiency bonus.

Seance — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, when you complete Ritual of Resurrection you can spend an additional 5 cursed energy to cause the target of the Seance to gain one of the following benefits.

Physical Information Overload. The target gains the hit points of the dead humanoid as temporary hit points if channeling Physical Information.

Soul Information Overload. The target gains access to all the dead humanoid’s Cursed Technique and Innate Technique features if channeling Soul Information. You cannot use Domain Expansion this way and can only use the minimum required cursed energy for innate technique features. The target also cannot use the dead humanoid’s innate technique and its own at the same time.

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20 you can choose a willing creature to gain the benefits of Seance.
Although you must have the body part of the dead humanoid being called, you don’t need to consume it as long as you are holding it. Within your domain, you no longer have to spend cursed energy to maintain the seance and automatically succeed against a creature’s soul information. All innate technique features gained through Seance in your domain are imbued with your domain’s guaranteed hit. Seances caused by your domain end when your domain disappears.

Shadow Killer — Innate Technique (1st level)

You possess the eerie ability to kill without touching.

Starting at 1st level, you can control your shadow and cast Minor Illusion through it in a 5 ft range around yourself.
You can also strike a creature through their shadow. When you make an attack roll, you can spend 1 cursed energy to target a creature’s shadow that exists within their space. If the creature is unaware of your technique, you automatically hit as they don’t guard their shadow. The target takes your attack in necrotic damage and you deal additional damage equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. This increases to twice your Cursed Energy modifier at 3rd level, thrice at 6th level, and four times at 11th level.

If your attack roll is higher than the creature’s passive Perception, they are unaware of how they were damaged. If your attack roll is lower, then they see you attack their shadow and become aware of your technique. A creature that is aware of your technique can make a Dexterity saving throw to try and avoid your assault on their shadow. On a failure, you automatically hit. On a success, you roll against their AC. You cannot use this technique if you cannot see the target’s shadow.

Shadow Killer — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your ability to affect creatures through their shadows has improved. When you make a weapon attack, you can spend 3 cursed energy to target a creature’s shadow. On a hit, instead of dealing damage you release your grip on the weapon used to make the attack, leaving it to pin the target’s shadow in place. The creature is grappled and restrained and is unable to move or be moved until the weapon is removed. The weapon can be removed as an attack.

Shadow Killer — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to become one with the shadows, gaining darkvision out to 200 ft and can see through magical darkness within this range. You can spend 2 CE to cast Pass Without Trace. When you take the Hide action in dim light or darkness, you become invisible until you attack, use a technique, or enter an area of bright light.

Shadow Killer — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have mastered the art of elimination without being seen. You can use Shadow Strike as a free action once per turn for 1 CE. This special attack deals critical damage on a hit if the target has not taken a turn in combat or is surprised. You cannot roll for a black flash in this way.

Shadow Killer — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. Within your domain, the shadows of all creatures are always visible to you and stretch towards you so they are always at your feet and able to be targeted. At initiative 20, three creatures of your choice suffer the full effect of Shadow Strike.

Shrine — Innate Technique (1st level)

Dissect and fillet, preparing your oven. Simple things like that are your cursed technique.

Starting at 1st level, you learn the basics of your technique, which is cutting. When you take the attack action, you can spend Cursed Energy up to your proficiency bonus to replace your attack with Dismantle. Make a melee or ranged CE attack with a range of 120/250 ft. On a hit you deal 1d12 slashing damage per CE spent. The base damage becomes 2d12 at 6th level as long as you spend 1 CE. This increases to 3d12 at 11th and 4d12 at 18th level.
If you gain the Extra Attack feature, you can replace attacks with Dismantle, but must spend Cursed Energy for each attack. If a target cannot see Dismantle, you gain advantage on Dismantle attacks against that creature (passive Perception lower than your CE save DC cannot see Dismantle). You gain +1 bonus to Dismantle’s critical range at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

Shrine — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you learn how to cleave living targets in one fell swoop. As an action for up to 10 Cursed Energy, you choose a target within 5 feet. Make a melee Cursed Energy attack. On a hit, the target takes a number of d10s equal to your proficiency bonus + Cursed Energy spent in slashing damage and must make a Constitution save.
On a failure, further uses against the same creature ignores resistances as Cleave adjusts to the target’s toughness.

Shrine — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you can utter an incantation to create an arrow of fire. As an action, you can spend Cursed Energy up to twice your proficiency bonus, choosing a point within 150/600 feet of you. Each creature within 15 ft of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw, which is made at advantage if the creature is more than 150 feet away. On a failed save, they take a d12 of fire damage for each cursed energy spent. On a successful save, they take half as much damage.

Shrine — Innate Technique (11th level)

Beginning at 11th level, your body has adjusted to better handle your cursed technique. You can now use Dismantle as a bonus action or reaction (one attack each). Additionally, when using Cleave against a creature that has failed its save, it treats immunity as resistance. If using the maximum of 10 cursed energy on Cleave, you can target a limb from the limb damage table.

Shrine — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At last at 18th level, you have reached the pinnacle of your innate technique, letting you finally expand your domain.
At initiative 20, the domain cuts everything, causing targets to suffer the effects of Cleave and Dismantle. Cleave targets creatures within cursed energy and Dismantle targets anything in the domain including objects. Cleave and Dismantle are treated as if the maximum amount of Cursed Energy was used.

Full turn: Action + Bonus Action + Movement

description.value:
Sky Manipulation — Innate Technique (1st level)

A great technique allowing you to grab space and wield it to your command.

Beginning at 1st level, your innate technique manifests, making you able to manipulate the sky around you. As a reaction to an attack roll, you can spend 1 Cursed Energy to add +4 to your AC by distorting the sky until the start of your next turn. If it makes a ranged attack miss, you can make a cursed energy attack roll against the attacker, redirecting the attack and dealing the attack's damage and effects on a hit. If it makes a melee weapon attack miss, it will render the limb used in the attack stuck and unusable until the beginning of the creature's next turn. If you have taken the dodge action, you can use this reaction on allies within 5 feet.

Sky Manipulation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Once you reach 3rd level, you have become better at manipulating the space around you. As a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can cover part of your body with a part of the sky, making those parts covered invisible for 1 hour. While you have this armor equipped, your AC is 11 + Your Cursed Energy modifier + your proficiency bonus. You also gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed while under the effects of Sky Armor.

Sky Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

When you reach 6th level, your manipulation has become so refined even techniques pass through you. You can now use your reaction against cursed energy attack rolls, and you can use this reaction for 3 Cursed Energy to redirect a cone or line saving throw, redirecting the attack if you pass the saving throw, making it not affect you or other creatures in the area.

Sky Manipulation — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have created an extension technique to your sky manipulation, literally breaking the sky as if it were ice. As an action for 5 Cursed Energy, you can force every creature in a 30 feet line to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they will take a number of d10s equal to twice your Cursed Energy modifier in force damage and be knocked prone, on a success they take half as much damage and are not prone. While you are flying, all creatures make their save at disadvantage.

Sky Manipulation — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level, you have learned the most powerful technique of your arsenal. Your domain is a beautiful blue sky full of clouds, with a shining sun illuminating everything. All hostile creatures inside the domain are considered falling unless they have flying speed. Once the domain is over, they take the maximum amount of falling damage.

Full turn: Action + Bonus Action + Movement

Solo Forbidden Zone — Innate Technique (1st level)

Starting at 1st level, through chanting, and dancing you bring out the maximum potential of those around you. As an action for 1 CE, you create a 30 ft sphere for up to 1 minute. Allies within the zone gain advantage on all rolls. You must use your bonus action on your turn to maintain the Zone.

Solo Forbidden Zone — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you gain better control over your Zone, allowing you to focus it on a single person. As an action for 3 CE you target a willing creature within 60 feet. That creature is under the effects of your Forbidden Zone for 1 minute or until you lose concentration.

Solo Forbidden Zone — Innate Technique (6th level)

Beginning at 6th level, you can spend CE up to your CE modifier + your proficiency as a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) to make a 50 ft sphere centered on yourself into a Ritual Zone for 1 minute while concentrating. You must maintain your Zone using your bonus action on your turn and cannot move more than 10 feet. You can choose to not allow hostile creatures to enter or leave your Zone, forcing them to make a Wisdom save, becoming unable to enter or leave for 1 minute on a failure. Allies gain your Zone’s normal effects and benefits depending on how much CE you spent to activate this technique:

  • Allies deal an additional 5 damage with techniques for each CE spent.

  • Allies gain temporary cursed energy equal to CE spent (doesn’t affect yourself).

  • If allies can spend additional cursed energy on a feature, they can spend additional cursed energy up to your CE modifier (min of 1).

Solo Forbidden Zone — Innate Technique (11th level)

Starting at 11th level, after setting up your Zone, you can maximize an ally's output. Once per turn when a creature uses a cursed technique that deals damage while within your zone, you can spend 5 CE to cause them to deal maximum damage instead of rolling.

Solo Forbidden Zone — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you reach the peak of your technique, allowing you to open your domain. All allies in your domain are under your Ritual Zone as if you had spent the maximum CE and their techniques become sure hits, as if they were the ones who cast the domain.

Star Dictator — Innate Technique (1st level)

The path of your shikigami constitutes the domain.

Starting at 1st level, you can spend cursed energy up to your proficiency bonus as an action. For every cursed energy, you summon a minor shikigami in an unoccupied space within 5 ft of you. As a bonus action, you can command any shikigami created with your technique, otherwise they take the dodge action. As an action, you can share senses with one of your minor shikigami. While sharing senses with your shikigami, you are blinded and deafened. You can only have up to your proficiency bonus in shikigami at a time.

Star Dictator — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Starting at 3rd level, you have learned to form a pseudo-domain that follows the path of your shikigami. As a bonus action, you command any number of your minor shikigami to create your domain. They spend their action taking the dash action to orbit around a point, forming a circle within 5 ft of the center. On each of your turns, you can use your bonus action to increase the radius of the domain by 5 ft or command more shikigami to join the domain orbit.
The maximum range and damage of the domain depends on the number of shikigami making up the domain. A creature within the domain other than you must make a Dexterity saving throw at the end of your turn. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d6 slashing damage per orbiting shikigami or half as much on a success.
The maximum radius of the domain is 5 ft x the number of orbiting shikigami. If one of the orbiting shikigami is killed, the range and damage decreases. If all of your shikigami stop orbiting the domain path, the pseudo-domain ends.

Star Dictator — Innate Technique (6th level)

Starting at 6th level, you have learned how to keep your pseudo-domain active without sacrificing offensive power. Your pseudo-domain now deals 1d8 slashing damage per shikigami creating the domain. You gain the ability to summon your major star shikigami. You can summon your major star shikigami as an action for 6 CE and can command it as a bonus action, otherwise it takes the dodge action. You can only have one major star shikigami active at a time. Once your major star shikigami is killed, you cannot summon it again for 1 hour.

As a Full-Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement), you can command the major star shikigami to begin forming a special pseudo-domain. Once it has completed a full orbit, the special domain allows your Minor Star Shikigami to move freely within the domain while still maintaining the range and damage of your pseudo-domain. This special domain still follows the same maximum for range and damage, now scaling with the number of Minor Star Shikigami within the domain.

Star Dictator — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned mass summoning. You can now maintain a number of Minor Star Shikigami equal to three times your proficiency bonus and can have two Major Star Shikigami active at once.
Additionally, the damage of your pseudo-domain increases to 1d10 slashing damage per shikigami orbiting and ignores immunity and resistance to slashing damage. The radius of your pseudo-domain increases to 10 ft x the number of orbiting shikigami.

Star Dictator — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain take 1d12 slashing damage for every star shikigami you have summoned within your domain.

Full turn: Action + Bonus Action + Movement

description.value:
Star Rage — Innate Technique (1st level)

Beginning at 1st level, you have learned the most fundamental technique for a star rage user, the virtual mass increase. As a bonus action for an amount of Cursed Energy up to twice your Cursed Energy modifier, you gain a mass increase for each CE spent for a number of rounds equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. You gain the following benefits depending on your added mass:

  • Stronger Martial Arts. Your Unarmed Strike die increases by one tier per two mass increases. (1->d4->d6->d8->d10->d12->2d8)

  • Mass Impact. At one mass increase, whenever you roll a critical with an unarmed strike the target must make a Constitution saving throw or be knocked prone. At two mass increases, a creature within 5 ft of the target must make a Constitution save or take half of the same damage. At three mass increases, if the target fails the Constitution saving throw upon a critical, it will also have its speed halved until the beginning of your next turn. At four mass increases their speed will be reduced to 0 if they fail.

  • Increased Damage. You gain a +1 to unarmed strikes damage rolls per mass increase.

  • Grappler. At one mass increase, you count as one size larger. You count as one size larger per 2 mass increases up to Gargantuan.

You can only activate this technique again after the full duration has passed.

Star Rage — Innate Technique (3rd level)

When you reach 3rd level, you have honed your skills with your technique, learning how to make it last longer. Virtual Mass Increase now lasts for a number of rounds equal to twice your Cursed Energy modifier. This becomes three times at 11th level and four at 18th.

Star Rage — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, you have gained experience in refining your technique and can now add three times your Cursed Energy modifier.
Increased Strength. When you spend at least 5 CE on virtual mass, you gain advantage on Strength and Constitution checks and saving throws and +1 to the rolls for each further mass improvement.

Star Rage — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have refined and optimized your technique. You can now add up to four times your Cursed Energy modifier to your virtual mass and use your technique with melee weapon attacks.
Critical Power. Your critical range increases by 1 for every four mass increases and you deal maximum damage to objects and structures.
Quick Activation. You have learned how to instantly activate your technique. You can now activate Star Rage as a free action.

Star Rage — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, 18th at level, you have learned to expand your domain. All in your domain are crushed by ground-shaking mass as every 1 ft cost 4 ft of movement. At initiative 20, all hostile creatures in your domain are knocked prone and take 8d8 force damage as they experience crushing mass. A creature must make a Strength (Athletics) check against your Cursed Energy save DC at the beginning of their turn to stand up and again at the end of their turn to remain standing.

Starlight Symphony — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can create and mold a shining cursed fog.

Starting at 1st level, you can spend Cursed Energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier as an action. You create 10 feet of fog around yourself for each cursed energy. The fog lasts for 1 minute, spreads around corners, heavily obscures the area and you choose if the fog follows you or not as part of the action to create it. Creatures within your fog have disadvantage on Perception and Investigation checks and cannot detect cursed energy.

At 6th level, you can use your reaction to give advantage or disadvantage to a roll made by a creature within your cursed fog and can spend up to twice your Cursed Energy modifier when creating your cursed fog. You can spend up to thrice your Cursed Energy modifier at 11th level.

Starlight Symphony — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you can summon a fox shikigami as an action for 2 cursed energy. The shikigami lasts for 24 hours or until dismissed as a free action. Your fox shikigami act on your turn and you can command all fox shikigami as a bonus action.
You can have a number of shikigami summoned equal to your proficiency bonus and always know if your shikigami has died.

Starlight Symphony — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to become the fog itself. As an action for 3 Cursed Energy you transform yourself or one of your fox shikigami into a misty cloud for up to 1 hour while concentrating. While in this form, your only method of moving is a fly speed of 30 feet. You can enter and occupy the space of another creature. While occupying the space of another creature, you can force them to make a Constitution saving throw, taking Xd8 equal to your Cursed Energy modifier in cold damage on a failed save as they choke on your fog.

You have resistance to nonmagical damage and advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws. You can pass through small holes, narrow openings, and even mere cracks, though you treat liquids as though they were solid surfaces. You can’t fall and remain hovering in the air even when stunned or otherwise incapacitated.
While in the form of a misty cloud, you can’t manipulate objects, and any objects you were carrying or holding can’t be dropped, used, or otherwise interacted with. You can spend an additional 3 cursed energy to also become invisible for the duration.

activation.condition: You can spend an additional 3 cursed energy to also become invisible for the duration.

description.value:
Starlight Symphony — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, as a full turn action for 8 cursed energy you can summon Inari in an unoccupied space within 10 feet. Inari disappears after 1 minute and uses your proficiency bonus. You can command Inari and your fox shikigami as an action on your turn. Inari is considered one of your fox shikigami for any of your features other than Living Fog.

Starlight Symphony — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have completed your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. Your domain is an expansive field of fog with two towering spirits at the north and south. All creatures other than you are completely blinded by the cursed fog within your domain and suffer the effects of your Cursed Fog. At initiative 20, all creatures take 5d10 cold damage as they struggle to breathe in the cursed fog.

Straw Doll Technique — Innate Technique (1st level)

Beginning at 1st level, due to your experience with your technique, you will start with 1 Hammer, 24 nails, and 1 straw doll. As an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you strike 2 nails by hitting them with your hammer. Make two melee or ranged cursed energy attack rolls with a range of 20/60 feet. On a hit, each nail deals 1d6 + your CE modifier piercing damage. You can also spend 2 additional Cursed Energy to make 2 additional attacks in this way.
At 6th level, you have become rather cheap with your nails, making sure to always recover as many as possible from the battlefield. As a bonus action while touching a creature that has taken damage from Nail Projectile, you can make a DC 10 Dexterity check. On a success, you regain the nail.

Straw Doll Technique — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have learned the true use of your technique. As a reaction while within 5 feet of a target that just took slashing or piercing damage, you make a Sleight of Hand check against the target’s AC. The damage dealt determines the size of the piece. You can mix a body part from a creature into the straw doll for three cursed energy. While within 200 feet, you can use your action to damage the original creature through your straw doll, depending on the body part. At 18th level, your attacks using Resonance lowers the target’s maximum health.

Damage Required Effect Damage Dice
<10% of Enemy HP Blood Or Hairs Minor Body Part: Target gains disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of their next turn. (Proficiency bonus)d6
25%> of Enemy HP Teeth, Skin, Bones Medium Body Part: The Target loses their reactions until the end of their next turn. (CE modifier + proficiency bonus)d8
50%> of Enemy HP Limbs Major Body Parts: The creature has to make a Constitution saving throw; on failure, black spikes erupt from the creature’s body stunning them for 1 minute. They can repeat the save at the end of their turn, ending the effect on success. (2×Cursed Energy modifier + proficiency bonus)d10

Straw Doll Technique — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, you learn a new way to damage your enemies. When you launch a Nail Projectile and hit a creature or as a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can stick a nail into an object. If hitting a creature, the initial attack deals no damage. As a bonus action or as a reaction to a creature coming within 5 feet of the nail, you can create cursed explosions. Creatures within 10 feet of the nails must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 1d8 necrotic damage for each nail, taking half as much damage on a success. You can spend additional Cursed Energy when you drive the nail, increasing the damage by 1d8 for every additional Cursed Energy spent.

Straw Doll Technique — Innate Technique (11th level)

When you reach 11th level, you’ve discovered a way to utilize Resonance. Instead of using the straw doll to target the creature, you can instead use the creature’s very body in place of it to dramatically increase its effectiveness. As an action for 6 cursed energy, you make an attack roll against a creature under one of the following conditions: incapacitated, restrained, stunned, petrified, or paralyzed. On a hit, the creature is knocked prone and struck by resonance with its body being used in place of the straw doll with the following effect:

Effect Damage Dice
For 1 minute, every time they try to use a feature that costs CE, they must make a Charisma saving throw at disadvantage. On a failure, the technique fails to activate and the cursed energy is wasted. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turns, still at disadvantage, ending the effect on a success. (2×CE modifier + your proficiency bonus)d12

Straw Doll Technique — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level, you have honed your technique. At initiative 20, you unleash a full-power Improved Resonance, on all creatures inside the domain.

Technique Extermination — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique bestows its user with the gift of angelic power, capable of smiting villains and hampering enemy’s cursed techniques.

Beginning at 1st level, you have gained use of the essentials of your technique. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you can target a creature you can see within 30 ft as a trumpet of light appears and a beam of light falls from the sky. The target must succeed a Charisma save, if the creature fails it takes 2d12 radiant damage and loses the ability to use Cursed Energy for 1 minute. On a success, they take half as much damage and don't have their cursed energy features negated. They can repeat the saving throw at the beginning of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

Technique Extermination — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your technique makes you feel like a divine being made to help others, you are a true angel. As a bonus action for 1 cursed energy, you can gain flying speed equal to half your walking speed for 1 minute, as wings of light emerge from your back and a halo stands on top of your head. While you have the wings active, you can freely move through barriers such as curtains without breaking them. You can also pass through walls and barriers that were cast with CE equal to or lower than your proficiency bonus. When said minute ends, you can spend another 1 more cursed energy to keep your fly speed for another minute. This fly speed increases to your walking speed at 11th level.
In addition, due to your holy nature you gain resistance to radiant damage.

Technique Extermination — Innate Technique (6th level)

Once you reach 6th level, your Extinguishment increases to 5d12 radiant damage and cursed tools of the targeted creature are also suppressed for the duration.

Technique Extermination — Innate Technique (11th level)

When you reach the 11th level, you have created an extension to your technique, one so powerful that you can burn your opponents as a radiant light falls upon them. As an action for 10 cursed energy, you summon a trumpet of light in your hands, blowing into it as you choose a point within 200 feet of you. A beam of light strikes down in a 10-foot radius circle centered on the point you choose, every creature in said area other than you has to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they take 10d12 radiant damage and suffer the effects of Extinguishment for 2 minutes. On a success, they take half as much damage. Undead, cursed spirits and creatures of evil alignment make this saving throw at disadvantage.
You can also use this technique to destroy barriers and cursed objects. As an action for 6 cursed energy, you can summon a trumpet of light and blow into it, making a beam of light targeting a cursed object, cursed item, cursed tool, magic item, or any kind of barrier created by cursed energy or magic within 30 feet. Make a cursed energy attack roll against the cursed energy or spell save DC. On a hit you destroy the target, neutralizing barriers and power of cursed objects.
If you use this technique with Maximum Output, its beam of light increases to a 30-foot circle and ignores features that reduce damage.

Technique Extermination — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, 18th level, your technique is honed to the finest of edges. At Initiative 20 all creatures suffer the full effects of Jacob’s Ladder.

Teleportation — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can teleport yourself and others to marked locations while not being viewed.

Beginning at 1st level, your technique allows you to teleport to destinations you have marked. As a bonus action for 1 cursed energy, you can mark a person, location, or object which you can touch. You can have up to twice your CE modifier in marks at once and your marks remain for up to 12 hours. You can remove any of your marks at will.
As an action for 2 cursed energy, while not being viewed, you and any willing creatures within 5ft of you that are also not being viewed teleport up to 500 feet to a mark of your choice.

Teleportation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have improved your technique. The range of your teleport now increases to (your CE modifier + your proficiency bonus + your level) x 100 feet, and you can now teleport as a reaction to an attack or saving throw as long as you have a way to cause yourself to disappear from view (such as covering yourself with a sheet).

Teleportation — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, with great training, you have reached the pinnacle of your teleport. As an action for 8 cursed energy you cast Teleport. You can only go to marks and you always go to the exact mark you want to go to, regardless of how far away from you they are. You are now able to teleport others while you do not leave. You can now choose to only teleport other creatures when using any teleport feature.
Additionally, you can attempt to teleport an unwilling creature within 5 ft. They must make a Cursed Energy saving throw. If they fail, they are teleported to one of your marks.
Additionally, your markings now last for a week instead of 12 hours.

Teleportation — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to mark things more efficiently. You can now mark as a free action instead of a bonus action and your amount of markings is increased to 3 times your CE modifier. You can spend 5 CE to make a mark last indefinitely unless destroyed.

Teleportation — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. All space within your domain is treated as being marked by you. At initiative 20, you can change the locations of a number of creatures up to twice your CE modifier, teleporting them anywhere within your domain, regardless of whether they can be seen. Additionally, you can teleport a creature as a reaction.

description.value:
Ten Shadows — Innate Technique (1st level)

You have the Zenin Clan’s praised technique, said to rival the six eyes.

Beginning at 1st level, you have the prized technique of the Zenin clan, the ten shadows earned to summon Shikigami from the shadows. As an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can summon up to 2 Divine Dogs(1 CE per dog) within 10 ft of you. Your Divine Dogs last for 1 hour, until they are reduced to 0 hit points or you dismiss any summoned shikigami as a bonus action while within line of sight. As a reaction to seeing your shikigami reduced to 0 hit points, you can unsummon them and cannot summon them again until you finish a long rest.
Your shikigami cannot use actions on their own. You must spend a bonus action to command your shikigami or can spend an action to order them to do something more specific for longer, such as protect that creature, grab that, defend that area, etc. The number of Shikigami you can control at once is equal to half your level(rounded up).

Ten Shadows — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Once you reach the 3rd level, you have gained access to your other spirits, and you must face them in ritual combat alone to gain access to them. As an action, you can summon an untamed Shikigami within 30 ft of you without spending cursed energy. Any creature within 50 feet is considered participating in the ritual. An untamed shikigami will be berserk (attack the nearest creature), but if you have defeated the shikigami alone (not including your shikigami) and reduce it to 0 hit points, you can now summon the shikigami normally as an action for up to 1 hour and can dismiss them as a bonus action. You can summon a number of shikigami at a time equal to half your level rounded up (Divine Dogs and Rabbits each count as one entity).

Cursed Energy Shikigami
1 Cursed Energy Gama
2 Cursed Energy Nue
4 Cursed Energy Great Serpent
6 Cursed Energy Rabbit Escape
7 Cursed Energy Mourn Tiger
8 Cursed Energy Max Elephant
9 Cursed Energy Round Deer
10 Cursed Energy Piercing Ox
20 Cursed Energy Divine General Mahoraga

If reduced to 0 hit points during a trial with multiple participants, you do not make death saving throws until all participants are unconscious.

Ten Shadows — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Any shikigami reduced to 0 hit points dies and cannot be summoned again. A destroyed shikigami is eligible for Totality, with the exception of Rabbit Escape or Mahoraga.

If one of your shikigami is killed, during a short or long rest you can perform a 1-hour ritual to pass on the strength of one deceased shikigami to a different Non-Totality (other than Rabbit Escape or Mahoraga), granting it a permanent Totality form. When you make a Totality, they gain the following changes:

  • Their Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Wisdom, and Charisma scores become those of the creature who has the higher score. Then they gain a bonus to that ability score equal to the modifier of the creature with the smaller score.(Ex: Nue has 16 Strength while Divine Dog has 12, their Totality would have 17 Strength.) They also gain the higher AC of the shikigami used.

  • They receive the hit points of both creatures.

  • Their movement speed is added together.(2 with 30 would have 60)

  • They receive all features, traits, actions, bonus actions, reactions, legendary actions, skill, saving throw proficiencies, damage resistances, damage immunities and condition immunities from both creatures.

  • Their size can be either of the shikigami.

  • The CE cost becomes the higher shikigami + half of the lower shikigami’s cost.

  • Their CR equals the creature with a higher CR + half the CR of the creature with the smaller CR rounded up.(Ex: Nue's CR is 4, and Great Serpent's CR is 5, their totality's CR would be 7)

  • After calculating ability scores, the difference in the ability modifier of the original user of a damaging feature and the Totality is added to the amount of dice. For save effects damage, the score corresponding to the save is used.
    (Ex: Mourn Tiger has a +5 in Dexterity and Nue has a +3. Mourn Tiger’s Dexterity Score increases by +3, meaning a +1 bonus to Dexterity modifier so you add 1 additional dice to the Totality's attack to the damage dice that use Dexterity as the ability modifier, changing Mourn Tiger’s bite attack from a 1d10+5 into a 2d10+6.) This increase only applies to direct attack rolls and saving throws.

As an optional ruling, your DM can choose to ignore Totality, instead having all shikigami come back on a long rest, rather than being killed and eligible for Totality.

Ten Shadows — Innate Technique (6th level)

Starting at 6th level, you've learned to make use of your ability to manipulate shadows, allowing you to form an extra dimensional space to hide your things and even manipulate the shadows of others.
Shadow Storage. You can store objects in an extra-dimensional space within your shadow. You can physically place something into your shadow, costing no cursed energy. However you must spend 1 cursed energy to interact with an object in this space, potentially removing it. Everything in your shadow counts for your carrying capacity. Additionally, you can trap creatures within your shadow. As a bonus action for 2 ce, you can force a creature to make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your CE save DC. This check is made at Disadvantage if they are in complete darkness or inside a veil, and automatically fail within your domain. On a failure they are trapped inside your shadow, counting for carrying capacity. They can hold their breath for a number of minutes equal to their Constitution modifier (min of 1) before suffocating. They can make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw at the end of their turns, freeing themselves on a success and appearing prone in an unoccupied space within 5 ft.

Ten Shadows — Innate Technique (11th level)

When you reach 11th level, you can combine your shikigami into different forms. As an action, you can temporarily combine two of your living shikigami into a single type, granting the base shikigami an alteration feature from the other. You spend half the CE cost of the base shikigami to summon up to your proficiency bonus in altered shikigami at once, spending CE for each.
An altered shikigami has half the hit points of the base shikigami and you can reduce its size category by 1 to reduce the CE cost by 1. When reduced to 0 hit points, it does not affect the shikigami used in its creation and is not eligible for Totality. You cannot summon any unaltered shikigami while altered shikigami are summoned. If the base shikigami or alteration shikigami’s CR is 4 or higher, you can only create up to two altered shikigami with them at a time.

Shikigami Alteration
Divine Dogs Pack Tactics feature
Gama Standing Leap feature
Great Serpent +15 hit points and Constrict attack
Nue 60 feet fly speed
Round Deer Antler attack
Piercing Ox Unrelenting Charge feature
Mourn Tiger Mourning Roar feature
Max Elephant +50 hit points

Ten Shadows — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally, at 18th level you have learned how to expand your domain. Your domain is a huge shadow barrier, filling your surroundings with overwhelming darkness. Any hostile creatures that end their turn within your domain must make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or become restrained and sink. They can make a Strength (Athletics) check at the beginning of their turn to escape. The area is difficult terrain for creatures of your choice, and you are under the effects of Freedom of Movement within the domain.
Shadow Clones. While inside the domain, as a bonus action you can spend cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to create a number of clones of yourself equal to the CE spent. The clones have all your features and stats, but not weapons or hit points and cannot use Cursed Energy. Their hit points are equal to your Cursed Energy modifier and become a shadow puddle once reduced to 0 hit points. You can use your reaction to switch places with a clone when you are hit, making the clone take the hit instead.
Shikigami Clones. Your domain allows you to summon copies of your shikigami to overwhelm your opponents. Whenever you summon a shikigami, you can instead spend cursed energy equal to the shikigami's cost(treat its price as if you were outside your domain) to summon a perfect copy of the shikigami. You can spend CE to make a number of shikigami clones up to your Cursed Energy modifier on the same turn. You cannot create copies of Mahoraga with this feature.
In addition, your normal Shikigami won't cost you Cursed Energy within your domain.

Tool Manipulation — Innate Technique (1st level)

You can control tools you imbue with cursed energy.

Beginning at 1st level, you can spend CE up to your CE modifier as a bonus action to imbue a tool you are holding with cursed energy. This imbuement lasts an hour for each cursed energy spent and gains the following benefits:

  • You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls using this tool or a +1 bonus to AC if the tool is armor or used defensively

  • The damage die increases by 1 tier and again at 6th and 11th level (D4<D6<D8<D10<2d6<2d8)

Tool Manipulation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, when you imbue a tool, you can spend an additional 2 CE to create a Floating Tool. You can command a Floating Tool as an action to hover up to 35 feet in any direction and make a melee attack using your CE modifier. The Floating Tool deals its normal weapon damage or 1d4 bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing if it is an improvised weapon. You can only have one floating tool at a time and it falls to the ground if it is more than 120 ft from you.

A Floating Tool has AC equal to your CE save DC and hit points equal to 5 x your proficiency bonus + 10 for each grade above 4th if it is a cursed tool. A Floating Tool reduced to 0 HP is destroyed unless it is a cursed tool, in which case it loses the benefits of Floating Tool. You can spend 2 CE as a bonus action to return the effect of Floating Tool to the cursed tool by touching it.

Tool Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level you have learned to use tools offensively. As an action for 3 CE, you can create a blast of wind from an imbued tool you are holding. Or from a Floating Tool within 60 ft for 1 additional CE.
This creates a 10 feet wide, 60 feet long line. Creatures within range must make a Strength saving throw, taking 3d10 bludgeoning damage and pushed back 10 feet on a failed save or half as much on a success.
At 11th level, your Wind Scythe now deals 6d10 bludgeoning damage and a creature that fails their save is pushed back 20 feet and knocked prone.

Tool Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

Additionally, your specialty grants you the following Tool Improvements.

Tool Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

  • The cost to create a Floating Tool becomes 1 CE

  • When you command a Floating Tool, they can move up to 40 feet

  • You gain a flying speed of 60 feet by mounting a Floating Tool

  • You can have 2 Floating Tools active at the same time, commanding both as part of the same action.

As a reaction, you can cause one of your imbued tools to protect you. It grants you a bonus to AC or reduces damage depending on its size. If the tool has a bonus to AC or damage rolls, it is included in the AC and reduction respectively.

Tool Manipulation — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have mastered your respective style, granting you the following:

Floating Tool Mastery. You can command two Floating Tools using your bonus action or one Floating Tool as a free action on your turn. You and other creatures also gain advantage on Dexterity saves while riding a Floating Tool.

Combat Tool Mastery. Your mastery over imbued tools allows you to manipulate the flow of combat with exceptional precision. When you use Combat Tool Improvement, the AC bonus it grants increases by 1, and the damage reduction provided increases by one additional die. In addition, you gain one extra reaction each round that can only be used to activate Combat Tool Improvement.

When your or a creature you can see makes an attack using your imbued tool, you can use your reaction to grant that attack roll advantage.

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level you have learned to manifest your domain. All weapon attacks made by creatures other than you become a guaranteed miss as you can manipulate all tools within your domain, causing them to come to life and obey your commands.
At initiative 20, you choose one of your imbued tools to gain the benefits of Floating Tool and have all Floating Tools move 60 ft and attack a creature within range or have all creatures suffer the effects of Wind Scythe. You can control a number of Floating Tools equal to your CE modifier (min of 2) within your domain.

Triple Core — Innate Technique (1st level)

3 cores, 1 body, you have different forms with separate powers.

Starting at 1st level, your cursed energy is gathered into a single core. As a bonus action, you can choose to enter a secondary form giving you access to a special ability for 1 minute. You gain one core option at this level:

  • Unblockable Blows: When you hit with a melee attack, you can spend 1 CE to ignore resistances. If the creature is not resistant, they are considered vulnerable.

  • Energy Blast: As an action you spend CE up to your CE modifier to launch a blast of cursed energy. You make a ranged cursed energy attack against a target within 80 feet dealing 2d6 necrotic damage for each CE.

  • Defensive Form. As a bonus action, you assume this form for 1 minute, buffing your defense. You gain a number of temporary hit points equal to twice your current cursed energy. You can spend 1 CE at the beginning of your turn to refresh the temporary hit points.

  • Divebomb. As part of the bonus action you take to enter this form, you spend CE up to your CE modifier. For the duration of this form, your speed increases by 10 ft per CE spent and you gain a +2 bonus to AC. You deal an additional 1d4 damage for every 15 ft you move in a straight line before hitting a target with a melee attack.

Triple Core — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you can choose two more core options. You can only have one core option active at a time.

Triple Core — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, you have learned to specialize in one of your forms, allowing it to become semi-permanent. Choose one of your core options you have access to and gain its upgraded option:

Unblockable Blows. Your strikes are imbued with unblockable power. Once per turn when you miss with a melee attack, you still deal damage equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier.
Energy Blast. Your cursed energy has become far more destructive. Once per turn when you deal damage with a ranged cursed energy attack, you add your Cursed Energy modifier to the damage roll. If you already add your modifier to the roll, you add it a second time.
Defensive Form. Your body passively reinforces itself with cursed energy. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by your Cursed Energy modifier + your proficiency bonus.
Divebomb. Your body has adapted to improve its swiftness. You can spend 1 ce to take the dash, disengage, or dodge action as a bonus action.

Your upgraded options are always active even when you haven’t entered a core form. Though you can not benefit from an upgraded option while in a different core option’s form. You can gain an additional upgraded option at 11th and 18th level.

Triple Core — Innate Technique (11th level)

Starting at 11th level, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can choose to lose access to one of your core forms for 1 week to return to half your maximum HP.

Triple Core — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you gain true understanding over your cores. When inside your domain, you are under the effect of all three cores.

Vengeful Spirit Manipulation — Innate Technique (1st level)

The Vengeful Cursed Spirit technique involves the use of the spirit of one you care about.

Beginning at 1st level, at some point in time, someone you cared about died. Unable to accept their death, you unconsciously cursed them and created a vengeful spirit of great power. Once per turn, you can call a part of the spirit to your aid. By spending 1 Cursed Energy, you manifest the spirit’s claw to make an additional melee attack as part of your Attack action. This claw attack deals 1d12 slashing damage. At 6th level, the number of attacks increases to two, and three 11th level. You cannot use this attack during manifestation.

activation.condition: Additional claw attack as part of Attack action, once per turn; 2 attacks at level 6, 3 at level 11. Unavailable during full manifestation.

description.value:
Vengeful Spirit Manipulation — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, your life is very stressful, being a sorcerer is filled with danger and trouble. When times of danger come, your Vengeful Spirit may forcefully manifest. When you take damage above your level + your Cursed Energy modifier, you must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you can handle the strain and don't let your spirit out. On a failure, your Vengeful Spirit manifests itself to protect you, going berserk (attacking the nearest creature to you). It acts on your turn, is charmed by you and cannot move more more than 200 feet from you. Once per round, as a free action you can make a DC 20 Persuasion check. On a success it will stop attacking and unmanifest. On a failure, it will keep attacking until there are no creatures within 200 feet. They will always focus on the last thing to damage you and then the closest creature to you. If killed, it respawns after finishing a long rest.
At 6th level, the DC for the Persuasion check becomes 15 and your Vengeful Spirit stays manifested for a number of rounds equal to your Cursed Energy modifier under your control before going berserk.
At 11th level, you have gained more control over your vengeful cursed spirit. You can now manifest your spirit as a bonus action for 1 minute, now obeying your verbal orders. You can summon the spirit a number of times equal to half your Cursed Energy modifier (rounded up), regaining expended uses on a long rest.

Vengeful Spirit Manipulation — Innate Technique (6th level)

When you reach 6th level, you begin to learn about your innate technique. As a bonus action, while your Vengeful Spirit is in the world, you can command it to make a claw attack against a creature within range. On a hit it can extract the creature's DNA with a claw attack. You can attempt to replicate it by spending 3 CE as an action to make an ability check using your Cursed Energy score. On a success you can copy one feature of the Cursed Technique you have seen that is of a level that you qualify for and fill prerequisites (such as RCT):
-Cursed Technique = User’s Cursed Energy save DC + 2
You cannot copy Domain Expansions or CR 5+ Summons with Mimicry.
When you copy a cursed technique, you can only spend the base cost the technique requires. No matter what you copy, you can only use the technique in its base form. For example, a maximum output hollow purple would only come as a hollow purple. You cannot use different copied techniques at the same time if they are from different innate techniques.
You can have a number of copied techniques features equal to your Cursed Energy Modifier and can use them a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus before they disappear and you must copy them again. If you have a limb or body part of the user, the number of times you can use the technique is doubled. When you copy more than your limit, you remove a copied feature to make space for another.
In addition, you automatically pass the Cursed Energy check if you have already copied the cursed technique before.

Vengeful Spirit Manipulation — Innate Technique (11th level)

Once you reach 11th level, the bond between the binding object and the Vengeful Spirit becomes stronger. Your Vengeful Spirit gains the following benefits:

  • Two of its ability scores will be increased by 2, and so will their maximum.

  • You will gain +2 to your CE score, including its maximum while your spirit is summoned.

  • Whenever it is summoned the Vengeful Spirit will gain temporary hit points equal to half your current hit points.

Vengeful Spirit Manipulation — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

Finally at 18th level, through many battles and copies, you have learned how to expand your domain. Inside this barrier, you are allowed to use all of the cursed techniques you currently have for no Cursed Energy. At initiative 20, you will also gain one additional action, which can only be used to activate a copied cursed technique, which affects all hostile creatures inside the barrier.

Voracity — Innate Technique (1st level)

You get stronger by eating.

Starting at 1st level, you are constantly filled with the hunger impulses that come with your technique. When you reduce a cursed spirit, shikigami, or cursed corpse to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to spend 3 cursed energy to devour its corpse. For 1 hour you gain a feature, action, movement, resistance, immunity, sense, AC, Ability Score or other statistic from the dead creature’s statblock such as Cursed Energy Affinity (Cannot take legendary actions, Cursed Energy or Domains). You can spend an additional 3 cursed energy to steal an additional ability and can steal a number of abilities from a single corpse up to your Cursed Energy modifier.
When you steal an ability that does not suit your body (such as fly speed), your body changes to fit the ability (eg. growing wings). For the duration, you count as the creature type your stolen abilities come from. If you have stolen abilities from multiple creatures, you count as the one you have the most abilities from. You can have stolen abilities equal to your Cursed Energy modifier active at once.
At 6th level, you can have stolen abilities from a number of creatures equal to your Cursed Energy modifier +2 active at once and last for 24 hours. You cannot use different innate techniques at once.

Voracity — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have learned to access previous abilities you have eaten. As a bonus action you can spend 4 cursed energy to gain an ability you have stolen in the past and can use it for 1 hour. This does not increase at 6th level.

Voracity — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, your stomach calls for satiation and gives you the means to feed it. The amount of cursed energy required for Hunger of the Accursed and Regurgitation decreases by 1 (minimum cost of 1).

Additionally, you have learned to use cursed energy to enhance the abilities of the devoured. You can use one of the following benefits once per turn when you use a stolen ability:
Efficiency. When you use an ability with a base cursed energy cost, the cost of the feature decreases by 1 (minimum cost of 1).
Output. When you use an ability that lets you spend up to a certain amount of cursed energy, you can increase that amount by 2.
Speed. When using stolen movement, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus to increase it by 5 ft per cursed energy spent.
Reinforcement. When using stolen AC and are hit by an attack roll, you can spend 1 CE to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack roll, potentially causing it to miss.
Instinct. When using a feature, you can spend 2 cursed energy to decrease its action cost by one (Full-Turn Action > Action > Bonus Action > Reaction).

Voracity — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level you have learned to draw the power of the devoured from your stomach and into your flesh. As an action you can transform into one of the creatures you have devoured, spending cursed energy equal to twice the Devoured’s CR (min of 1) or Level. Your statistics are replaced by the statblock of the chosen Devoured, but you retain your alignment, personality, mental scores, Cursed Energy and Hit Points.
You gain temporary hit points equal to the Hit Points of the Devoured. These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain when the technique ends. The technique ends early if you have no Temporary Hit Points from this technique left.

You are limited in the actions it can perform by the anatomy of your new form and can only use your cursed techniques if your new form is capable of forming hand signs and chanting. This form lasts for a number of minutes equal to your level + your cursed energy modifier. You cannot use or benefit from Regurgitation while using this feature.

At 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you can regurgitate a creature whose corpse you devoured into an unoccupied space within 5 ft of you. The creature is friendly to you and your allies and acts immediately after your turn, attacking all enemies within your domain whether you command it to or not. If the creature was sentient in life, it is barely sentient within your domain as a mere husk of its former self. All regurgitated creatures disappear once your domain ends.

████ and Light — Innate Technique (1st level)

Your technique allows you to form killing intent into bars of light.

At 1st level, you can form killing intent into light. You learn the Light cantrip. As a bonus action for 2 cursed energy, you mold killing intent into a bar of light in a free hand. This weapon lasts for 1 minute and counts as a simple melee weapon with which you are proficient. It deals 2d8 radiant damage on a hit and has the finesse, light, and thrown properties (range 20/60). Additionally, you can use your Cursed Energy modifier for attack and damage rolls using this weapon. If you drop the weapon or throw it, it dissipates and reappears in your hand.

████ and Light — Innate Technique (3rd level)

At 3rd level, you have learned two new ways to use your technique:

Rain of Light. As an action for 3 cursed energy, you manifest bars of light to devastate your enemies. In either a 15 ft cone or 10 ft radius around yourself, you force all creatures to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take 3d10 radiant damage and are restrained by bars of light piercing their body. A restrained creature can repeat the save at the end of their turn, escaping on a success. This damage increases to 5d10 at 6th level, 8d10 at 11th level, and 10d10 at 18th level. The range of the cone increases by 15 ft and the radius increases by 5 ft at 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

████ of Dawn. As an action for 2 cursed energy, any magical darkness within 30 feet of you is dispelled. Additionally, each hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes radiant damage equal to 2d10 + your CE modifier and is blinded until the end of their turn on a failed saving throw, and half as much damage and not being blinded on a successful save. A creature behind total cover is unaffected. This increases to 3d10 at 6th level, 5d10 at 11th level and 8d10 at 18th level.

When you hit a creature with a melee attack using your Light Construct, you can teleport 10 ft to an unoccupied space you can see as your body becomes a beam of light for a moment.

████ and Light — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to imbue your body with killing intent to momentarily give it the properties of light. As an action for 8 CE, you instantaneously move in a 5 ft wide, 120 feet long line. All creatures in that line must make a Constitution saving throw or take 18d10 radiant damage and be knocked prone on a failed save or take half as much damage and not be knocked prone on a successful save. However, this technique risks tearing your body apart. For every creature, object, or structure you move through, you must make a Constitution saving throw against your Cursed Energy save DC. On a failed save, you take 20 bludgeoning damage. If used at Maximum Output, objects and structures take maximum damage and creatures with a Constitution score lower than your CE score automatically fail the saving throw. At 18th level, the length of the line increases to 200 ft and becomes 300 ft at 20th level.

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

While within your domain, your movement speed doubles and all movement on your turn is considered an instantaneous teleport and cannot be reacted to as your every move is at light speed, causing your body to break down into light particles whenever you move. As an action on your turn, you can teleport anywhere within your domain. You can choose one creature within 5 ft of the point you start from or end up at. That creature takes 4d12 radiant damage.

████ and Light Reversal — requires Reverse Cursed Technique. Not added automatically.

Through studying reverse cursed energy, you have learned your reversal, allowing you to instead create constructs of darkness from your killing intent. You learn the Darkness spell and cast it as an action for 2 CE.

Creeps and Curses V.3.1

████ and Light Reversal — requires Reverse Cursed Technique. Not added automatically.

As a bonus action for 4 cursed energy, you mold killing intent into a bar of darkness in a free hand. This weapon lasts for 1 minute and counts as a simple melee weapon with which you are proficient. It deals 4d8 necrotic damage on a hit and has the finesse, light, and thrown properties (range 20/60). Additionally, you can use your Cursed Energy modifier for attack and damage rolls using this weapon. If you drop the weapon or throw it, it dissipates and reappears in your hand. On a hit with this weapon, a creature’s speed is halved until the end of their next turn. This does not stack.

Creeps and Curses V.3.1

████ and Light Reversal — requires Reverse Cursed Technique. Not added automatically.

As an action for 12 cursed energy, you create a dark vortex in your hands for up to 1 minute while you maintain concentration. All creatures within 60 ft must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, they take 6d10 necrotic damage and are pulled 10 ft closer. On a successful save, they take half as much damage and are not pulled. You maintain the vortex as an action on your turn, forcing all creatures within range to repeat the save. As a reaction to taking damage while maintaining the vortex, you can absorb the attack into the vortex, rolling your vortex damage and reducing the attack by that much. If this reduces the damage to 0, the attack or effect is nullified. If the damage is from a melee attack, the weapon is destroyed unless it is Grade 1 cursed tool or higher. If used at Maximum Output, a creature that is pulled within 5 ft or is within 5 ft and fails their save, they treat this damage as a Limb Removing Effect. The damage of this technique increases to 10d10 at 6th level, 14d10 at 11th level, and 18d10 at 18th level.

Vairocana — Innate Technique (1st level)

Harmony and Chaos, the infinite universe that makes up all of creation.

At 1st level, you possess the ability to connect to all things that exist. As an action for 3 cursed energy, you can cast the Locate Creature spell without any components. The range increases to 1 mile at 6th level, 5 miles ft at 11th level and 30 miles at 18th level. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you can cast Speak with Animals or Tongues. At 6th level, you can extend the benefits of Tongues to a number of additional creatures equal to your CE modifier that are within range when you cast it.

Creeps and Curses V.3.1

Vairocana — Innate Technique (3rd level)

Starting at 3rd level, you have learned to harness the destabilization of the world and channel into direct attacks or channel it into the area around you. As an action for 2 CE, you can cast Chaos Bolt. Chaos Bolt is automatically cast as a third level spell when you reach 6th level, automatically cast as 5th level at 11th level, and automatically cast as 8th level at 18th level. As an action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to cause Chaos to form in the world around you. Roll a d100 on the Chaos Table which determines the effect. If an effect is random, it can also affect you unless the effect originates from you. (X = your CE modifier)

Creeps and Curses V.3.1

Vairocana — Innate Technique (6th level)

At 6th level, after using Chaos, you can spend 1 CE to increase either the effect’s duration or damage dice by your CE modifier. If the effect’s duration is 1 round or 1 minute, the duration is instead doubled. When you cast Chaos Bolt, you can spend Cursed Energy up to your proficiency bonus to upcast Chaos Bolt by one spell level per CE spent (up to a maximum of 9th level).

Creeps and Curses V.3.1

Vairocana — Innate Technique (11th level)

At 11th level, you have learned to balance the chaos and harmony. When you use Chaos, you can choose either Order or Equilibrium:

Order. You control a random element of the rolled Chaos effect. This can include where an area of effect appears, which creature is affected, or the place a creature teleports to.

Equilibrium. This causes a number of creatures up to your Cursed Energy modifier to be immune to the Chaos effect. They cannot take damage or be selected by the Chaos. After using this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

documents.name: Domain Expansion: Mandala of Mutual Paradox

description.value:
Creeps and Curses V.3.1

Vairocana — Innate Technique (18th level)

Domain Expansion (rules): full-turn action, 20 CE unless stated, 175-ft radius, 1 minute. When the domain ends you suffer Technique Burnout (applied automatically by the module).

At 18th level, you have finally learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you can choose a Chaos effect of 90 or below which functions as your guaranteed hit and can affect all creatures of your choice within your domain, depending on the effect. While within your domain, any uses of Chaos function as your domain’s guaranteed hit, allowing the range of the effect to encompass the entirety of your domain and letting you pick specific targets.
