description.value:
Creeps and Curses V.3.1

Vairocana Reversal — requires Reverse Cursed Technique. Not added automatically.

Through mastering reverse cursed technique, you have learned your reversal. Rather than breaking the logic of this world and ignoring the laws of physics, your reversal allows you to instead create your own logic and laws of physics. While using Cosmic Genesis, you cannot use your other Innate Technique features. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you force a new rule of reality into the world around you in a 30 ft radius centered on you. This rule affects all creatures, objects, and terrain within range for a number of rounds equal to twice your Cursed Energy modifier (minimum of 2 rounds). The rule you impose must alter a fundamental interaction of reality. The DM has final say over whether an implemented rule is valid. Examples include:

Rule of Absolute Gravity. Gravity is absolute and cannot be ignored. Creatures cannot fly or teleport and jumping distance is halved.

Rule of Perfect Motion. An object in motion will remain in motion, forever. Creatures ignore difficult terrain and cannot have their speed reduced.

Rule of Universal Sight. Eyes could always perceive the entire electromagnetic spectrum. Creatures cannot benefit from invisibility and hidden creatures are automatically revealed.

Rule of Damage Inversion. Fire always healed instead of damaging. Fire damage heals for half the damage roll and deals no actual damage.

Creeps and Curses V.3.1

Vairocana Reversal — requires Reverse Cursed Technique. Not added automatically.

At 6th level, you can cause your original created world of rules to expand. At the start of your turn while Cosmic Genesis is active, you can spend 1 CE to gain one of the following benefits.

Expansion. The range of Cosmic Genesis increases by 10 ft (to a maximum of 120 ft).

Addition. You add a minor rule that functions half as effectively (to a maximum of 3 minor rules).

Duration. The duration of Cosmic Genesis increases by 1 round.

Antigravity System — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned how to reverse your own technique, manifesting a field of intense gravity. As an action for 6 cursed energy, you force every creature within a 10-foot-radius of you to make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, they take 10d10 force damage and are knocked prone and restrained until the beginning of your next turn or until they leave the area, and their melee attack rolls will automatically fail. On a success, they take half as much damage. Melee attack rolls will be made with disadvantage.

This technique deals twice as much damage to objects and structures. You can also use this technique as a reaction to an attack being made against you or if you're forced to make a saving throw. If used against a saving throw, you reduce the damage of the saving throw by the damage of your Gravity System. If you reduce the damage to 0, the effect ends. Any remaining damage after being reduced, is transferred to you. This only works on physical saves or things affected by gravity. Ranged attacks made inside Gravity System or whose projectiles enter it will fail if the roll is lower than twice your cursed energy DC. If a Dexterity or Constitution saving throw targets a creature inside Gravity System, its total damage will be reduced by your Gravity System damage die. This does not affect thunder or psychic damage. This technique's damage increases to 15d10 at 11th level, 20d10 at 18th level, and to 25d10 at 20th level.

Perfect Gravity. At 18th level, your gravity has reached its peak, completely destroying your opponents on contact. If your opponent's Strength score is equal or less than your cursed energy DC, they have disadvantage on the saving throw. Also, if they fail your saving throw by 5 or more they gain one level of exhaustion. Additionally, while a creature is restrained they now automatically fail Dexterity saving throws.

Auspicious Beast Summon — Cursed Technique Reversal

After you have mastered Reverse Cursed Technique, you have finally unlocked your cursed technique reversal. You now have the ability to remove other people's summons. As an action or reaction for 5 cursed energy, you can force all summoners of any shikigami, curses, familiars, or any other form of summon within 60 ft to make a CE saving throw. On a failure, their summons are undone.

system.requirements: Cursed Technique Reversal, Auspicious Beast Summon

description.value:
Black Bird Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

With your mastery of Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned Black Bird Manipulation's reversal. You are now able to tame Doves for 2 CE. As a bonus action, you can turn an amount of Crows equal to your CE modifier into Doves, spending 2 CE per Crow. Doves operate and follow the same rules as Crows but cannot be used for Bird Strike. As part of controlling a Dove, you can spend cursed energy up to twice your CE modifier to heal a creature within 5 ft of the Dove by sacrificing the Dove. The creature regains 1d8 hit points per Cursed Energy spent. While any allies are within 30 ft of a Dove, they have advantage on saving throws against the Frightened and Charmed conditions. If any allied creatures within range are reduced to 0 hit points or making death saves, they are instead stabilized. Additionally, a Dove can suppress an effect causing a creature within range to be Charmed or Frightened. If the Dove leaves the 30 ft radius of that creature, any suppressed effect resumes.

system.requirements: Cursed Technique Reversal, Black Bird Manipulation

description.value:
Black Box — Cursed Technique Reversal

Your mastery of Reverse Cursed Technique has led to you unlocking your cursed technique reversal. Instead of creating incredibly dense barriers, you create brittle barriers that are easy to break. As an action for 4 CE, you create a 10 ft see-through cube within 30 feet of you for 1 minute. If a Large or smaller creature is within range, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or be trapped within the cube. A creature inside your cube has full cover against attacks outside. The cube has AC equal to your Cursed Energy save minus 5, and hit points equal to twice your proficiency bonus. If reduced to 0 hit points, all creatures within 5 ft must make a Dexterity saving throw as shards explode in every direction. On a failure, creatures take Xd8 slashing damage (your CE modifier + your proficiency bonus) or half as much on a success. Creatures within your cube make this save at disadvantage. You can also use this as a reaction for 6 CE within 10 ft of you.

Black Box — Cursed Technique Reversal, 3rd level

At 3rd level, you can spend up to twice your CE modifier in additional cursed energy to gain a weakening for every 2 CE spent.

Fragility. Your Cube loses 1 HP and gains a -1 to AC for every weakening and lasts an additional minute for every 2 weakenings.

Shatterability. Your box deals additional slashing damage equal to your CE modifier for every weakening.

Size. For every weakening, you can make your Glass Box 5 feet larger, allowing you to fit more creatures. (10 ft < 15 ft < 20ft)

Blazing Courage — Cursed Technique Reversal

Your mastery of Reverse Cursed Technique has led to you unlocking your cursed technique reversal. You are now able to imbue your weapon with ice instead of fire. You can spend up to twice your CE modifier (minimum of 2) in cursed energy as a bonus action while holding a melee weapon, freezing said weapon for 1 minute. For the duration, the weapon deals 2d6 cold damage on a hit per 2 energy spent. At 6th level, you now deal 2d8 cold damage per energy spent, this increases to 2d10 at 11th level.

Blazing Courage — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered extending your ice outside of your blade as well as fixing your blade. If your weapon is suffering any penalties from being broken in some kind, when you activate freezing resolve those penalties are removed until the technique ends. Also, while Freezing Resolve is active, you can spend 6 Cursed Energy as an Action to emit an aura of ice within a 10 ft radius centered on you that lasts for 1 minute. While the aura persists you have resistance to cold and fire damage, and any creature that enters the ring of ice or starts its turn on the radius must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they take your Freezing Resolve damage dice and their movement speed becomes 0. On a success, they take half as much damage.

Blood Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

Coming with your mastery over both Reverse Cursed Technique and Blood Manipulation, you have gained your technique reversal. As an action for 5 cursed energy if a target was damaged by a slashing or piercing attack within the last round or otherwise considered to have an open wound, you can attempt to manipulate the blood in a creature's body within 60 feet of you to make them your puppet. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. If they are dead, they automatically fail. If you try to control another Blood Manipulation user, the target has advantage on the Constitution saving throw. On a failure the target becomes your puppet. Creatures with no bodily fluids are immune to this feature and this technique requires concentration. The target can still talk, see, hear, and have their own consciousness, but they cannot control the rest of their body and are incapacitated and cannot use their cursed technique. You can use an action or bonus action to move the target up to 30 feet, or you can have them attack with any weapon they have on them or that is within their reach. You roll for attack and damage, and you are proficient with any weapon. The creature can repeat the Constitution saving throw at the beginning of their turns.

Boogie Woogie — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over the Reversed Cursed Technique, you have found the reversal of your technique. Instead of switching your targets, you immobilize them for a short period, it's extremely simple but effective. You can immobilize yourself and 2 other creatures, cursed objects or tools within 60 ft of you for 2 cursed energy. All of the chosen creatures (including you) are stunned until the beginning of your next turn. You can use this technique as an action, bonus action, or reaction, however, it cannot benefit from additional reactions. After the first time this technique was used, any of the creatures affected can roll a CE saving throw at the end of their turns to end the effects.

Body Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

Due to your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, you have unlocked your cursed technique reversal. Your reversal is very interesting as so is your innate technique. Normally you are controlling your brain, but with your reversal, you are able to disrupt the brains of others. As an action for 8 cursed energy, you can reach out and touch the head of a creature within range. This disrupts their brain function causing them to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they will take 8d8 psychic damage and have their neural network disrupted for 1 minute. While disrupted, they must make another Constitution saving throw when they attempt to use an innate technique feature. On a failure their cursed energy will be shot out in a useless form being wasted. At the end of their turns, an affected creature can repeat the initial saving throw, ending the disruption on a success.

Centipede Shroud — Cursed Technique Reversal

Due to your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, you have unlocked your cursed technique reversal. Your reversal allows you to instead summon a white millipede that can be used offensively instead of supporting you. You can summon your cursed millipede for 6 cursed energy as a bonus action. It has the same stat block as your cursed centipede, but deals twice as much damage die on a hit. While within 5 ft of you, the millipede can enter your space, giving you the following benefits: ● On a hit with a melee or ranged attack, you deal an additional 2d10 damage as your Millipede fights with you. ● Your AC decreases by your proficiency bonus. ● When you or the millipede take damage, you can choose to have the other take the damage instead. If this damage would reduce the millipede to 0 hit points, you take the remaining damage. Once per turn, you can replace one of your attacks with two attacks from the millipede, which deals an additional 2d10 piercing damage on a hit. You cannot have your centipede and millipede summoned at the same time until you reach level 11. At level 11, you can have only one of each summoned at the same time.

Clone — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, you have found out the reversal of your technique. You have learned how to clone things without cursed energy, such as ordinary objects and weapons. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you can clone a non-magical or cursed energy filled object or structure within sight range, spending 2 additional ce for every size category above medium. Objects and structures created this way have hit points equal to your clones, but work and function the exact same as the normal object or structure. For 6 cursed energy, you can clone a common magical item or semi-grade cursed tool. You can expend 8 cursed energy to clone an uncommon magical item or grade 3 cursed tool. Lastly, you can expend 10 cursed energy to clone a rare magical item or a grade 2 cursed tool. Magical items and cursed tools created from this feature last for 1 hour.

Comedian — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned to channel reverse cursed energy into your technique to create your reversal! Instead of bringing your humor into reality, you play the straight man and force people into reality. As an action for 2 CE, you activate your technique for 1 minute while maintaining concentration. While your technique is active, you and a number of creatures of your choice up to your CE modifier within 20 ft are immune to the frightened or charmed condition. While your reversal is active, you cannot use Comedy.

Comedian — Cursed Technique Reversal

When a creature you can see within 60 ft would try to teleport, avoid damage, or do something obviously impossible via normal means while your reversal is active, you can spend 5 CE to force that creature to make a Cursed Energy saving throw. On a failed save, their attempt fails and they take 2d8 psychic damage as you lecture them on realism (Eg. You can’t just dodge a meteor, are you stupid or something?). Creatures without cursed energy automatically fail this saving throw.

Construction — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over the Reversed Cursed Technique, you have found the reversal of your technique. You have learned how to destroy objects and gain cursed energy from this deconstruction. Either as an action, bonus action or reaction, you can channel your Cursed Technique Reversal to destroy an object. Choose one non-magical or cursed energy filled object within reach that you vaporize from existence upon touching it. You must expend cursed energy dependent on the size of the object, requiring 1 CE for tiny, 2 CE for small, 4 CE for medium, and 8 CE for large.

If you destroy a cursed tool that you made with the Construction or Cursed Creations feature, you regain cursed energy equal to half the cursed energy you spent to create it (rounded down). You can also spend 10 cursed energy in the attempt of destroying a magical or cursed energy-filled object upon succeeding on a CE check. The DC for a common magical item or semi-grade cursed tool is 5. The DC for an uncommon magical item or grade 3 cursed tool is 10. The DC for a rare magical item or grade 2 cursed tool is 15. The DC for a very rare magical item or grade 1 cursed tool is 20. The DC for a legendary magical item or a special grade cursed tool is 25. You gain 5 CE for deconstructing a 4th grade tool and an additional 5 CE for each grade above 4th the tool is.

activation.condition: You gain 5 CE for deconstructing a 4th grade tool and an additional 5 CE for each grade...

description.value:
Contractual Recreation — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned how to reverse your technique, transforming things into receipts. As a bonus action for an amount required of energy depending on the object's size, you can transform it into a receipt as long as it could be realistically sold. You cannot do this to magical objects, cursed objects, cursed tools, or if a creature is holding the object.

Cursed Cannon — Cursed Technique Reversal

After mastering Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned your cursed technique reversal. You have learned how to defend against cursed energy. Whenever you are the target of a cursed energy effect, you can attempt to deflect the cursed energy being used. As a reaction, you can make a Constitution saving throw with the DC equaling 10 + 1/2 the cursed energy spent. On a success, you gain cursed energy equal to what was spent. If the effect was a cursed energy attack roll or forced a saving throw, the effect is negated. If the effect was a melee attack roll, you will nullify any features apart of it that are fueled by cursed energy. If you fail, you regain no cursed energy and the attack automatically hits. If the effect forces a saving throw you automatically fail the saving throw of the effect you were trying to absorb. This cannot absorb Maximums, Barriers, or Domain Expansions.

Cursed Circuitry — Cursed Technique Reversal

Because you have mastered Reverse Cursed Technique, you have gained your technique reversal. Instead of optimizing cursed energy usage, you can cripple a creature’s ability to optimize. As an action for 10 CE, you can target a creature within 5 ft. The target must make a CE saving throw. On a failure, the target takes your CE modifier in necrotic damage for every cursed energy they use for 1 hour as their attempts to utilize cursed energy destroys their bodies.

Cursed Speech — Cursed Technique Reversal

Because you have mastered Reverse Cursed Technique, you have gained your technique reversal. Instead of sending commands with your speech, you cancel out commands with your silence. You can cast Silence for 2 CE. You can activate Cursed Silence as an action for 8 cursed energy, one creature within 120 feet of you to make a CE saving throw. On a failure, they are now silenced, not being able to speak and suffering the effects of cursed silence for 1 minute. On a success, they become immune to this feature for 1 minute. For the duration, the creature affected by Cursed Silence must make a Wisdom saving throw whenever they try to make an action. On a failure, they do not take said action as it would be too loud and skip it. For the duration, you cannot speak and are concentrating as if you were concentrating on a spell. You can end your reversal technique at will.

Cursed Spirit Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

With your mastery of the Reverse cursed technique, you have now unlocked your reversal, the ability to infuse spirits with positive energy, annihilating them. As an action or reaction for an amount of cursed energy equal to half of the spirit's CR(rounded up) you can target a spirit with a number of hit points equal to twice your CE modifier times twice your proficiency bonus that is within 60 feet of you. The spirit must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they are overloaded with positive energy and die. You can also ignore the conditions if the spirit’s CR is equal to or lower than your proficiency bonus.

system.requirements: Cursed Technique Reversal, Cursed Spirit Manipulation

description.value:
Cursed Transmutation — Cursed Technique Reversal

Your reversal allows you to instead alter chemical structure to make things extremely resistant to all forms of change. As an action, you can spend up to twice your cursed energy modifier to give yourself or an object or willing creature you touch a number of temporary hit points equal to the hit points that would be regained if you had used Reverse Cursed Technique using that amount of cursed energy. While a creature has these temporary hit points, it is immune to limb damaging effects and has advantage on saving throws against effects that would alter their form. While an object has these temporary hit points, it is immune to effects that would deal higher damage against objects or structures.

Dark Claw — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned the reversal of your technique. Instead of hardening cursed energy to form claws, you mold soft cursed energy over your hand. As a bonus action for 2 CE, you activate this technique for 2 hours or until you end it as a bonus action. While your reversal is active, you cannot form claws and you gain a special reaction. When you are targeted by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack roll using your unarmed strikes (using Strength, Dexterity, or your Cursed Energy modifier) against the damage roll. If your roll is higher, the attack’s impact is absorbed by your soft cursed energy and the damage is nullified. You can spend 2 CE to use this again without spending your reaction.

You gain a +2 bonus to this special attack roll at 6th level. This increases to +3 at 11th level and +4 at 18th level.

Disaster Flames — Cursed Technique Reversal

By mastering Reverse Cursed Technique and your primary ability, you have inverted your control over flames into the power to extinguish and nullify them, even affecting the heat within living beings.

As an action or reaction to being targeted by a cursed technique AOE that deals fire damage, you can spend 2 cursed energy to extinguish a 10 feet cube of flames within 30 feet where the technique is nullified. If the technique is an attack roll, you can spend 2 CE as a reaction to reduce the fire damage by 6d8. If an attack’s damage is reduced to 0, any additional effects of the attack are canceled out.

Hypothermic Touch. At 3rd level, as an action you can spend an amount of cursed energy up to twice your CE modifier to make a melee attack roll and extinguish the heat within a target's body. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 2d8 cold damage per cursed energy spent. On a success, they take half as much damage. If they fail by 5 or more, their movement is reduced to 0 until the end of their turn. This reversal does not affect creatures that do not rely on body heat or are immune to cold damage.

Disaster Verdure — Cursed Technique Reversal

As an action for 6 cursed energy you unleash a wave of decay, causing all plants and plant-based creatures within a 30-foot radius to wither and die. Nonmagical plants automatically wither and die, while plant-based creatures must make a Constitution saving throw against your cursed energy save DC. On a failure, they take 5d12 necrotic damage. On a success they take half damage.

Withering Plant. At 3rd level, you're able to force a plant within a creature and cause it to decay, spreading internal damage. As an action, if a target was affected by a slashing or piercing attack within the last round or are under the bleeding condition or otherwise considered to have an open wound, you can spend cursed energy up to twice your CE modifier to make a melee attack roll and implant any type of flora into their open wound and cause rapid decay. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 2d8 necrotic damage per cursed energy spent. On a success, they take half as much damage.

Disaster Tides — Cursed Technique Reversal

While studying reverse cursed technique you have managed to invert your technique, instead of creating you now can destroy water. As an action for 2 cursed energy per 10 gallons destroyed, you can destroy up to 10 times your CE modifier gallons of water within range. Alternatively, you destroy fog in a 30-foot cube within range. You can also remove the water of a living being within reach of you. As an action for up to twice your CE modifier, you touch a creature and force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they take 2d8 necrotic damage per energy spent. On a success, they take half as much. If they fail the save by 5 or more, they gain 1 level of exhaustion. This reversal does not work in creatures without water in their body.

Disaster Storms — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned your reversal which allows you to instead create a beautiful sunny day that empowers you and allies. You can spend 6 cursed energy as an action to create a miniature sun floating above your head for 2 minutes that creates a sunny aura in a 20 ft radius centered around you. You can spend additional cursed energy equal to twice your proficiency bonus to increase the radius of the aura by 5 ft per cursed energy. Friendly creatures within the aura have resistance to fire damage and gain temporary hit points equal to twice your CE modifier (min of 2) at the start of your turn. You cannot have Sunny Day and Storm Creation or Divine Storm Sovereign active at the same time.

Disaster Storms — Cursed Technique Reversal

You can spend 4 CE to replace an attack on your turn with a burning ray from the miniature sun. Make a cursed energy attack against a creature within 120 ft. On a hit, you deal 6d6 fire damage. This increases to 8d6 at 6th level and 12d6 at 11th level. If this attack hits a creature within the radius, you add your CE modifier to the damage roll.

Disaster Vermin — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned the reversal of your technique. Rather than consuming and multiplying, you suppress the biological instincts of others. As an action for 6 CE, you create a 15 ft aura centered on you for 1 minute. A creature that starts their turn within this aura must make a Constitution saving throw whenever they attempt to gain temporary hit points or regain hit points. On a failed save, their body rejects the effect and the action and cursed energy cost used to give the temporary hit points or hit points are wasted. A creature that fails this saving throw by 5 or more has their body begin to shut down, giving them disadvantage on Constitution saves and wasting their bonus action and reaction until the end of their next turn.

Dragon Vein — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned the reversal of your technique. Instead of reinforcing your body with the power of the earth, you gain detachment and remove earthly desires. As a bonus action for 6 CE, you gain a flying speed equal to twice your walking speed for 2 minutes and can hover. While you are flying and not touching the ground, you regain hit points equal to twice your Cursed Energy modifier at the start of your turn while you have at least 1 hit point.

At 11th level, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage while you are flying, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

Deadly Sentencing — Cursed Technique Reversal

Because of your unique technique and your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, your cursed technique reversal is much different than others. Your reversal works inside of your domain. The main properties of your domain stay the same, but you now are proving the innocence of a deceased creature. If you witness a creature die in the range you can cast your domain, you can use a reaction to open it in its reversal. This costs cursed energy if you do not have a free use. When you open it in this way, you bring yourself, the deceased creature, and the creature who killed them. For the duration of the domain, the deceased creature is revived. Inside the domain, Judgeman will first announce the charges against the defendant, which are actual crimes they may or may not have committed(Chosen by the GM). These crimes should relate to why the defendant died. Judgeman automatically knows everything about everyone inside the domain but this information isn't shared with you. The verdict of the trial depends on the arguments presented by both sides. After the accusation is reviewed, the defendant is given one chance to defend their case. You can help the defendant prove their innocence. They have three options: silence, confession, or denial. If the defendant chooses to deny the charges, they can lie in their statements. The defendant's goal is to dispel all doubt and win a pronouncement of innocence from Judgeman. Lies the defendant makes can be cross examined by the prosecutor(Deception vs Insight) as normal, same for lies from the prosecutor being cross examined by the defendant. Confession or Silence make the guilty verdict automatic in the former’s case, or uncontestable given sufficient evidence in the latter’s case. Judgeman will give you information in the form of evidence to help you find the defendant not guilty. The evidence appears as a sealed envelope in your hand. The evidence submitted is not necessarily conclusive and it will not be opened and shared with the prosecutor until after their statement, but you will be informed of the contained information by Judgeman upon receiving the envelope. Evidence that is mostly unrelated or merely tangentially related may require a persuasion check to go through, with the DC depending on how much of a reach the argument is. (10 slight reach, 15 moderate reach, 20 hard reach, 25 exceedingly hard reach, and 30 nearly impossible to agree with reach. 45 for fully impossible to agree with reach). The prosecutor also only has one chance to make a statement. The prosecutor's goal is to provide reasoning for why they killed the defendant. After their statement, they must make the same persuasion check against your argument if their reasoning was not sufficient. (15 slight reach, 20 moderate reach, 25 hard reach, 30 exceedingly hard reach, and 35 nearly impossible to agree. 50 for fully impossible to agree with). Once the prosecution and defense have both made their statements, Judgeman(the Game Master) will deliver a lawful verdict. The person who proved their argument better will win the case. If the defendant is found innocent, the domain will end and they will be revived with full hit points. If the defendant is found guilty they will remain dead. If the defendant is found guilty, the domain will end and you will gain 1 level of exhaustion for 1 minute, and cannot use your innate technique features. Every time you cause a creature to be innocent, you gain an additional free domain use that day, and will gain refinement points as if you have reduced them to 0 hit points.

Earth Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

As an action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to target a 5 ft cube of earth, stone, or metal within 20 ft of you and cause it to disintegrate. Metal costs an additional 1 cursed energy to disintegrate. If there is no ground beneath it, a creature standing in that space falls through. Otherwise, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

activation.condition: Metal costs an additional 1 cursed energy to disintegrate.

description.value:
Earth Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal, 3rd level

At 3rd level, as an action you can spend up to twice your cursed energy modifier to disintegrate earth, stone, or metal in a 5 ft cube that you touch, spending 2 cursed energy per cube. All materials in the cube must be touching each to be disintegrated. You can choose to destroy several 5 ft cubes as long as they are touching the cube you touched. A creature touching this ground when it is disintegrated must make a Constitution saving throw or take 2d10 necrotic damage as they experience your technique. If there is no ground beneath it, a creature standing on it falls through. Otherwise, all affected ground counts as difficult terrain. This damage increases to 3d10 at 3rd level, 4d10 at 6th level, 6d10 at 11th level, and 10d10 at 18th level.

Earth Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal, 11th level

At 11th level, as an action for 1 CE you can target a small non-magical object made of earth, stone, or metal and turn it to dust. If a creature is holding it, they can make a Dexterity saving throw to dodge your touch. At 6th level, you can use this on a cursed tool of Second Grade or lower for 2 CE. If you touch it, it gains a -1 to attack and damage rolls if it is a weapon or AC if it is armor (first reducing the tool’s bonuses if any). If this penalty reaches -3, the item disintegrates into dust. At 11th level this can affect first grade tools for 3 CE, at 18th level it can affect special grades for 6 CE.

Eight Heads — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered reverse cursed technique and learned the reversal of your technique. Life is precious. Unlike you, most people do not get do-overs. As an action for 10 CE, you target a creature within 60 ft and reinforce their mortality. Until they complete a long rest, they are unable to regain hit points, automatically fail death saves, and take additional necrotic damage equal to your CE modifier whenever they take necrotic damage.

Offering. At 11th level, when you would use Maximum: Sacrifice, you can instead spend 12 cursed energy. A creature of your choice within the barrier instead regains 10d4 hit points at the start of their turn.

Esoteric Art — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned the reversal of your technique that causes creative destruction rather than creative freedom. As an action for 2 CE you touch a non-magical object or structure within 5 ft, spending 2 CE for every size category larger than medium it is. The target takes 50 necrotic damage + (25 for every additional CE). If this destroys the object or structure, it liquefies into black ink.

Esoteric Art — Cursed Technique Reversal

As an action for 4 CE, you force a creature within 30 ft that you can see to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they begin to lose definition for 1 minute. For the duration their body becomes blurred and their appearance is almost impossible to discern. Both attacks they make and attacks made against them are at disadvantage. Additionally, at the start of their turn you can force the target to take necrotic damage equal to twice your level and reduce its movement speed by 5 ft. If this reduces the target’s movement to 0, it becomes restrained for the rest of the duration as it melts into the environment.

Explosive Flesh — Cursed Technique Reversal

After mastering Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned your cursed technique reversal. You gain the ability to turn the body parts of creatures you touch into bombs. Once per turn for X cursed energy when you make a melee weapon attack you can try to blow up the body parts of other creatures. On a hit, they must make a CE saving throw. On a failed save, you can choose a body part of the creature to explode, causing damage and effects as per your original abilities. On a success, nothing happens. The Cursed energy cost for this feature is equal to twice the Explosive Feature’s cost depending on the body part targeted and the damage dice for Explosive Flesh is doubled when using this Technique. The creature suffers the effects of Explosive Flesh as normal. The limb that is targeted cannot be the skull, neck, or torso.

Fa Jin — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered reverse cursed technique and learned the reversal of your technique. Once per turn on a hit with an unarmed strike, you can spend 2 ce to give the target 3 negative Jin charges. When that creature makes an attack or uses a technique that deals damage, you can spend any number of their negative Jin charges to deal 1d6 less damage. If this reduces an attack or effect’s damage to 0, it is nullified and has no effect.

Fa Jin — Cursed Technique Reversal, 6th level

At 6th level, as an action for 6 CE you can create a 60 feet line while wielding a slashing or piercing weapon or a 30 feet cone while wielding a bludgeoning weapon or unarmed strike. All creatures in range must make a CE saving throw. On a failure, they take 6d8 necrotic damage and gain 3 negative Jin charges. You gain 3 Jin charges for every creature that fails its save against your technique.

Faceless God — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned the reversal of your technique. Rather than destroying the mind with madness and corruption, you strengthen it with wisdom and rationality. As an action for 6 CE, you activate your reversal for 2 minutes. You and creatures of your choice within 30 ft that can see you gain immunity to the charmed and frightened condition, resistance to psychic damage and advantage on mental saving throws. You cannot have Face of Wisdom and Madness Inducement active at the same time.

Fate — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned your reversal that uses the opposite of your technique. Rather than the restricting binds of Fate, you can break free and become truly unchained by Destiny. As an action for 4 CE, you activate your reversal for 1 minute. For the duration, you cannot use cursed energy in any way and are considered to be completely devoid of cursed energy, making you immune to the guaranteed hit effects of domains, effects that target based on cursed energy, or effects that would give you disadvantage or penalties to attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

G Warstaff — Cursed Technique Reversal

With your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique comes your cursed technique reversal. Just like when using G Warstaff normally, you fulfill G Warstaff's condition for ink by hitting a creature. However, instead of being able to see their future, you can see their past. As a bonus action for 2 cursed energy, you can view their manga panel and learn the general actions they took over the past few weeks. You can see a number of weeks in the past equal to the amount of seconds marked by G Warstaff.

Golden Hour — Cursed Technique Reversal

After mastering Reverse Cursed Technique, you have unlocked your cursed technique reversal. Once per turn on a hit with a melee attack, you can spend cursed energy up to twice your CE modifier. On a hit, in addition to the attack's damage, the target must make a Constitution saving throw against your Cursed Energy save DC. On a failure, the target is slowed for a turn for every 2 cursed energy spent. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The DC for an affected creature equals your Cursed Energy save plus the number of of remaining turns. An affected target's speed is halved, it takes a -2 penalty to AC and Dexterity saving throws, and it can't use reactions. On its turn, it can use either an action or a bonus action, not both. Regardless of the creature's abilities or cursed items, it can't make more than one melee or ranged attack during its turn. If the creature attempts to use a technique with a casting time of 1 action, roll a d20. On an 11 or higher, the technique doesn't take effect until the creature's next turn, and the creature must use its action on that turn to complete it. If it can't, the technique is wasted.

Golden Hour — Cursed Technique Reversal

You can spend 2 cursed energy as a bonus action to briefly slow your own perception of time. Until the start of your next turn, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and Dexterity saving throws.

Hair Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned your reversal, allowing you to gain the opposite of your technique. As an action for 4 CE, you implant your own hairs onto a creature within 10 ft of you. A creature can make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid this effect on a success. When you implant your hairs into a creature, you can use your Hair Manipulation features (other than Domain Expansion) through that creature’s hair a number of times equal to twice your CE modifier before your implanted hairs run out of cursed energy. A creature can target the hair with attacks and effects to destroy the implanted hair. The hair has an AC equal to your CE save DC and is destroyed if it takes fire or slashing damage equal to your level at once. Destroying the implanted hair in this way leaves the target bald.

Heart Catch — Cursed Technique Reversal

After mastering Reverse Cursed Technique, you have unlocked your cursed technique reversal. You are now able to summon small feet which disrupt the focus of creatures. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you may shoot out a bunch of little feet in a 30 foot cone. Creatures in this cone must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 5d6 bludgeoning damage and are frightened for 1 minute. On a success, they take half damage and are not frightened. Frightened creatures can repeat the save at the end of their turns.

description.value:
Idle Transfiguration — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned how to reverse your technique, allowing you to transfigure targets without souls. As a Bonus Action while holding or touching an object or weapon, you can spend Cursed Energy up to twice your proficiency bonus. For every 1 Cursed Energy spent, you can change one property of the object or to increase/decrease the size category of the object. The Special property costs 3 Cursed Energy instead of 1, and you must work with your DM to figure out its rules. These transfigurations last until you dismiss them as a Free Action while holding or touching the object.

Soul Splitting Weapon. At 6th level, you have learned to transfigure objects in a way to damage the souls of others. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a transfigured weapon, you can spend 4 CE to cause that creature to also suffer the effects of Transfiguration on a hit.

Ice Formation — Cursed Technique Reversal

Because of your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned your cursed technique reversal. You can now enhance the heat in the air, making creatures boil alive. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you can force a number of targets up to your CE modifier within 30 ft of you to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they take 8d10 fire damage and receive one level of exhaustion. On a success, they take half as much damage and do not receive a level of exhaustion. Any damage dealt by this technique reversal also reduces the target’s maximum hit points from boiling their blood into air. The lost hit points are regained after they take a long rest. This technique’s damage increases to 10d10 fire damage at 18th level and 16d10 fire damage at 20th level.

Illusive Mirage — Cursed Technique Reversal

Due to your mastery of Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned your cursed technique reversal. You are now able to make the distorted faces real. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you can distort a creature's face that is distorted for a cursed creature. The creature must make a CE saving throw. On a failure, their face is distorted and they have disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma checks and saves and lose concentration on any technique or feature it was concentrating on. After failing, a creature may repeat the saves at the end of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

Inverse — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned to reverse your technique, allowing you to inverse the damage of your own attacks. As a bonus action for 4 cursed energy, you activate Power Inversion for 2 minutes. While active, when you deal damage, it is modified based on a set damage limit and a threshold. The set damage limit is equal to your proficiency bonus multiplied by your CE score, and the threshold is equal to your proficiency bonus multiplied by your CE modifier. When you deal damage that exceeds your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and deal the remaining difference as damage. However, when the damage is below your threshold, you subtract the damage from your set limit and increase the damage dealt by that amount. If the calculation results in a negative number, the damage remains unchanged. For example, if your set limit is 80 and you deal 100 damage, you would subtract the threshold from the damage if it exceeds it (e.g., 100 - 20 = 80), dealing the remaining 80 damage. Conversely, if you deal 10 damage and your threshold is 20, you would subtract that amount from your set limit (80 - 10 = 70), resulting in dealing 70 damage instead. You can spend 2 cursed energy at the end of the 2 minutes to maintain the effect for an additional 2 minutes.

Laplace’s Demon — Cursed Technique Reversal

describes how a deterministic system can nonetheless exhibit behavior that is impossible to predict: as in the butterfly effect, minor variations between the starting conditions of two systems can result in major differences. You can spend 4 cursed energy as a reaction to instead of using logic, force a chaotic rush of extremity for 2 minutes. You gain the following benefits for the duration: ● When you make attack rolls, you treat a creature’s AC as being lowered by your Intelligence modifier. ● When you miss an attack roll, you have advantage on your next attack against that creature. ● Roll a D4 at the start of your turn. Depending on the outcome, you must take the following action as a bonus action: (1: Hide, 2: Disengage, 3: Dash, 4: Attack, (one melee attack))

Laplace’s Demon — Cursed Technique Reversal, 3rd level

At 3rd level when you use Future and Past, you can instead expend 2 CE as a reaction to replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by a creature you can see with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll. If the target fails the roll, they gain disadvantage on all attack rolls, saving throws, or ability checks until the end of their next turn. If the target succeeds, they instead gain advantage.

Limitless — Cursed Technique Reversal

You gain the ability to Reverse your Lapse Blue technique, creating a great amount of space. As an action, you can spend up to twice your CE modifier to create a 15 feet cone. Creatures in range must make a Strength save, taking 4d8 force damage + an additional 2d8 for every additional 2 CE spent and being launched 20ft for every 2 CE spent. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage and is only launched half the distance. If the creature impacts an object or structure they take the remaining distance as fall damage and fall prone. This increases to a 30 ft cone at 11th level.

Love Rendezvous — Cursed Technique Reversal

Because of your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, you have unlocked your cursed technique reversal, now making your technique repel instead of attract. When you use Love Rendezvous, you can spend 2 cursed energy to instead turn it into Hate Separation, causing the order of the stars to be inverted. Anyone appointed with a star must follow a reversed sequential order if they want to attempt approaching another star. When they make their movement, they must move directly toward the previous star in order and touch them, which allows them to move on to the next star in reverse order. Failing to do this will result in them being unable to close the distance toward their target, though they still expend any movement until the technique is disabled. The objects, creatures, and cursed energy marked with the same star will be repelled toward the creature with the lowest cursed energy, being all rapidly launched toward that point. The creature with the lowest cursed energy will take 2 dice of bludgeoning damage per 10ft the other stars have traveled and their size, while the objects and creatures that are repelled and crash into the target will take half as much damage. If the marked creature goes in the correct reversed order, nothing happens, and the stars they've touched disappear. Upon touching all stars in the reversed order, the stars on them disappear. See the following chart for the measure of damage:

  • Size Damage

  • Dice Tiny 1d4 Small d6 Medium d8 Large d10 Huge d12 Gargantu2d12 an The reversed order of the stars is as follows: ○ ★Gacrux → ★Ginan → ★Mimosa → ★Acrux → ★Imai.** If a creature has shikigami summoned, the shikigami are marked with the same stars as the summoner's. If a creature marked with a star attempts to target you in the incorrect reversed order with a cursed energy attack roll or forces you to make a saving throw against a feature, the attack or feature is repelled toward the creature with the lowest cursed energy. For attack rolls, the attacker instead targets the creature with the lowest cursed energy, rolling against their AC. For saving throws, the repelled effect forces the attacker to roll against the DC of the creature with the lowest cursed energy. As long as the cursed energy of the feature belongs to the mark, the feature cannot close the distance between the attacker and their intended target, allowing the intended target to take no damage from the attack as long as the reversed sequence is violated. If an ★Gacrux attempts to target ★Acrux with a cursed energy ray without first moving through ★Ginan and ★Mimosa, the cursed energy ray will instead be repelled toward the creature with the lowest cursed energy in the area. This repulsion continues until the attacker follows the reversed sequence correctly.

Miracle — Cursed Technique Reversal

After mastering reverse cursed technique, you found out your technique reversal, learning about Calamity Marks. Whenever you witness a calamity happening, a yellow marking appears right somewhere on your body, making you gain a Calamity Mark. You can have up to 6 Calamity Marks.

  • Calamity Description

  • Unlucky… Failing makes no one but the person who failed sad. Whenever you or a hostile creature you can see or hear rolls the minimum amount they could on a dice roll, you gain 1 Calamity Mark.

  • Opposite Nobody likes opposite numbers, it just looks ugly.

  • Numbers… Every time you or a hostile creature you can see or hear rolls two different numbers with one being odd and the other being even, you gain 1 Calamity Mark.

  • Trash… Finding free stuff is cool, but only if it’s valuable. Every time you or a hostile creature you can see finds a new item, weapon or armor of at max Uncommon rarity you gain 1 Calamity Mark. This only counts towards cursed tools and magical items.

  • Failing Overcoming hardships is something rare to see in such

  • with Ease… a vile world we live in, so seeing it is truly a miracle. Whenever you or a hostile creature you can see or hear fails in a saving throw, ability check, or attack roll they had advantage on, you gain 1 Calamity Mark. As a reaction to a creature succeeding a roll, you can spend 1 Calamity Marks and 2 cursed energy to roll a d10. After rolling it, subtract it from the roll. If they fail because of your die and it reaches a 1 or lower (counting the natural die with no modifiers), it is considered as if they have rolled a natural 1 and ignores features that avoid natural 1s.

Missile Fist — Cursed Technique Reversal

After mastering the Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned the reversal of your offensive Missile Fist is the defensive Leg Aegis. As a reaction to being attacked, you can spend Cursed Energy up to twice your Cursed Energy modifier to summon a large leg in front of you that kicks away attacks. The Leg Aegis has hit points equal to 10 times the amount of Cursed Energy spent, and its Armor Class is equal to your Cursed Energy Save DC. The Leg Aegis absorbs damage you would take, and automatically fails saving throws. The Leg Aegis lasts until its hit points are depleted or until the beginning of your next turn.

Moon Dregs — Cursed Technique Reversal (Sun Dregs)

You have unlocked your reversal. You can use your action to spend 10 cursed energy to summon a Jellyfish shikigami, which lasts for 8 hours and uses your proficiency bonus. You cannot have Sun Dregs and Moon Dregs summoned at the same time until you reach 18th level. At 6th level, Sun Dregs can make 2 attacks and does not provoke opportunity attacks from a creature they have made a melee attack against that turn. When Sun Dregs is destroyed, you cannot summon it again for 2 minutes.

Moon Dregs — Cursed Technique Reversal (Sun Dregs), 3rd level

At 3rd level, when Sun Dregs hit a creature, you can spend 2 cursed energy to cause the attack to deal an extra 4d6 radiant damage. At 11th level, you can add your Cursed Energy modifier to Sun Dregs AC as well as its Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores. Sun Dregs can be commanded as a free action on your turn.

Mythical Beast Amber — Cursed Technique Reversal

Your mastery of the Reverse Cursed Technique has granted you the reversal of your technique, the ability to turn your body back to flesh after using your Release. As a bonus action, while Mythical Beast Amber Release is active, you can spend 6 cursed energy to start reversing the effects. The amount of time that you were using your Release is now the amount of time it will take to fully reverse the effects. While the technique is active, you must maintain concentration. If you lose concentration, the reversal ends and you must immediately make the saving throw using your current stage's save DC. If you wait for the same amount of time that you had your Release active then your Mythical Beast Amber Release will be deactivated and you do not have to make a saving throw. Even if you spent Cursed Energy to speed up your transformation, you must wait the number of rounds as if you had progressed normally.

system.requirements: Cursed Technique Reversal, Mythical Beast Amber

Pachinko Fever — Cursed Technique Reversal

Your mastery over the Reverse Cursed Technique has granted you your technique’s reversal. Whenever you expand your domain, instead of rolling for a jackpot, you can force all creatures within your domain to roll for a Jackpot following the usual rules of your domain. On a Jackpot, a creature is rewarded with 10 cursed energy. On a failure, the creature loses all their current cursed energy and cannot regain cursed energy for 1 minute.

Pain Killer — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered reverse cursed technique and learned the reversal of your technique. You can attempt to touch a creature within 5 feet by succeeding a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check against their AC. On a success, you can spend CE up to your CE modifier to cause them to take 5 additional psychic damage from any source of damage for every 2 CE spent. This lasts for 1 hour and increases with your duration of Pain Killer. At 3rd level, you can use this feature with Practiced Hands.

Pain Killer — Cursed Technique Reversal, 6th level

At 6th level, if a creature has less than their hit point maximum, they immediately take 10 psychic damage from Killer Pain and a creature under the effects of Killer Pain makes death saves at disadvantage. Additionally, you can spend an additional 6 CE as part of using Killer Pain to give the target the poisoned condition for the duration.

description.value:
Paralyzing Gaze — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have gained the ability to reverse your technique, making your technique quicken instead of slow. As an action for 4 CE, you can choose a target that you can see within 30 ft. The target doubles their movement, gains a bonus to their AC equal to your CE modifier and gains an additional bonus action on their turn. At the start of your turn, you can spend 2 CE as a bonus action to maintain the technique. This effect ends if line of sight is broken.

Prayer Song — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered Reverse Cursed Technique and therefore gained your cursed technique reversal. Dancing is your whole thing, so your reversal forces you to not be able to dance. However, this makes you incredibly sad. As a bonus action, you can stop using your technique and spend 6 cursed energy to enter this new sad form for 1 minute. During this you have disadvantage on all saving throws, attack rolls are made with disadvantage, and attacks against you have advantage. However, this increased sadness boosts your negative emotions and generates more cursed energy. You regain cursed energy equal to your CE modifier at the beginning of your turns. This regen only works if you are in combat where your life is in danger. You can deactivate your reversal at will.

Projection Sorcery — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered the Reverse Cursed Technique and the 24 FPS rule, learning how to rewind time itself. As a Full Turn Action, you can activate Replay Technique by spending Cursed Energy up to twice your CE modifier. For every 2 cursed energy spent, you teleport back 6 seconds in time to where you previously were. You cannot use Replay Sorcery and Projection Sorcery at the same time.

Puppet Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

Due to mastering Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned your cursed technique reversal. Instead of being able to control puppets, you can now sever the connection between one and their summons. As an action for 5 cursed energy, choose one person within 60 feet of yourself or one of your puppets who currently have some form of summon under their control. That person is then forced to make a CE saving throw. On a failure, the target loses control over their summons for 1 minute. These summons go berserk and attack the nearest creature for the duration. The creature can regain control by succeeding on another CE saving throw at the end of their turns.

Ratio — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over the Reversed Cursed Technique, you have found the reversal of your technique. You have learnt how to invert your own ratio, placing it onto yourself to develop weak points but the effect causes all areas excluding those weak points to be reinforced beyond comparison. As a bonus action or reaction whenever an attack is made against you or you roll a saving throw for 8 cursed energy, you can impose the ratio onto your body for a number of rounds equal to CE modifier (minimum of 1). By doing so, you roll a d10 every time an attack roll is made against you or you make a saving throw. If you roll anything other than a 3 or 7, you gain resistance to all damage taken, damage reduction equaling half of your level, rounded down (damage reduction occurs after damage resistance), and any damage resistance you have prior to placing the ratio onto yourself becomes damage immunity. If you roll a 3 or 7, the attack roll hits regardless of your AC or you automatically fail the save.

Regalia — Cursed Technique Reversal

Due to mastering Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned your cursed technique reversal. Instead of releasing the seal on your soul’s cursed tool, you can instead seal the cursed tools of others. Once per turn, when you hit a creature wielding or using a cursed tool, you can spend 4 CE to force them to make a Cursed Energy save against your DC. On a failure, a cursed tool of your choice that the target is wielding or wearing becomes non-functional. The target gains a -2 penalty to the save for every rarity below Special Grade the targeted cursed tool is. They lose any benefits of the cursed tool and their attunement breaks if they are attuned. The cursed tool reverts to a non-functional cursed object without any bonuses and cannot be attuned to for 1 hour. After the hour has passed, the item returns to normal and can be attuned to.

Retrograde — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned the reversal of your technique. Rather than reversing what was, you reinforce what will happen as a certainty. As an action for 6 CE, you target a creature within 30 ft that you can see and declare their defeat/victory to be certain. For 1 minute, they are under the effects of Certain Defeat or Certain Victory. You can only have a declaration against one creature at a time.

Certain Defeat. A creature under your declaration cannot gain advantage and is unaffected by any effects that would cause it to reroll dice (including Retrograde). The first time the creature takes damage or fails a saving throw each round, they take a number of d10s in necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus and can only take this damage once per round.

Certain Victory. A creature under your declaration cannot gain disadvantage. Additionally, when they have advantage on a roll they instead roll 3 dice and take their pick as victory guides their hand. If using Certain Victory on yourself, you can only use Retrograde features on other creatures.

Rockstar — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered both the Reverse Cursed Technique and the art of soothing jazz. Doing so has unlocked your cursed technique reversal and instead of electrifying rock, you opt for smooth jazz. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you fill a 30-foot radius around yourself with smooth jazz. Any creature entirely inside of this radius is deafened and can only hear your music, giving them immunity to thunder damage. You must concentrate on this as if you were concentrating on a spell. This effect ends after 1 minute or when you end it at will.

Rot — Cursed Technique Reversal

Your blood is blood red, healthy and capable of healing the body whenever it touches it. Whenever you use a Rot Technique, you can choose to cause the damage taken to instead heal that amount of hit points instead of damaging. Additionally, you can spend 2 additional cursed energy when using a Rot Technique or Rotten Blood so whenever it damages a creature, whether through an attack roll or a saving throw, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, nothing happens. On a success, they regain additional hit points equal to twice your Rotten Blood damage.

Schrift X — Cursed Technique Reversal

As a bonus action for 2 CE, you apply a cursed seal to a target within 30 feet. On their next turn, the target makes attacks as if all creatures are behind half cover. At 11th level, this increases to three quarters cover.

Schrift X — Cursed Technique Reversal, 3rd level

At 3rd level, When you see a creature being targeted by a ranged attack, you can spend 6 CE to cause the attack to automatically miss.

Seance — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have now mastered Reverse Cursed technique and learned your cursed technique reversal. Rather than drawing the dead into you, you are now able to use your Séance technique to put yourself into the body of others.

As a full turn action for 8 cursed energy, you can target a willing or helpless (restrained, incapacitated, unconscious) creature and turn them into yourself. You take control of the target as you overwrite them with your soul information. Your real body will remain in the same position as when you used this technique and is unconscious. You have all of your own statistics, other than the target’s cursed technique and innate technique features and cursed energy. You must spend 1 cursed energy at the beginning of your turns to keep yourself in control. You return to your original body once the cursed energy is not spent on this.

Shadow Killer — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered your reversal, allowing you to heal instead of harm through shadows. When you make an attack roll, you can spend 2 cursed energy to target the shadow of a creature within your reach. On a hit, you stitch up their wounds through their shadow and the target regains hit points equal to your attack's damage roll + your Cursed Energy modifier. This healing increases to twice your Cursed Energy modifier at 6th level, and to thrice at 11th level.

Shadow Killer — Cursed Technique Reversal, 3rd level

At 3rd level, while within 10 ft of a bound creature you can spend 2 cursed energy as a bonus action to attempt to break their bindings. Make a Cursed Energy check against the DC of their bindings. On a success, you destroy the bindings with your shadow. You can use this as a full-turn action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) to gain advantage on the check.

Shrine — Cursed Technique Reversal

With your mastery of Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned Shrine's reversal. You are now able to attach things with your technique instead of cutting them apart. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can spend cursed energy up to twice your CE modifier to replace a Dismantle with an Assemble, using Dismantle's range. A creature or object targeted by an Assemble will regain 2d8 hit points per 2 cursed energy spent. If their limbs are wounded or worse, the limbs receive twice as many hit points. At 18th level, you can spend up to thrice your CE modifier.

Sky Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over the Reverse Cursed Technique, you have found the reversal of your technique. Instead of being able to bend and shape the sky, you remove it entirely, making it seem as if it never existed in the first place and pulling in outside space to cover it up. As an action for 6 cursed energy, you choose a point within 60 feet of you. All creatures in a 20 foot radius of said point must make a Strength saving throw, as you delete the space surrounding the area. On a failure, a creature is pulled to the point and takes bludgeoning damage depending on the size and quantity of creatures it hits. On a success, a creature is still pushed however they take half as much damage. If they fail by 5 or more, they are also stunned until the beginning of your next turn. A creature takes bludgeoning damage equal to twice your CE modifier per creature hit. However, for every size the creature is above tiny, your CE modifier is added once again. Creatures smaller than medium or with a Strength score lower than your cursed energy DC make the saving throw with disadvantage.

Solo Forbidden Zone — Cursed Technique Reversal

Your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique has unlocked your cursed technique reversal. This allows you to now create an area that drains enemies of their cursed energy. As an action for up to your CE modifier + your proficiency bonus in cursed energy, you can create a 15 ft radius circle centered around yourself. Creatures of your choice in that circle at the beginning of your turn must make a CE saving throw or they will lose an amount of cursed energy equal to the amount you spent at the beginning of your turn for 1 minute while they remain in the circle.

system.requirements: Cursed Technique Reversal, Solo Forbidden Zone

description.value:
Star Dictator — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have learned your technique reversal that allows your pseudo-domains to instead form an anti-domain. For 4 cursed energy, you reverse one of your active pseudo-domains into an anti-domain. Any guaranteed hits or effects that would cause attacks to automatically hit and saving throws to automatically fail are nullified and have no effect against orbiting shikigami and creatures within the anti-domain. A creature that hits your orbiting shikigami that are creating the anti-domain takes 1d12 slashing damage.

Star Rage — Cursed Technique Reversal

Due to your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, you have learned to reverse the mass increase. This allows you to get rid of all the mass in your body. This state can be entered as a bonus action or a reaction. You can spend as much Cursed energy on this with no limit, gaining a mass decrease for each cursed energy spent. This state lasts double your current time limit or until you end it as a free action. This cannot be used with Virtual Mass Increase.

Decreased Weight. For every mass decrease, your movement speed increases by 10 feet and you gain a +1 to unarmed attack rolls, but a -1 to damage rolls. If you move in a straight line before hitting a target with an unarmed strike, you gain a +1 to damage rolls for every 5 feet.

Increased Evasion. When you spend at least 6 CE on virtual mass, you gain the Evasion feature and advantage on Dexterity checks and saving throws. You gain a further +2 to Dexterity rolls and AC and -1 to Strength checks and saves for each additional mass decrease.

Critical Speed. Your critical range increases by 2 for every four mass decreases and you deal minimum damage to objects and structures.

Zero Virtual Mass. Despite your reversal being powerful there is a limit. At 11th level, if you spend more than 10 Cursed Energy, you can choose to reduce your mass to 0. Reducing your mass in this way forces you to enter an incorporeal state, and temporarily takes away half of your maximum hit points. During this state, you become unaffected by all damage except psychic, and can phase through objects and creatures. You also cannot interact with other creatures or objects. In addition your speed increases by 30 feet. This lasts for 1 minute or until stopped as a free action.

Starlight Symphony — Cursed Technique Reversal (Dark Orchestra)

You can spend Cursed Energy up to twice your Cursed Energy modifier as an action. You create 10 feet of fog around yourself for every 2 cursed energy. The fog lasts for 2 minutes, spreads around corners and you choose if the fog follows you or not as part of the action to create it. Your fog counts as magical darkness and creatures within your fog have disadvantage on Perception and Investigation checks and automatically fail any ability checks made to detect cursed energy.

At 6th level, you can use your reaction to give advantage or disadvantage to a roll made by a creature within your cursed fog and can spend up to four times your Cursed Energy modifier when creating your cursed fog. You can spend up to five times your Cursed Energy modifier at 11th level.

Straw Doll Technique — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over the Reversed Cursed Technique, you have found the reversal of your technique. You have learned how to alter your own physical form and even your very soul to force an opponent into suffering just as much as yourself. As a reaction for 8 cursed energy whenever you use the reaction for the Resonance feature, you instead merge with the chosen piece of the creature you are targeting and your straw doll to become a living straw doll. When you take damage from an attack or damaging effect, the creature you targeted with this feature takes a quarter of the damage you received (rounded up) that will ignore any resistances and immunities. When you are forced to make a saving throw, the creature affected by this feature must make the same saving throw as you do, suffering any additional effects other than damage that result from a failed or successful saves (If they would take damage from a save, it is still a quarter of the damage, rounded down). You are treated as a straw doll and an inanimate object for the purposes of Cursed Straw features and effects. All damage you receive from a Cursed Straw feature is reduced to a quarter of its original damage (rounded down) rather than half of it (Target still takes quarter damage from these features). You ignore any effects that your Cursed Straw features would inflict when you perform them on yourself. You do not take any extra damage if you score a Black Flash from a self-inflicted attack. Lastly, the Cursed Doll Transformation lasts for 1 minute, until the creature has been reduced to 0 hit points, you are dead or you use Cursed Doll Transformation on another target.

system.requirements: Cursed Technique Reversal, Straw Doll Technique

description.value:
Technique Extermination — Cursed Technique Reversal

After mastering Reverse Cursed Technique, you have now unlocked your technique reversal. Instead of extinguishing someone’s technique you amplify it for a certain amount of time. As a bonus action, you can spend 4 cursed energy to choose one ally or enemy within 60 ft to ignite their cursed technique. For the next minute, the chosen creature's techniques exhibit the following enhancements: ● The damage dice of their techniques are increased by one tier (for example, from d6 to d8). ● They can add your CE modifier to the damage of their techniques. However, once the minute has elapsed, the creature suffers the effects of Technique Extinguishment for one minute, during which they experience the following additional effects: ● They cannot regain cursed energy until the end of their next turn. ● Their maximum cursed energy is reduced by an amount equal to your CE modifier until they finish a long rest. If the target is an unwilling creature, they must make a CE saving throw, on a failure, they are affected by this reversal. On a success, nothing happens. They can repeat the saving throw at the beginning of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

Teleportation — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have mastered Reverse Cursed Technique and unlocked your cursed technique reversal. You have now learned how to force people to stay still by reversing your technique. As a bonus action for 2 cursed energy, you can cover an enemy and force them to make a CE saving throw. This must be an enemy that is not being viewed by other creatures or they must be in melee range so you can cover them with your sheet. On a failure, their speed is reduced to 0 for 1 minute, on a success they are not affected. A creature who fails can repeat the saving throw at the end of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

Ten Shadows — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over Reversed Cursed Technique, you have found the reversal of your technique. You have learnt how to channel light rather than shadow, illuminating your or another creature's shadow. As a bonus action for 4 cursed energy, you may target a creature's shadow who you can see, erupting it in a blinding flash of light. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a success, nothing happens. On a failure, the creature is blinded until the end of your turn.

Summon Dispelling. You can also manipulate the light to interfere with the summons of others. As a bonus action, you can invert the shadow of a summon within 120 feet which you are connected to, for a number of cursed energy equal to half of the summon's CR or level(rounded down) You may force its summoner to make a CE saving throw. On a failure, the Summon becomes incapacitated and cannot move until the end of your next turn. If the summoner fails the saving throw by 5 or more, the summon is unsummoned, and cannot be summoned again for a number of rounds equal to your CE modifier.

Light Ridge. As a reaction to a melee attack roll for 2 cursed energy, if the attacker is within 10 feet of you, you may force them to make a Constitution Saving throw, on a success, nothing happens. On a failure, the attack misses, and the attacker is blinded until the end of the turn. A creature is immune to this feature if they do not rely on sight, such as with blindsight. Using Light Manipulation causes your shadow storage to become unstable. When you use Light Manipulation, you must make a DC 15 Concentration check. On a failure, one random object, if any, currently inside your shadow storage will be ejected out, ending up within 5 feet of the shadow on which Light Manipulation was used. At 11th level, you can now use Light Manipulation to target an entire area of shadow, inverting it into a blinding flash of Light. As a bonus action for 6 cursed energy, you may cause a creature's Shadow that you are connected to and can see, or your own shadow, to flash in a large radius. All creatures within a 20 feet radius must make a constitution saving throw. On a success, nothing happens, on a failure becoming blinded for one minute. A creature can repeat the save at the beginning of their turns, ending the effects on a success. Using Light manipulation in this way causes all items within your Shadow Storage to be forced out, ending up within 5 feet of the shadow on which Light Manipulation was used.

Tool Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

You have found out about your technique reversal, allowing you to control living creatures as your tools. As an action for 6 cursed energy, you force one creature within 60 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they are charmed by you for 1 minute while concentrating. While the target is charmed, you have a telepathic link while the two of you are on the same plane of existence. You can use this telepathic link to issue commands to the creature as a bonus action. Each time the target takes damage, it can repeat the save against the technique. If the saving throw succeeds, the technique ends. You can only control two creatures at once. At 11th level, you can control a number of creatures up to your CE modifier (minimum of 2).

Triple Core — Cursed Technique Reversal

With great mastery over Reversed Cursed Technique, you have found the reversal of your technique, allowing you to reverse the functions of your cores, allowing you to enter one of the following forms as a bonus action. You cannot use a Core form with Core Reversal.

Blocking Blows. : When you are hit with a melee attack, you can spend 2 CE to gain resistance to that damage.

Reverse Energy Blast. : As an action you spend CE to launch a blast of reverse cursed energy. You make a ranged cursed energy attack against a target within 160 feet dealing 4d6 radiant damage for every 2 CE.

Offensive Form. : As a bonus action, you assume this form for 1 minute, buffing your offense. You deal additional damage equal to 2 times your current cursed energy and costing 2 CE at the beginning of your turn to maintain.

Crash. : When you hit a creature with a melee attack, they are affected by your technique and cannot control their speed. If a creature moves more than 20 feet on their turn, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

Vengeful Spirit Manipulation — Cursed Technique Reversal

Coming with your mastery over Reverse Cursed Technique, you can now copy the reversal features of cursed techniques you’ve copied.

system.requirements: Cursed Technique Reversal, Vengeful Spirit Manipulation

description.value:
Voracity — Cursed Technique Reversal

As an action, you can spend 6 cursed energy to force all creatures of your choice within 30 ft to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, their movement speed is halved for 1 minute and they waste their action vomiting or dry heaving after being overcome by nausea and burning stomach pain. A creature can repeat this save at the end of their turn, ending the effect on themselves on a success.
